GroupSeminorm.toSeminormedGroup.comment:
Construct a seminormed group from a seminorm, i.e., registering the pseudodistance and the
pseudometric space structure from the seminorm properties. Note that in most cases this instance
creates bad definitional equalities (e.g., it does not take into account a possibly existing
`UniformSpace` instance on `E`).

explanatories.Norm.norm: This definition describes a function that assigns a real-valued norm to each element of a given type equipped with a norm structure.
explanatories.NormedCommGroup.dist_eq: This theorem states that in a normed commutative group, the distance between two elements is equal to the norm of their division.
explanatories.SeminormedGroup.dist_eq: This theorem states that the distance between two elements in a seminormed group is equal to the norm of their quotient.
explanatories.SeminormedCommGroup.dist_eq: This theorem establishes that the distance between two elements in a seminormed commutative group is equal to the norm of their quotient.
explanatories.Dist.dist: A distance function that defines how to measure the separation between elements of a type can be created when the type adheres to the properties of a distance metric.

explanatories.div_self': In a group, the division of any element by itself yields the identity element.
explanatories.GroupSeminormClass.map_one_eq_zero: This theorem states that the output of the function when the input is one equals zero.

explanatories.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.

explanatories.dist_self: The theorem states that the distance from any point to itself in a pseudo-metric space is zero.
explanatories.edist_dist: The extended distance between two points in a pseudo-metric space is equal to the extended non-negative real version of their distance.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto.dist: The convergence of two functions towards different points in a pseudometric space guarantees that the distance between their outputs also converges to the distance between those points.
explanatories.Continuous.dist: The distance between the images of two continuous functions in a pseudometric space is also a continuous function.

GroupSeminorm.toSeminormedGroup.description: This definition creates a seminormed group from a seminorm by establishing the structure of a pseudometric space based on the properties of the seminorm.

  (h : ∀ᶠ (n : α) in t₀, ‖f n‖ ≤ a n) (h' : Tendsto a t₀ (𝓝 0)) : Tendsto f t₀ (𝓝 1)
squeeze_one_norm'.comment:
Special case of the sandwich theorem: if the norm of `f` is eventually bounded by a real
function `a` which tends to `0`, then `f` tends to `1` (neutral element of `SeminormedGroup`).
In this pair of lemmas (`squeeze_one_norm'` and `squeeze_one_norm`), following a convention of
similar lemmas in `Topology.MetricSpace.Basic` and `Topology.Algebra.Order`, the `'` version is
phrased using "eventually" and the non-`'` version is phrased absolutely.

We could repeat this instance to provide a `[SeminormedGroup E] : SeminormedGroup Eᵃᵒᵖ` instance,
but that case would likely never be used.

  [SemilatticeSup α] {u : α → E} : CauchySeq u ↔ ∀ ε > 0, ∃ N, ∀ (m : α), N ≤ m → ∀ (n : α), N ≤ n → ‖u m / u n‖ < ε

explanatories.CauchySeq: A Cauchy sequence is a function defined on a preorder that captures the notion of converging behavior in a uniform space.
explanatories.Metric.cauchySeq_iff: Cauchy sequences in a pseudometric space are characterized by the property that the distance between their elements becomes arbitrarily small beyond a certain index.

NormedCommGroup.cauchySeq_iff.description: The theorem establishes that a sequence in a seminormed group is Cauchy if and only if for every positive distance there exists a point beyond which all pairs of sequence terms are within that distance when measured by the norm.

A helper lemma used to prove that the (scalar or usual) product of a function that tends to one
and a bounded function tends to one. This lemma is formulated for any binary operation
`op : E → F → G` with an estimate `‖op x y‖ ≤ A * ‖x‖ * ‖y‖` for some constant A instead of
multiplication so that it can be applied to `(*)`, `flip (*)`, `(•)`, and `flip (•)`.

explanatories.Filter.IsBoundedUnder: The definition indicates that the image of a filter under a specified function becomes eventually bounded with respect to a given relation, meaning it can be constrained by a uniform bound at some point in its progression.

MonoidHomClass.lipschitz_of_bound.code:
MonoidHomClass.lipschitz_of_bound.{u_1, u_3, u_4} {𝓕 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_3} {F : Type u_4} [SeminormedGroup E]
  [SeminormedGroup F] [FunLike 𝓕 E F] [MonoidHomClass 𝓕 E F] (f : 𝓕) (C : ℝ) (h : ∀ (x : E), ‖f x‖ ≤ C * ‖x‖) :
  LipschitzWith C.toNNReal ⇑f
MonoidHomClass.lipschitz_of_bound.comment:
A homomorphism `f` of seminormed groups is Lipschitz, if there exists a constant `C` such that
for all `x`, one has `‖f x‖ ≤ C * ‖x‖`. The analogous condition for a linear map of
(semi)normed spaces is in `Mathlib/Analysis/NormedSpace/OperatorNorm.lean`.

explanatories.FunLike: This definition introduces a class that indicates certain terms can be coerced injectively into functions from one type to another.
explanatories.LipschitzWith: A function is Lipschitz continuous with a non-negative constant if the distance between its outputs is bounded by the constant multiplied by the distance between its inputs.
explanatories.Real.toNNReal: This defines a function that converts a real number into a nonnegative real number, returning zero for negative inputs.

MonoidHomClass.lipschitz_of_bound.description: A homomorphism between seminormed groups is Lipschitz continuous if there exists a constant such that the norm of the image of any element is bounded by that constant multiplied by the norm of the original element.

  {f : α → E} : LipschitzWith K f⁻¹ ↔ LipschitzWith K f

explanatories.LipschitzWith: A function is Lipschitz continuous with a non-negative constant if the distance between its outputs is bounded by the constant multiplied by the distance between its inputs.

lipschitzWith_inv_iff.description: A function is Lipschitz continuous with respect to a constant if and only if its inverse function is also Lipschitz continuous with the same constant.

explanatories.AntilipschitzWith: A function is classified as an Antilipschitz map if the distance between any two points in the domain is at most a constant multiple of the distance between their images in the codomain.

antilipschitzWith_inv_iff.description: A function and its inverse are both Antilipschitz if and only if they satisfy the same antilipschitz condition with respect to their respective metrics.

explanatories.LipschitzOnWith: A function is Lipschitz continuous on a set with a non-negative constant if the distance between its outputs is bounded by the constant multiplied by the distance between its inputs, for all points within that set.

lipschitzOnWith_inv_iff.description: The function is Lipschitz continuous on a set with respect to a seminormed commutative group if and only if its inverse function is Lipschitz continuous on the complementary set.

NormedAddGroupHom.SurjectiveOnWith.comment:
A normed group hom is surjective on the subgroup `K` with constant `C` if every element
`x` of `K` has a preimage whose norm is bounded above by `C*‖x‖`. This is a more
abstract version of `f` having a right inverse defined on `K` with operator norm
at most `C`.

NormedAddGroupHom.SurjectiveOnWith.description: This definition introduces the concept of a bounded homomorphism being surjective onto a subgroup if each element in that subgroup has a preimage with a norm not exceeding a specified constant times the norm of the element.

SemiNormedGrp.cokernelCocone.fullDefinition: def cokernelCocone {X Y : SemiNormedGrp.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) : Cofork f 0 :=   @Cofork.ofπ _ _ _ _ _ _ (SemiNormedGrp.of (Y ⧸ NormedAddGroupHom.range f)) f.range.normedMk     (by       ext a       simp only [comp_apply, Limits.zero_comp]       -- Porting note: `simp` not firing on the below       -- This used to be `rw`, but we need `erw` after leanprover/lean4#2644       erw [comp_apply, NormedAddGroupHom.zero_apply]       -- Porting note: Lean 3 didn't need this instance       letI : SeminormedAddCommGroup ((forget SemiNormedGrp).obj Y) :=         (inferInstance : SeminormedAddCommGroup Y)       -- Porting note: again simp doesn't seem to be firing in the below line       -- This used to be `rw`, but we need `erw` after leanprover/lean4#2644       erw [← NormedAddGroupHom.mem_ker, f.range.ker_normedMk, f.mem_range]     -- This used to be `simp only [exists_apply_eq_apply]` before leanprover/lean4#2644       convert exists_apply_eq_apply f a) set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in

norm_mk_lt.code:
norm_mk_lt.{u_1} {M : Type u_1} [SeminormedAddCommGroup M] {S : AddSubgroup M} (x : M ⧸ S) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
  ∃ m, (mk' S) m = x ∧ ‖m‖ < ‖x‖ + ε

and `‖m‖ < ‖x‖ + ε`.
norm_mk_lt.description: For any element in the quotient space of a seminormed additive group and any positive real number, there exists a representative element from the original group whose norm is less than the norm of the quotient element plus that positive number.

norm_mk_lt'.code:

norm_mk_lt'.comment: For any `m : M` and any `0 < ε`, there is `s ∈ S` such that `‖m + s‖ < ‖mk' S m‖ + ε`.
norm_mk_lt'.description: For any element in a seminormed additive group and any positive real number, there exists an element in the subgroup such that the norm of their sum is less than the norm of the equivalent quotient element plus that positive number.

norm_mk_eq_zero.code:

Ideal.Quotient.semiNormedCommRing.fullDefinition: instance Ideal.Quotient.semiNormedCommRing : SeminormedCommRing (R ⧸ I) where   dist_eq := dist_eq_norm   mul_comm := _root_.mul_comm   norm_mul x y := le_of_forall_pos_le_add fun ε hε => by     have := ((nhds_basis_ball.prod_nhds nhds_basis_ball).tendsto_iff nhds_basis_ball).mp       (continuous_mul.tendsto (‖x‖, ‖y‖)) ε hε     simp only [Set.mem_prod, mem_ball, and_imp, Prod.forall, exists_prop, Prod.exists] at this     rcases this with ⟨ε₁, ε₂, ⟨h₁, h₂⟩, h⟩     obtain ⟨⟨a, rfl, ha⟩, ⟨b, rfl, hb⟩⟩ := Ideal.Quotient.norm_mk_lt x h₁,       Ideal.Quotient.norm_mk_lt y h₂     simp only [dist, abs_sub_lt_iff] at h     specialize h ‖a‖ ‖b‖ ⟨by linarith, by linarith [Ideal.Quotient.norm_mk_le I a]⟩       ⟨by linarith, by linarith [Ideal.Quotient.norm_mk_le I b]⟩     calc       _ ≤ ‖a‖ * ‖b‖ := (Ideal.Quotient.norm_mk_le I (a * b)).trans (norm_mul_le a b)       _ ≤ _ := (sub_lt_iff_lt_add'.mp h.1).le

controlled_closure_of_complete.comment:
Given `f : NormedAddGroupHom G H` for some complete `G` and a subgroup `K` of `H`, if every
element `x` of `K` has a preimage under `f` whose norm is at most `C*‖x‖` then the same holds for
elements of the (topological) closure of `K` with constant `C+ε` instead of `C`, for any
positive `ε`.

explanatories.NormedAddGroupHom.SurjectiveOnWith: This definition introduces the concept of a bounded homomorphism being surjective onto a subgroup if each element in that subgroup has a preimage with a norm not exceeding a specified constant times the norm of the element.
explanatories.AddSubgroup.topologicalClosure: The topological closure of a subgroup in a topological group is also a subgroup.

controlled_closure_of_complete.description: This theorem asserts that if a bounded homomorphism maps elements of a subgroup to preimages within a specified norm, then it extends this mapping to the topological closure of that subgroup with an adjusted bound.

controlled_closure_range_of_complete.code:
controlled_closure_range_of_complete.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {G : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup G] [CompleteSpace G]
  {H : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup H] {f : NormedAddGroupHom G H} {K : Type u_3} [SeminormedAddCommGroup K]
  {j : NormedAddGroupHom K H} (hj : ∀ (x : K), ‖j x‖ = ‖x‖) {C ε : ℝ} (hC : 0 < C) (hε : 0 < ε)
  (hyp : ∀ (k : K), ∃ g, f g = j k ∧ ‖g‖ ≤ C * ‖k‖) : f.SurjectiveOnWith j.range.topologicalClosure (C + ε)
controlled_closure_range_of_complete.comment:
Given `f : NormedAddGroupHom G H` for some complete `G`, if every element `x` of the image of
an isometric immersion `j : NormedAddGroupHom K H` has a preimage under `f` whose norm is at most
`C*‖x‖` then the same holds for elements of the (topological) closure of this image with constant
`C+ε` instead of `C`, for any positive `ε`.
This is useful in particular if `j` is the inclusion of a normed group into its completion
(in this case the closure is the full target group).

explanatories.NormedAddGroupHom.SurjectiveOnWith: This definition introduces the concept of a bounded homomorphism being surjective onto a subgroup if each element in that subgroup has a preimage with a norm not exceeding a specified constant times the norm of the element.
explanatories.AddSubgroup.topologicalClosure: The topological closure of a subgroup in a topological group is also a subgroup.

controlled_closure_range_of_complete.description: This theorem states that if a bounded homomorphism can map elements of a certain isometric immersion to preimages within a specified norm, then this property extends to the topological closure of that image with an increased bound.

explanatories.continuous_iff_continuousAt: A function is continuous if and only if it is continuous at every point in its domain.
explanatories.tendsto_iff_norm_sub_tendsto_zero: This theorem states that a function converges to a point in a seminormed group if and only if the norm of its quotient with that point converges to zero.
explanatories.squeeze_zero: If a non-negative function is bounded above by another function that tends to zero, then the non-negative function also converges to zero under the same limit.
explanatories.norm_nonneg: This theorem asserts that the norm of any element in a seminormed group is non-negative.
explanatories.continuous_fst: This theorem asserts that the first projection function from a product space to one of its component spaces is continuous.
explanatories.Continuous.tendsto: A continuous function at a point preserves the convergence of sequences by ensuring that the limit of the function's output at that point is the image of the limit of the input.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto.sub: If two functions converge to elements in a topological group, then the quotient of those functions also converges to the quotient of those elements.
explanatories.tendsto_const_nhds: The constant function that maps every input to a specific point tends to that point in the neighborhood as the filter approaches it.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto.norm: This theorem asserts that if a function converges to a limit in a seminormed group, then the norm of that function also converges to the norm of the limit.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto.add: The product of two functions that converge to respective limits in a topological space with a continuous multiplication structure also converges to the product of those limits.
explanatories.continuous_snd: This theorem asserts that the second projection map from the Cartesian product of two topological spaces is continuous.
explanatories.Continuous.sub: The quotient of two continuous functions in a topological space, when appropriately defined, is also a continuous function.

NormedDivisionRing.to_hasContinuousInv₀.fullDefinition: instance (priority := 100) NormedDivisionRing.to_hasContinuousInv₀ : HasContinuousInv₀ α := by   refine ⟨fun r r0 => tendsto_iff_norm_sub_tendsto_zero.2 ?_⟩   have r0' : 0 < ‖r‖ := norm_pos_iff.2 r0   rcases exists_between r0' with ⟨ε, ε0, εr⟩   have : ∀ᶠ e in 𝓝 r, ‖e⁻¹ - r⁻¹‖ ≤ ‖r - e‖ / ‖r‖ / ε := by     filter_upwards [(isOpen_lt continuous_const continuous_norm).eventually_mem εr] with e he     have e0 : e ≠ 0 := norm_pos_iff.1 (ε0.trans he)     calc       ‖e⁻¹ - r⁻¹‖ = ‖r‖⁻¹ * ‖r - e‖ * ‖e‖⁻¹ := by         rw [← norm_inv, ← norm_inv, ← norm_mul, ← norm_mul, _root_.mul_sub, _root_.sub_mul,           mul_assoc _ e, inv_mul_cancel r0, mul_inv_cancel e0, one_mul, mul_one]       -- Porting note: `ENNReal.{mul_sub, sub_mul}` should be `protected`       _ = ‖r - e‖ / ‖r‖ / ‖e‖ := by field_simp [mul_comm]       _ ≤ ‖r - e‖ / ‖r‖ / ε := by gcongr   refine squeeze_zero' (eventually_of_forall fun _ => norm_nonneg _) this ?_   refine (((continuous_const.sub continuous_id).norm.div_const _).div_const _).tendsto' _ _ ?_   simp

  (s : Set E) : Prop
StarConvex.comment:
Star-convexity of sets. `s` is star-convex at `x` if every segment from `x` to a point in `s` is
contained in `s`.
StarConvex.fullDefinition: def StarConvex : Prop :=   ∀ ⦃y : E⦄, y ∈ s → ∀ ⦃a b : 𝕜⦄, 0 ≤ a → 0 ≤ b → a + b = 1 → a • x + b • y ∈ s
StarConvex.description: A set is defined to be star-convex at a given point if every line segment drawn from that point to any point within the set remains entirely within the set itself.

LinearOrder.convexOn_of_lt.code:
LinearOrder.convexOn_of_lt.{u_1, u_2, u_5} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {β : Type u_5} [OrderedSemiring 𝕜]
  [AddCommMonoid E] [OrderedAddCommMonoid β] [Module 𝕜 E] [Module 𝕜 β] [LinearOrder E] {s : Set E} {f : E → β}
  (hs : Convex 𝕜 s)
  (hf :
    ∀ ⦃x : E⦄,
      x ∈ s →
        ∀ ⦃y : E⦄, y ∈ s → x < y → ∀ ⦃a b : 𝕜⦄, 0 < a → 0 < b → a + b = 1 → f (a • x + b • y) ≤ a • f x + b • f y) :
  ConvexOn 𝕜 s f
LinearOrder.convexOn_of_lt.comment:
For a function on a convex set in a linearly ordered space (where the order and the algebraic
structures aren't necessarily compatible), in order to prove that it is convex, it suffices to
verify the inequality `f (a • x + b • y) ≤ a • f x + b • f y` only for `x < y` and positive `a`,
`b`. The main use case is `E = 𝕜` however one can apply it, e.g., to `𝕜^n` with lexicographic order.

LinearOrder.strictConvexOn_of_lt.code:
LinearOrder.strictConvexOn_of_lt.{u_1, u_2, u_5} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {β : Type u_5} [OrderedSemiring 𝕜]
  [AddCommMonoid E] [OrderedAddCommMonoid β] [Module 𝕜 E] [Module 𝕜 β] [LinearOrder E] {s : Set E} {f : E → β}
  (hs : Convex 𝕜 s)
  (hf :
    ∀ ⦃x : E⦄,
      x ∈ s →
        ∀ ⦃y : E⦄, y ∈ s → x < y → ∀ ⦃a b : 𝕜⦄, 0 < a → 0 < b → a + b = 1 → f (a • x + b • y) < a • f x + b • f y) :
  StrictConvexOn 𝕜 s f
LinearOrder.strictConvexOn_of_lt.comment:
For a function on a convex set in a linearly ordered space (where the order and the algebraic
structures aren't necessarily compatible), in order to prove that it is strictly convex, it suffices
to verify the inequality `f (a • x + b • y) < a • f x + b • f y` for `x < y` and positive `a`, `b`.
The main use case is `E = 𝕜` however one can apply it, e.g., to `𝕜^n` with lexicographic order.

explanatories.ConvexCone.smul_mem: Scaling a point in a convex cone by a positive scalar results in a point that still lies within the same cone.
explanatories.ConvexCone.add_mem: The sum of any two elements within a convex cone is also an element of that same cone.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_smul: This theorem states that a linear map commutes with scalar multiplication, meaning that applying the map to the product of a scalar and a vector is the same as multiplying the image of the vector by the scalar.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_add: This theorem states that a linear map preserves the addition operation by ensuring that the image of the sum of two elements equals the sum of their images.
explanatories.Set.mem_preimage: An element is in the preimage of a set under a function if and only if the image of that element is in the original set.
explanatories.Submodule.smul_mem: This theorem demonstrates that if an element belongs to a submodule, then its scalar multiplication by any element from the semiring also lies within the same submodule, thereby confirming closure under scalar multiplication.
explanatories.Submodule.add_mem: This theorem asserts that the sum of two elements from a submodule of a module is also an element of that submodule.

ConvexCone.comap.description: The preimage of a convex cone through a linear map is also a convex cone.

explanatories.Set.mem_iUnion: An element belongs to the union of a collection of sets if and only if it is an element of at least one set within that collection.
explanatories.Set.mem_smul_set: The theorem states that an element belongs to the scalar multiplication of a set by an element if and only if there exists an element in the set such that the scalar multiplication of that element with the given scalar equals the element in question.
explanatories.mul_pos: This theorem asserts that the product of two positive elements in a type with certain algebraic properties is also positive.
explanatories.smul_smul: This theorem shows that the action of the product of two elements from a monoid on another element is the same as performing the actions sequentially and is associative.
explanatories.convex_iff_div: A set is convex if and only if any point within the set can be expressed as a weighted average of two other points in the set using non-negative weights that sum to one.
explanatories.mul_div_assoc': In a structure with division and inverses, multiplying an element by the quotient of two elements is equivalent to multiplying the same element by the numerator and then dividing by the denominator.

convex.to_cone.fullDefinition: def toCone (s : Set E) (hs : Convex 𝕜 s) : ConvexCone 𝕜 E := by   apply ConvexCone.mk (⋃ (c : 𝕜) (_ : 0 < c), c • s) <;> simp only [mem_iUnion, mem_smul_set]   · rintro c c_pos _ ⟨c', c'_pos, x, hx, rfl⟩     exact ⟨c * c', mul_pos c_pos c'_pos, x, hx, (smul_smul _ _ _).symm⟩   · rintro _ ⟨cx, cx_pos, x, hx, rfl⟩ _ ⟨cy, cy_pos, y, hy, rfl⟩     have : 0 < cx + cy := add_pos cx_pos cy_pos     refine ⟨_, this, _, convex_iff_div.1 hs hx hy cx_pos.le cy_pos.le this, ?_⟩     simp only [smul_add, smul_smul, mul_div_assoc', mul_div_cancel_left₀ _ this.ne']

RieszExtension.step.code:
RieszExtension.step.{u_2} {E : Type u_2} [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E] (s : ConvexCone ℝ E) (f : E →ₗ.[ℝ] ℝ)
  (nonneg : ∀ (x : ↥f.domain), ↑x ∈ s → 0 ≤ ↑f x) (dense : ∀ (y : E), ∃ x, ↑x + y ∈ s) (hdom : f.domain ≠ ⊤) :
  ∃ g, f < g ∧ ∀ (x : ↥g.domain), ↑x ∈ s → 0 ≤ ↑g x
RieszExtension.step.comment:
Induction step in M. Riesz extension theorem. Given a convex cone `s` in a vector space `E`,
a partially defined linear map `f : f.domain → ℝ`, assume that `f` is nonnegative on `f.domain ∩ p`
and `p + s = E`. If `f` is not defined on the whole `E`, then we can extend it to a larger
submodule without breaking the non-negativity condition.

RieszExtension.step.description: Under certain conditions, it is possible to extend a partially defined linear map to a larger domain while maintaining the property of non-negativity on a convex cone in a vector space.

riesz_extension.code:
riesz_extension.{u_2} {E : Type u_2} [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E] (s : ConvexCone ℝ E) (f : E →ₗ.[ℝ] ℝ)
  (nonneg : ∀ (x : ↥f.domain), ↑x ∈ s → 0 ≤ ↑f x) (dense : ∀ (y : E), ∃ x, ↑x + y ∈ s) :
  ∃ g, (∀ (x : ↥f.domain), g ↑x = ↑f x) ∧ ∀ x ∈ s, 0 ≤ g x
riesz_extension.comment:
M. **Riesz extension theorem**: given a convex cone `s` in a vector space `E`, a submodule `p`,
and a linear `f : p → ℝ`, assume that `f` is nonnegative on `p ∩ s` and `p + s = E`. Then
there exists a globally defined linear function `g : E → ℝ` that agrees with `f` on `p`,
and is nonnegative on `s`.
riesz_extension.description: Given a convex cone in a vector space and a nonnegative linear map defined on a submodule, it is possible to find a globally defined linear function that extends this map while remaining nonnegative on the convex cone.

exists_extension_of_le_sublinear.code:
exists_extension_of_le_sublinear.{u_2} {E : Type u_2} [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E] (f : E →ₗ.[ℝ] ℝ) (N : E → ℝ)
  (N_hom : ∀ (c : ℝ), 0 < c → ∀ (x : E), N (c • x) = c * N x) (N_add : ∀ (x y : E), N (x + y) ≤ N x + N y)
  (hf : ∀ (x : ↥f.domain), ↑f x ≤ N ↑x) : ∃ g, (∀ (x : ↥f.domain), g ↑x = ↑f x) ∧ ∀ (x : E), g x ≤ N x
exists_extension_of_le_sublinear.comment:
**Hahn-Banach theorem**: if `N : E → ℝ` is a sublinear map, `f` is a linear map
defined on a subspace of `E`, and `f x ≤ N x` for all `x` in the domain of `f`,
then `f` can be extended to the whole space to a linear map `g` such that `g x ≤ N x`
for all `x`.
exists_extension_of_le_sublinear.description: If a sublinear map bounds a given linear map defined on a subspace, then it is possible to extend this linear map to the entire space while preserving the bounding condition.

PointedCone.comment: A pointed cone is a submodule of a module with scalars restricted to being nonnegative.
PointedCone.fullDefinition: abbrev PointedCone (𝕜 E) [OrderedSemiring 𝕜] [AddCommMonoid E] [Module 𝕜 E] :=   Submodule {c : 𝕜 // 0 ≤ c} E
PointedCone.description: This defines a pointed cone as a submodule within a module where the scalar multiplication is limited to nonnegative values.

  (S : PointedCone 𝕜 E) : ConvexCone 𝕜 E
PointedCone.toConvexCone.comment: Every pointed cone is a convex cone.

explanatories.Submodule.smul_mem: This theorem demonstrates that if an element belongs to a submodule, then its scalar multiplication by any element from the semiring also lies within the same submodule, thereby confirming closure under scalar multiplication.
explanatories.le_of_lt: This theorem asserts that if one element is strictly less than another in a preorder, then it is also less than or equal to that element.
explanatories.Submodule.add_mem: This theorem asserts that the sum of two elements from a submodule of a module is also an element of that submodule.
explanatories.ConvexCone.add_mem: The sum of any two elements within a convex cone is also an element of that same cone.
explanatories.ConvexCone.smul_mem: Scaling a point in a convex cone by a positive scalar results in a point that still lies within the same cone.

PointedCone.toConvexCone.fullDefinition: def toConvexCone (S : PointedCone 𝕜 E) : ConvexCone 𝕜 E where   carrier := S   smul_mem' c hc _ hx := S.smul_mem ⟨c, le_of_lt hc⟩ hx   add_mem' _ hx _ hy := S.add_mem hx hy
PointedCone.toConvexCone.description: This defines a mapping from a pointed cone to a convex cone, establishing that every pointed cone inherently qualifies as a convex cone.

explanatories.ConvexCone.add_mem: The sum of any two elements within a convex cone is also an element of that same cone.
explanatories.SetLike.mem_coe: This theorem states that an element belongs to the set representation of an element from a structure defined as `SetLike` if and only if it belongs to the element itself.
explanatories.eq_or_lt_of_le: A theorem stating that in a partially ordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to another, then it is either equal to or strictly less than the other.
explanatories.ConvexCone.smul_mem: Scaling a point in a convex cone by a positive scalar results in a point that still lies within the same cone.

ConvexCone.toPointedCone.fullDefinition: def _root_.ConvexCone.toPointedCone {S : ConvexCone 𝕜 E} (hS : S.Pointed) : PointedCone 𝕜 E where   carrier := S   add_mem' hx hy := S.add_mem hx hy   zero_mem' := hS   smul_mem' := fun ⟨c, hc⟩ x hx => by     simp_rw [SetLike.mem_coe]     cases' eq_or_lt_of_le hc with hzero hpos     · unfold ConvexCone.Pointed at hS       convert hS       simp [← hzero]     · apply ConvexCone.smul_mem       · convert hpos       · exact hx
ConvexCone.toPointedCone.description: This defines a construction that generates a pointed cone from a pointed convex cone, demonstrating the relationship between these two geometric structures.

  {x y z : 𝕜} (hx : x ∈ s) (hz : z ∈ s) (hxy : x < y) (hyz : y < z) : (f y - f x) / (y - x) ≤ (f z - f y) / (z - y)

`f` on `[x, y]` is less than the slope of the secant line of `f` on `[y, z]`.

  (ht : t ∈ K.faces) :
  Disjoint ((convexHull 𝕜) ↑s) ((convexHull 𝕜) ↑t) ∨

Geometry.SimplicialComplex.disjoint_or_e.comment:
The conclusion is the usual meaning of "glue nicely" in textbooks. It turns out to be quite
unusable, as it's about faces as sets in space rather than simplices. Further, additional structure
on `𝕜` means the only choice of `u` is `s ∩ t` (but it's hard to prove).

Finset.centerMass_pair.code:
Finset.centerMass_pair.{u_1, u_3, u_5} {R : Type u_1} {E : Type u_3} {ι : Type u_5} [LinearOrderedField R]
  [AddCommGroup E] [Module R E] (i j : ι) (w : ι → R) (z : ι → E) (hne : i ≠ j) :

Finset.centerMass_pair.description: The center of mass of a pair of points, given their respective weights, is expressed as a weighted combination of their positions based on those weights.

Finset.centerMass_insert.code:
Finset.centerMass_insert.{u_1, u_3, u_5} {R : Type u_1} {E : Type u_3} {ι : Type u_5} [LinearOrderedField R]
  [AddCommGroup E] [Module R E] (i : ι) (t : Finset ι) {w : ι → R} (z : ι → E) (ha : i ∉ t) (hw : ∑ j ∈ t, w j ≠ 0) :
  (insert i t).centerMass w z =
    (w i / (w i + ∑ j ∈ t, w j)) • z i + ((∑ j ∈ t, w j) / (w i + ∑ j ∈ t, w j)) • t.centerMass w z
Finset.centerMass_insert.description: The center of mass of the union of a point and a finite set of points is expressed as a combination of the new point's position weighted by its weight and the center of mass of the original set, appropriately weighted by their total weights.

Finset.centerMass.eq_1.description: The center of mass for a finite set of points with assigned weights and positions is defined as the weighted average of the positions, scaled by the total weight.

Finset.centerMass_segment'.code:
Finset.centerMass_segment'.{u_1, u_3, u_5, u_6} {R : Type u_1} {E : Type u_3} {ι : Type u_5} {ι' : Type u_6}
  [LinearOrderedField R] [AddCommGroup E] [Module R E] (s : Finset ι) (t : Finset ι') (ws : ι → R) (zs : ι → E)
  (wt : ι' → R) (zt : ι' → E) (hws : ∑ i ∈ s, ws i = 1) (hwt : ∑ i ∈ t, wt i = 1) (a b : R) (hab : a + b = 1) :
  a • s.centerMass ws zs + b • t.centerMass wt zt =
    (s.disjSum t).centerMass (Sum.elim (fun i => a * ws i) fun j => b * wt j) (Sum.elim zs zt)
Finset.centerMass_segment'.comment:
A convex combination of two centers of mass is a center of mass as well. This version
deals with two different index types.

explanatories.Finset.disjSum: The definition specifies a disjoint sum of two finite sets, resulting in a new finite set that combines the elements from both sets while keeping them distinct.

Finset.centerMass_segment'.description: The center of mass of a convex combination of two finite sets of points is the same as the convex combination of their individual centers of mass, even when the sets are indexed differently.

  a • s.centerMass ws zs + b • t.centerMass wt zt =
    (s.disjSum t).centerMass (Sum.elim (fun i => a * ws i) fun j => b * wt j) (Sum.elim zs zt)

A convex combination of two centers of mass is a center of mass as well. This version

Finset.centerMass_segment.code:
Finset.centerMass_segment.{u_1, u_3, u_5} {R : Type u_1} {E : Type u_3} {ι : Type u_5} [LinearOrderedField R]
  [AddCommGroup E] [Module R E] (s : Finset ι) (w₁ w₂ : ι → R) (z : ι → E) (hw₁ : ∑ i ∈ s, w₁ i = 1)
  (hw₂ : ∑ i ∈ s, w₂ i = 1) (a b : R) (hab : a + b = 1) :

explanatories.Finset.sup': This definition describes a function that computes the supremum of the images of elements from a nonempty finite set under a given function in a join-semilattice structure, where the proof of nonemptiness is required.

Finset.centerMass_le_sup.description: The center of mass of a finite set is less than or equal to the supremum of the function values over that set, given that all weights are non-negative and their total is positive.

A version of `Convex.sum_mem` for `finsum`s. If `s` is a convex set, `w : ι → R` is a family of

that `z i ∈ s` whenever `w i ≠ 0`, then the sum `∑ᶠ i, w i • z i` belongs to `s`. See also
`PartitionOfUnity.finsum_smul_mem_convex`.

Set.Finite.convexHull_eq_image.code:
Set.Finite.convexHull_eq_image.{u_1, u_3} {R : Type u_1} {E : Type u_3} [LinearOrderedField R] [AddCommGroup E]
  [Module R E] {s : Set E} (hs : s.Finite) :
  (convexHull R) s = ⇑(∑ x : ↑s, (LinearMap.proj x).smulRight ↑x) '' stdSimplex R ↑s
Set.Finite.convexHull_eq_image.comment:
The convex hull of a finite set is the image of the standard simplex in `s → ℝ`
under the linear map sending each function `w` to `∑ x ∈ s, w x • x`.

Since we have no sums over finite sets, we use sum over `@Finset.univ _ hs.fintype`.
The map is defined in terms of operations on `(s → ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ` so that later we will not need
to prove that this map is linear.

explanatories.stdSimplex: The standard simplex is the set of functions from a finite type to a non-negative ordered semiring where the coordinates sum to one, representing a foundational object in the category of convex spaces.
explanatories.LinearMap.proj: This definition introduces a linear map that extracts a specific component from a family of modules indexed by a set.
explanatories.LinearMap.smulRight: This definition specifies how to construct a new linear map by taking an existing linear map and associating it with a fixed element, such that the output of the new map scales with that element's scalar multiplication.

Set.Finite.convexHull_eq_image.description: The convex hull of a finite set corresponds to the image of the standard simplex under a linear transformation that combines the weighted points from that set.

StrictConvexOn.map_sum_lt.code:
StrictConvexOn.map_sum_lt.{u_1, u_2, u_4, u_5} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {β : Type u_4} {ι : Type u_5}
  [LinearOrderedField 𝕜] [AddCommGroup E] [OrderedAddCommGroup β] [Module 𝕜 E] [Module 𝕜 β] [OrderedSMul 𝕜 β]
  {s : Set E} {f : E → β} {t : Finset ι} {w : ι → 𝕜} {p : ι → E} (hf : StrictConvexOn 𝕜 s f) (h₀ : ∀ i ∈ t, 0 < w i)
  (h₁ : ∑ i ∈ t, w i = 1) (hmem : ∀ i ∈ t, p i ∈ s) (hp : ∃ j ∈ t, ∃ k ∈ t, p j ≠ p k) :
  f (∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i) < ∑ i ∈ t, w i • f (p i)
StrictConvexOn.map_sum_lt.comment:
Convex **strict Jensen inequality**.

If the function is strictly convex, the weights are strictly positive and the indexed family of
points is non-constant, then Jensen's inequality is strict.

See also `StrictConvexOn.map_sum_eq_iff`.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

StrictConvexOn.map_sum_lt.description: For a strictly convex function defined on a set, when using strictly positive weights and a non-constant collection of points, the function value at the weighted sum of those points is strictly less than the weighted sum of the function values at those points, reflecting a strict form of Jensen's inequality.

StrictConvexOn.eq_of_le_map_sum.code:
StrictConvexOn.eq_of_le_map_sum.{u_1, u_2, u_4, u_5} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {β : Type u_4} {ι : Type u_5}
  [LinearOrderedField 𝕜] [AddCommGroup E] [OrderedAddCommGroup β] [Module 𝕜 E] [Module 𝕜 β] [OrderedSMul 𝕜 β]
  {s : Set E} {f : E → β} {t : Finset ι} {w : ι → 𝕜} {p : ι → E} (hf : StrictConvexOn 𝕜 s f) (h₀ : ∀ i ∈ t, 0 < w i)
  (h₁ : ∑ i ∈ t, w i = 1) (hmem : ∀ i ∈ t, p i ∈ s) (h_eq : ∑ i ∈ t, w i • f (p i) ≤ f (∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i)) ⦃j : ι⦄ :
  j ∈ t → ∀ ⦃k : ι⦄, k ∈ t → p j = p k
StrictConvexOn.eq_of_le_map_sum.comment:
A form of the **equality case of Jensen's equality**.

For a strictly convex function `f` and positive weights `w`, if
`f (∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i) = ∑ i ∈ t, w i • f (p i)`, then the points `p` are all equal.

See also `StrictConvexOn.map_sum_eq_iff`.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

StrictConvexOn.eq_of_le_map_sum.description: For a strictly convex function with positive weights, if the function value at the weighted sum of a set of points equals the weighted sum of the function values at those points, then all the points must be identical.

  [LinearOrderedField 𝕜] [AddCommGroup E] [OrderedAddCommGroup β] [Module 𝕜 E] [Module 𝕜 β] [OrderedSMul 𝕜 β]

  (h₁ : ∑ i ∈ t, w i = 1) (hmem : ∀ i ∈ t, p i ∈ s) :
  f (∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i) = ∑ i ∈ t, w i • f (p i) ↔ ∀ j ∈ t, p j = ∑ i ∈ t, w i • p i

Convex.radon_partition.comment:
**Radon's theorem on convex sets**.

Any family `f` of affine dependent vectors contains a set `I` with the property that convex hulls of
`I` and `Iᶜ` intersect nontrivially.

Convex.helly_theorem'.code:
Convex.helly_theorem'.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {ι : Type u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_2} {E : Type u_3} [DecidableEq ι]
  [LinearOrderedField 𝕜] [AddCommGroup E] [Module 𝕜 E] [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 E] {F : ι → Set E} {s : Finset ι}
  (h_convex : ∀ i ∈ s, Convex 𝕜 (F i)) (h_inter : ∀ I ⊆ s, I.card ≤ finrank 𝕜 E + 1 → (⋂ i ∈ I, F i).Nonempty) :
  (⋂ i ∈ s, F i).Nonempty
Convex.helly_theorem'.comment:
**Helly's theorem** for finite families of convex sets.

If `F` is a finite family of convex sets in a vector space of finite dimension `d`, and any
`k ≤ d + 1` sets of `F` intersect nontrivially, then all sets of `F` intersect nontrivially.

explanatories.DecidableEq: A type is said to have decidable equality if it is possible to determine whether any two elements of that type are equal.
explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.
explanatories.FiniteDimensional: This definition characterizes vector spaces as finite-dimensional if they can be understood as finite modules over a division ring.
explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Finset.card: This definition indicates that the cardinality of a finite set represents the total number of its elements.
explanatories.FiniteDimensional.finrank: The finite rank of a module is defined as a natural number representing its rank, which is considered to be zero when the module has infinite rank.
explanatories.PartENat.card: This definition specifies that the cardinality of a type is represented as an extended natural number, with infinite types having a cardinality denoted by a specific maximum value.

Convex.helly_theorem'.description: If a finite family of convex sets in a finite-dimensional vector space has the property that every subset of size at most one more than the dimension intersects nontrivially, then all sets in the family must also intersect nontrivially.

Convex.helly_theorem_set'.comment:
**Helly's theorem** for finite sets of convex sets.

If `F` is a finite set of convex sets in a vector space of finite dimension `d`, and any `k ≤ d + 1`
sets from `F` intersect nontrivially, then all sets from `F` intersect nontrivially.

explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.
explanatories.FiniteDimensional: This definition characterizes vector spaces as finite-dimensional if they can be understood as finite modules over a division ring.
explanatories.Finset.card: This definition indicates that the cardinality of a finite set represents the total number of its elements.
explanatories.FiniteDimensional.finrank: The finite rank of a module is defined as a natural number representing its rank, which is considered to be zero when the module has infinite rank.
explanatories.PartENat.card: This definition specifies that the cardinality of a type is represented as an extended natural number, with infinite types having a cardinality denoted by a specific maximum value.

Convex.helly_theorem_set'.description: If a finite collection of convex sets in a finite-dimensional vector space has the property that any subset of size at most one more than the dimension intersects nontrivially, then the intersection of all sets in the collection is nonempty.

  {F : ι → Set E} (h_convex : ∀ (i : ι), Convex 𝕜 (F i)) (h_compact : ∀ (i : ι), IsCompact (F i))
  (h_inter : ∀ (I : Finset ι), I.card ≤ finrank 𝕜 E + 1 → (⋂ i ∈ I, F i).Nonempty) : (⋂ i, F i).Nonempty
Convex.helly_theorem_compact'.comment:
**Helly's theorem** for families of compact convex sets.

If `F` is a family of compact convex sets in a vector space of finite dimension `d`, and any
`k ≤ d + 1` sets of `F` intersect nontrivially, then all sets of `F` intersect nontrivially.

explanatories.DecidableEq: A type is said to have decidable equality if it is possible to determine whether any two elements of that type are equal.
explanatories.Set.Nonempty: This defines a property that indicates a set is non-empty, providing a convenient notation for use in theorem assumptions.
explanatories.FiniteDimensional: This definition characterizes vector spaces as finite-dimensional if they can be understood as finite modules over a division ring.
explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.Finset.card: This definition indicates that the cardinality of a finite set represents the total number of its elements.
explanatories.FiniteDimensional.finrank: The finite rank of a module is defined as a natural number representing its rank, which is considered to be zero when the module has infinite rank.
explanatories.IsCompact: This defines the property of a set within a topological space being compact, which requires that for any nontrivial filter containing the set, there is an element within the set such that every set in the filter intersects with every neighborhood of that element.
explanatories.PartENat.card: This definition specifies that the cardinality of a type is represented as an extended natural number, with infinite types having a cardinality denoted by a specific maximum value.

Convex.helly_theorem_compact'.description: If a family of compact convex sets in a finite-dimensional vector space has the property that any subset of size at most one more than the dimension intersects nontrivially, then the intersection of all sets in the family is also nonempty.

egauge.code: egauge.{u_1, u_2} (𝕜 : Type u_1) [NNNorm 𝕜] {E : Type u_2} [SMul 𝕜 E] (s : Set E) (x : E) : ℝ≥0∞
egauge.comment:
The Minkowski functional for vector spaces over normed fields.
Given a set `s` in a vector space over a normed field `𝕜`,
`egauge s` is the functional which sends `x : E`
to the infimum of `‖c‖₊` over `c` such that `x` belongs to `s` scaled by `c`.

The definition only requires `𝕜` to have a `NNNorm` instance
and `(· • ·) : 𝕜 → E → E` to be defined.
This way the definition applies, e.g., to `𝕜 = ℝ≥0`.
For `𝕜 = ℝ≥0`, the function is equal (up to conversion to `ℝ`)
to the usual Minkowski functional defined in `gauge`.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

egauge.fullDefinition: noncomputable def egauge (𝕜 : Type*) [NNNorm 𝕜] {E : Type*} [SMul 𝕜 E] (s : Set E) (x : E) : ℝ≥0∞ :=   ⨅ (c : 𝕜) (_ : x ∈ c • s), ‖c‖₊
egauge.description: The egauge functional assigns a non-negative extended real number to a point in a vector space based on the infimum of the norms of scalars that can scale a set to include that point.

exists_continuous_forall_mem_convex_of_l.code:
exists_continuous_forall_mem_convex_of_local.{u_2, u_3} {X : Type u_2} {E : Type u_3} [TopologicalSpace X]
  [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E] [NormalSpace X] [ParacompactSpace X] [TopologicalSpace E] [ContinuousAdd E]
  [ContinuousSMul ℝ E] {t : X → Set E} (ht : ∀ (x : X), Convex ℝ (t x))
  (H : ∀ (x : X), ∃ U ∈ 𝓝 x, ∃ g, ContinuousOn g U ∧ ∀ y ∈ U, g y ∈ t y) : ∃ g, ∀ (x : X), g x ∈ t x
exists_continuous_forall_mem_convex_of_l.comment:
Let `X` be a normal paracompact topological space (e.g., any extended metric space). Let `E` be
a topological real vector space. Let `t : X → Set E` be a family of convex sets. Suppose that for
each point `x : X`, there exists a neighborhood `U ∈ 𝓝 X` and a function `g : X → E` that is
continuous on `U` and sends each `y ∈ U` to a point of `t y`. Then there exists a continuous map
`g : C(X, E)` such that `g x ∈ t x` for all `x`. See also
`exists_continuous_forall_mem_convex_of_local_const`.

explanatories.ContinuousOn: This defines a property indicating that a function between topological spaces is continuous at every point of a specified subset.

exists_continuous_forall_mem_convex_of_l.description: Given a normal paracompact topological space and a family of convex sets, the existence of local continuous functions implies the existence of a global continuous function that stays within these convex sets.

  [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E] [NormalSpace X] [ParacompactSpace X] [TopologicalSpace E] [ContinuousAdd E]
  [ContinuousSMul ℝ E] {t : X → Set E} (ht : ∀ (x : X), Convex ℝ (t x))
  (H : ∀ (x : X), ∃ c, ∀ᶠ (y : X) in 𝓝 x, c ∈ t y) : ∃ g, ∀ (x : X), g x ∈ t x
exists_continuous_forall_mem_convex_of_l.comment:
Let `X` be a normal paracompact topological space (e.g., any extended metric space). Let `E` be
a topological real vector space. Let `t : X → Set E` be a family of convex sets. Suppose that for
each point `x : X`, there exists a vector `c : E` that belongs to `t y` for all `y` in a
neighborhood of `x`. Then there exists a continuous map `g : C(X, E)` such that `g x ∈ t x` for all
`x`. See also `exists_continuous_forall_mem_convex_of_local`.

gaugeRescale.comment:
The gauge rescale map `gaugeRescale s t` sends each point `x` to the point `y` on the same ray
that has the same gauge w.r.t. `t` as `x` has w.r.t. `s`.

The characteristic property is satisfied if `gauge t x ≠ 0`, see `gauge_gaugeRescale'`.
In particular, it is satisfied for all `x`,
provided that `t` is absorbent and von Neumann bounded.

gaugeRescale.description: The gauge rescale map transforms each point in one set to a corresponding point in another set along the same direction, preserving a specific scaling relationship based on their respective gauges.

there exists a homeomorphism of the ambient space
that sends the interior, the closure, and the frontier of one set

explanatories.Eq.le: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if two elements are equal, then one is less than or equal to the other.
explanatories.LT.lt.le: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if one element is strictly less than a second, then it is also less than or equal to that second element.
explanatories.exists_forall_closed_ball_dist_add_le_tw: In a uniform convex space, for any positive epsilon, there exists a positive delta such that if two vectors are within a unit ball and at least epsilon apart, their sum stays within a distance of two minus delta from the origin.
explanatories.StrictConvexSpace.of_norm_add_ne_two: The theorem shows that a normed space is strictly convex if for any two distinct points of norm one, the norm of their sum is not equal to two.
explanatories.norm_sub_pos_iff: This theorem states that the norm of the quotient of two elements is positive if and only if the two elements are not equal.
explanatories.le_rfl: This theorem states that every element in a preorder is less than or equal to itself.
explanatories.LE.le.trans_lt: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second element and the second element is strictly less than a third, then the first element is strictly less than the third.
explanatories.sub_lt_self: This theorem states that if a positive element is subtracted from another element in an additive group, the result will be less than the original element.
explanatories.LT.lt.ne: A theorem indicating that in a preordered structure, if one element is strictly less than another, then they must be distinct.

one_add_mul_self_lt_rpow_one_add.code: one_add_mul_self_lt_rpow_one_add {s : ℝ} (hs : -1 ≤ s) (hs' : s ≠ 0) {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 < p) : 1 + p * s < (1 + s) ^ p
one_add_mul_self_lt_rpow_one_add.comment:
**Bernoulli's inequality** for real exponents, strict version: for `1 < p` and `-1 ≤ s`, with
`s ≠ 0`, we have `1 + p * s < (1 + s) ^ p`.
one_add_mul_self_lt_rpow_one_add.description: For values greater than one, if a real number is between negative one and zero, Bernoulli's inequality states that the sum of one and the product of this number with another greater than one is less than the result of raising the sum of one and this number to the power of that greater value.

one_add_mul_self_le_rpow_one_add.code: one_add_mul_self_le_rpow_one_add {s : ℝ} (hs : -1 ≤ s) {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p) : 1 + p * s ≤ (1 + s) ^ p
one_add_mul_self_le_rpow_one_add.comment:
**Bernoulli's inequality** for real exponents, non-strict version: for `1 ≤ p` and `-1 ≤ s`
we have `1 + p * s ≤ (1 + s) ^ p`.
one_add_mul_self_le_rpow_one_add.description: For values greater than or equal to one, if a real number is between negative one and zero, Bernoulli's inequality states that the sum of one and the product of this number with another value greater than or equal to one is less than or equal to the result of raising the sum of one and this number to the power of that greater value.

rpow_one_add_lt_one_add_mul_self.code:
rpow_one_add_lt_one_add_mul_self {s : ℝ} (hs : -1 ≤ s) (hs' : s ≠ 0) {p : ℝ} (hp1 : 0 < p) (hp2 : p < 1) :
  (1 + s) ^ p < 1 + p * s
rpow_one_add_lt_one_add_mul_self.comment:
**Bernoulli's inequality** for real exponents, strict version: for `0 < p < 1` and `-1 ≤ s`,
with `s ≠ 0`, we have `(1 + s) ^ p < 1 + p * s`.
rpow_one_add_lt_one_add_mul_self.description: For real numbers where the exponent is strictly between zero and one, and the base is slightly greater than negative one, the result of raising the base plus one to the exponent will be strictly less than the sum of one and the product of the exponent and the base.

UniformConvexOn.code: UniformConvexOn.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] (s : Set E) (φ : ℝ → ℝ) (f : E → ℝ) : Prop
UniformConvexOn.comment:
A function `f` from a real normed space is uniformly convex with modulus `φ` if
`f (t • x + (1 - t) • y) ≤ t • f x + (1 - t) • f y - t * (1 - t) * φ ‖x - y‖` for all `t ∈ [0, 1]`.

`φ` is usually taken to be a monotone function such that `φ r = 0 ↔ r = 0`.

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.

UniformConvexOn.fullDefinition: def UniformConvexOn (s : Set E) (φ : ℝ → ℝ) (f : E → ℝ) : Prop :=   Convex ℝ s ∧ ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ s → ∀ ⦃y⦄, y ∈ s → ∀ ⦃a b : ℝ⦄, 0 ≤ a → 0 ≤ b → a + b = 1 →     f (a • x + b • y) ≤ a • f x + b • f y - a * b * φ ‖x - y‖
UniformConvexOn.description: A function from a real normed space is uniformly convex with a given modulus if it satisfies a specific inequality involving linear combinations of points in the space.

UniformConcaveOn.code:
UniformConcaveOn.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] (s : Set E) (φ : ℝ → ℝ) (f : E → ℝ) :
  Prop
UniformConcaveOn.comment:
A function `f` from a real normed space is uniformly concave with modulus `φ` if
`t • f x + (1 - t) • f y + t * (1 - t) * φ ‖x - y‖ ≤ f (t • x + (1 - t) • y)` for all `t ∈ [0, 1]`.

`φ` is usually taken to be a monotone function such that `φ r = 0 ↔ r = 0`.

explanatories.Convex: This definition characterizes a set as convex if, for any two points within the set, the entire line segment connecting them remains within the set.

UniformConcaveOn.fullDefinition: def UniformConcaveOn (s : Set E) (φ : ℝ → ℝ) (f : E → ℝ) : Prop :=   Convex ℝ s ∧ ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ s → ∀ ⦃y⦄, y ∈ s → ∀ ⦃a b : ℝ⦄, 0 ≤ a → 0 ≤ b → a + b = 1 →     a • f x + b • f y + a * b * φ ‖x - y‖ ≤ f (a • x + b • y)
UniformConcaveOn.description: A function from a real normed space is uniformly concave with a given modulus if it satisfies a specific inequality involving linear combinations of points in the space.

StrongConvexOn.comment:
A function `f` from a real normed space is `m`-strongly convex if it is uniformly convex with
modulus `φ(r) = m / 2 * r ^ 2`.

In an inner product space, this is equivalent to `x ↦ f x - m / 2 * ‖x‖ ^ 2` being convex.

aux_sub.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] {a b m : ℝ} {x y : E} {f : E → ℝ}
  (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hb : 0 ≤ b) (hab : a + b = 1) :
  a * (f x - m / 2 * ‖x‖ ^ 2) + b * (f y - m / 2 * ‖y‖ ^ 2) + m / 2 * ‖a • x + b • y‖ ^ 2 =
    a * f x + b * f y - m / 2 * a * b * ‖x - y‖ ^ 2
_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.description: A weighted combination of a function evaluated at two points, adjusted by a quadratic term related to those points, is equal to the same weighted combination of the function values minus a term involving their squared distance.

_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.code:
aux_add.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] {a b m : ℝ} {x y : E} {f : E → ℝ}
  (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hb : 0 ≤ b) (hab : a + b = 1) :
  a * (f x + m / 2 * ‖x‖ ^ 2) + b * (f y + m / 2 * ‖y‖ ^ 2) - m / 2 * ‖a • x + b • y‖ ^ 2 =
    a * f x + b * f y + m / 2 * a * b * ‖x - y‖ ^ 2
_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.description: The expression shows that a specific weighted combination of function values and their corresponding quadratic terms at two points is equal to a similar combination plus a corrective term involving the squared distance between those points, under certain conditions on the weights.

convex_on_of_deriv2_nonneg.description: This theorem asserts that if a function is continuous on a convex set and twice differentiable in the interior with a nonnegative second derivative, then the function is convex on that set.

concaveOn_of_deriv2_nonpos.code:
concaveOn_of_deriv2_nonpos {D : Set ℝ} (hD : Convex ℝ D) {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : ContinuousOn f D)
  (hf' : DifferentiableOn ℝ f (interior D)) (hf'' : DifferentiableOn ℝ (deriv f) (interior D))
  (hf''_nonpos : ∀ x ∈ interior D, deriv^[2] f x ≤ 0) : ConcaveOn ℝ D f
concaveOn_of_deriv2_nonpos.comment:
If a function `f` is continuous on a convex set `D ⊆ ℝ`, is twice differentiable on its
interior, and `f''` is nonpositive on the interior, then `f` is concave on `D`.

  [NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E] {μ : Measure α} {s : Set E} {f : α → E} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (hs : Convex ℝ s)
  (hsc : IsClosed s) (hf : ∀ᵐ (x : α) ∂μ, f x ∈ s) (hfi : Integrable f μ) : ∫ (x : α), f x ∂μ ∈ s
Convex.integral_mem.comment:
If `μ` is a probability measure on `α`, `s` is a convex closed set in `E`, and `f` is an
integrable function sending `μ`-a.e. points to `s`, then the expected value of `f` belongs to `s`:
`∫ x, f x ∂μ ∈ s`. See also `Convex.sum_mem` for a finite sum version of this lemma.

ConvexOn.map_average_le.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {m0 : MeasurableSpace α} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E] {μ : Measure α} {s : Set E} {f : α → E} {g : E → ℝ} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] [NeZero μ]
  (hg : ConvexOn ℝ s g) (hgc : ContinuousOn g s) (hsc : IsClosed s) (hfs : ∀ᵐ (x : α) ∂μ, f x ∈ s)
  (hfi : Integrable f μ) (hgi : Integrable (g ∘ f) μ) : g (⨍ (x : α), f x ∂μ) ≤ ⨍ (x : α), g (f x) ∂μ
ConvexOn.map_average_le.comment:
**Jensen's inequality**: if a function `g : E → ℝ` is convex and continuous on a convex closed
set `s`, `μ` is a finite non-zero measure on `α`, and `f : α → E` is a function sending
`μ`-a.e. points to `s`, then the value of `g` at the average value of `f` is less than or equal to
the average value of `g ∘ f` provided that both `f` and `g ∘ f` are integrable. See also
`ConvexOn.map_centerMass_le` for a finite sum version of this lemma.

WithLp.comment:
A type synonym for the given `V`, associated with the L`p` norm. Note that by default this just
forgets the norm structure on `V`; it is up to downstream users to implement the L`p` norm (for
instance, on `Prod` and finite `Pi` types).
WithLp.fullDefinition: def WithLp (_p : ℝ≥0∞) (V : Type uV) : Type uV := V
WithLp.description: This defines a type associated with the Lp norm for a given type, with the understanding that the norm structure is not inherently included and must be implemented by users.

WithLp.equiv.comment:
The canonical equivalence between `WithLp p V` and `V`. This should always be used to convert
back and forth between the representations.

explanatories.Equiv.refl: This definition states that every type is self-equivalent, meaning it has an equivalence relation to itself.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.refl: This definition asserts that the identity map can be viewed as a linear equivalence between a module and itself over a semiring.

WithLp.equiv.fullDefinition: protected def equiv : WithLp p V ≃ V := Equiv.refl _
WithLp.equiv.description: This establishes a canonical equivalence between a type associated with the Lp norm and the original type, facilitating conversion between the two representations.

IsLprojection.Subtype.hasCompl.fullDefinition: instance Subtype.hasCompl : HasCompl { f : M // IsLprojection X f } :=   ⟨fun P => ⟨1 - P, P.prop.Lcomplement⟩⟩

  [FaithfulSMul M X] : SDiff { P // IsLprojection X P }

explanatories.IsLprojection.Lcomplement: This theorem establishes that if an operation is a linear projection, then its complement also qualifies as a linear projection in the same vector space.
explanatories.IsLprojection.mul: This theorem shows that the product of two linear projections is also a linear projection in the same vector space.
explanatories.Subtype.prop: This theorem asserts that for a specific subtype, the property defining the subtype holds when applied to its element.
explanatories.SDiff.sdiff: The set difference operation identifies all elements in one set that do not belong to another set.

IsLprojection.Subtype.sdiff.fullDefinition: instance Subtype.sdiff [FaithfulSMul M X] : SDiff { P : M // IsLprojection X P } :=   ⟨fun P Q => ⟨P * (1 - Q), P.prop.mul Q.prop.Lcomplement⟩⟩
IsLprojection.Subtype.sdiff.description: This definition establishes a subtype representing the set difference of linear projections within the context of a normed vector space.

explanatories.mul_one: This theorem establishes that multiplying any element in a multiplicative structure by one results in that same element.
explanatories.MulZeroClass.zero_mul: This theorem establishes that multiplying any element by zero results in zero, demonstrating that zero acts as a left absorbing element in multiplication.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Bot.bot: A function that retrieves the bottom element in a partially ordered set or lattice structure.
explanatories.Top.top: A function that retrieves the top element in a partially ordered set or lattice structure.
explanatories.OrderTop.le_top: Every element in an ordered type that has a maximum element is less than or equal to that maximum element.
explanatories.OrderBot.bot_le: The least element in an ordered type is less than or equal to any other element in that type.

IsLprojection.Subtype.boundedOrder.fullDefinition: instance Subtype.boundedOrder [FaithfulSMul M X] :     BoundedOrder { P : M // IsLprojection X P } where   top := 1   le_top P := (mul_one (P : M)).symm   bot := 0   bot_le P := (zero_mul (P : M)).symm
IsLprojection.Subtype.boundedOrder.description: This definition establishes that the set of linear projections in a normed vector space forms a bounded order structure.

explanatories.LinearMap.mkContinuous: This definition formulates a method for creating a continuous linear map from a linear map and a specified upper bound on its norm.
explanatories.mul_one: This theorem establishes that multiplying any element in a multiplicative structure by one results in that same element.
explanatories.smul_eq_mul: This theorem establishes that the scalar multiplication of two elements is equivalent to their multiplication in a type that has a multiplication operation.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_smul: This theorem states that a linear map commutes with scalar multiplication, meaning that applying the map to the product of a scalar and a vector is the same as multiplying the image of the vector by the scalar.
explanatories.mul_comm: This theorem states that multiplication is commutative in a certain algebraic structure, meaning that the product of two elements is the same regardless of their order.
explanatories.norm_smul_le: This theorem states that in a seminormed additive group, the norm of the scalar multiplication of an element by a scalar is less than or equal to the product of the norms of the scalar and the element.

LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap₁.description: This definition provides a way to reinterpret a linear map from a field into a module as a continuous linear map.

explanatories.LinearMap.mkContinuous: This definition formulates a method for creating a continuous linear map from a linear map and a specified upper bound on its norm.
explanatories.mul_one: This theorem establishes that multiplying any element in a multiplicative structure by one results in that same element.
explanatories.smul_eq_mul: This theorem establishes that the scalar multiplication of two elements is equivalent to their multiplication in a type that has a multiplication operation.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_smul: This theorem states that a linear map commutes with scalar multiplication, meaning that applying the map to the product of a scalar and a vector is the same as multiplying the image of the vector by the scalar.
explanatories.mul_comm: This theorem states that multiplication is commutative in a certain algebraic structure, meaning that the product of two elements is the same regardless of their order.
explanatories.norm_smul_le: This theorem states that in a seminormed additive group, the norm of the scalar multiplication of an element by a scalar is less than or equal to the product of the norms of the scalar and the element.

linear_map.to_continuous_linear_map₁.fullDefinition: def LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap₁ (f : 𝕜 →ₗ[𝕜] E) : 𝕜 →L[𝕜] E :=   f.mkContinuous ‖f 1‖ fun x => by     conv_lhs => rw [← mul_one x]     rw [← smul_eq_mul, f.map_smul, mul_comm]; exact norm_smul_le _ _
linear_map.to_continuous_linear_map₁.description: This definition provides a way to reinterpret a linear map from a field into a module as a continuous linear map.

A (semi-)linear map which is a homothety is a continuous linear map.
Since the field `𝕜` need not have `ℝ` as a subfield, this theorem is not directly deducible from
the corresponding theorem about isometries plus a theorem about scalar multiplication.  Likewise
for the other theorems about homotheties in this file.

NormedSpace.norm_smul_le.comment:
A normed space over a normed field is a vector space endowed with a norm which satisfies the
equality `‖c • x‖ = ‖c‖ ‖x‖`. We require only `‖c • x‖ ≤ ‖c‖ ‖x‖` in the definition, then prove
`‖c • x‖ = ‖c‖ ‖x‖` in `norm_smul`.

Note that since this requires `SeminormedAddCommGroup` and not `NormedAddCommGroup`, this
typeclass can be used for "semi normed spaces" too, just as `Module` can be used for
"semi modules".
NormedSpace.norm_smul_le.description: This theorem demonstrates that the norm of the scalar multiplication of a vector by a scalar is less than or equal to the product of the norms of the scalar and the vector.

explanatories.ULift.seminormedAddCommGroup: This definition establishes that the lifted version of a seminormed commutative group retains the structure of a seminormed commutative group.
explanatories.Prod.instModule: This definition establishes a module structure over the product of two types that both support module structures defined over a semiring.
explanatories.Prod.norm_def: This theorem defines the norm of an ordered pair as the maximum of the individual norms of its components.
explanatories.Prod.smul_snd: This theorem confirms that when multiplying a pair of elements by a scalar, the operation applied to the second component of the pair yields the same result as applying the scalar directly to that component.
explanatories.Prod.smul_fst: This theorem asserts that when multiplying a pair of elements with a scalar, the operation applied to the first component of the pair yields the same result as applying the scalar directly to that component.
explanatories.mul_max_of_nonneg: In a linear ordered semiring, multiplying a nonnegative number by the maximum of two other numbers yields the same result as taking the maximum of the products of the nonnegative number with each of the two numbers.
explanatories.norm_nonneg: This theorem asserts that the norm of any element in a seminormed group is non-negative.
explanatories.le_rfl: This theorem states that every element in a preorder is less than or equal to itself.

Prod.normedSpace.fullDefinition: instance Prod.normedSpace : NormedSpace 𝕜 (E × F) :=   { Prod.seminormedAddCommGroup (E := E) (F := F), Prod.instModule with     norm_smul_le := fun s x => by       simp only [norm_smul, Prod.norm_def, Prod.smul_snd, Prod.smul_fst,         mul_max_of_nonneg, norm_nonneg, le_rfl] }
Prod.normedSpace.description: This definition establishes that the Cartesian product of two normed spaces over a normed field also forms a normed space, equipped with the supremum norm.

NormedSpace.toModule'.comment:
While this may appear identical to `NormedSpace.toModule`, it contains an implicit argument
involving `NormedAddCommGroup.toSeminormedAddCommGroup` that typeclass inference has trouble
inferring.

Specifically, the following instance cannot be found without this `NormedSpace.toModule'`:
```lean
example
  (𝕜 ι : Type*) (E : ι → Type*)
  [NormedField 𝕜] [Π i, NormedAddCommGroup (E i)] [Π i, NormedSpace 𝕜 (E i)] :
  Π i, Module 𝕜 (E i) := by infer_instance
```

[This Zulip thread](https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/113488-general/topic/Typeclass.20resolution.20under.20binders/near/245151099)
gives some more context.

NormedSpace.noncompactSpace.comment:
A normed vector space over an infinite normed field is a noncompact space.
This cannot be an instance because in order to apply it,

We register this as an instance in two cases: `𝕜 = E` and `𝕜 = ℝ`.

the strategy there, a non-unital *normed* algebra can be written as:
```lean

variable [NormedSpace 𝕜 𝕜'] [SMulCommClass 𝕜 𝕜' 𝕜'] [IsScalarTower 𝕜 𝕜' 𝕜']
```

explanatories.NormedSpace.norm_smul_le: This theorem demonstrates that the norm of the scalar multiplication of a vector by a scalar is less than or equal to the product of the norms of the scalar and the vector.

NormedAlgebra.norm_smul_le.description: This theorem asserts that in a normed algebra, the norm of the product of a scalar and an element is less than or equal to the product of their respective norms.

explanatories.Prod.normedSpace: This definition establishes that the Cartesian product of two normed spaces over a normed field also forms a normed space, equipped with the supremum norm.
explanatories.Pi.normedSpace: This definition states that the product of a finite collection of normed spaces is itself a normed space, equipped with the supremum norm.
explanatories.Submodule.normedSpace: This definition states that any subspace of a normed space inherits the structure of a normed space by using the restriction of the original norm.

explanatories.ULift.normedSpace: This definition establishes that the type obtained by lifting a seminormed additive group into a larger context retains its structure as a normed space.

RestrictScalars.normedSpace.fullDefinition: instance RestrictScalars.normedSpace : NormedSpace 𝕜 (RestrictScalars 𝕜 𝕜' E) :=   { RestrictScalars.module 𝕜 𝕜' E with     norm_smul_le := fun c x =>       (norm_smul_le (algebraMap 𝕜 𝕜' c) (_ : E)).trans_eq <| by rw [norm_algebraMap'] }
RestrictScalars.normedSpace.description: This definition states that if a space is normed over one field, it can be treated as a normed space over a subfield that is a normed algebra over the larger field.

NormedSpace.restrictScalars.comment:
Warning: This declaration should be used judiciously.
Please consider using `IsScalarTower` and/or `RestrictScalars 𝕜 𝕜' E` instead.

This definition allows the `RestrictScalars.normedSpace` instance to be put directly on `E`
rather on `RestrictScalars 𝕜 𝕜' E`. This would be a very bad instance; both because `𝕜'` cannot be
inferred, and because it is likely to create instance diamonds.

AffineIsometryEquiv.mk'.comment:
Construct an affine isometry equivalence by verifying the relation between the map and its
linear part at one base point. Namely, this function takes a map `e : P₁ → P₂`, a linear isometry
equivalence `e' : V₁ ≃ᵢₗ[k] V₂`, and a point `p` such that for any other point `p'` we have
`e p' = e' (p' -ᵥ p) +ᵥ e p`.

SpectrumRestricts.starAlgHom.fullDefinition: def starAlgHom {R : Type u} {S : Type v} {A : Type w} [Semifield R]     [StarRing R] [TopologicalSpace R] [TopologicalSemiring R] [ContinuousStar R] [Semifield S]     [StarRing S] [TopologicalSpace S] [TopologicalSemiring S] [ContinuousStar S] [Ring A]     [StarRing A] [Algebra R S] [Algebra R A] [Algebra S A]     [IsScalarTower R S A] [StarModule R S] [ContinuousSMul R S] {a : A}     (φ : C(spectrum S a, S) →⋆ₐ[S] A) {f : C(S, R)} (h : SpectrumRestricts a f) :     C(spectrum R a, R) →⋆ₐ[R] A :=   (φ.restrictScalars R).comp <|     (ContinuousMap.compStarAlgHom (spectrum S a) (.ofId R S) (algebraMapCLM R S).continuous).comp <|       ContinuousMap.compStarAlgHom' R R         ⟨Subtype.map f h.subset_preimage, (map_continuous f).subtype_map           fun x (hx : x ∈ spectrum S a) => h.subset_preimage hx⟩

SpectrumRestricts.homeomorph.fullDefinition: def homeomorph {R S A : Type*} [Semifield R] [Semifield S] [Ring A]     [Algebra R S] [Algebra R A] [Algebra S A] [IsScalarTower R S A] [TopologicalSpace R]     [TopologicalSpace S] [ContinuousSMul R S] {a : A} {f : C(S, R)} (h : SpectrumRestricts a f) :     spectrum S a ≃ₜ spectrum R a where   toFun := MapsTo.restrict f _ _ h.subset_preimage   invFun := MapsTo.restrict (algebraMap R S) _ _ (image_subset_iff.mp h.algebraMap_image.subset)   left_inv x := Subtype.ext <| h.rightInvOn x.2   right_inv x := Subtype.ext <| h.left_inv x   continuous_toFun := continuous_induced_rng.mpr <| f.continuous.comp continuous_induced_dom   continuous_invFun := continuous_induced_rng.mpr <|     continuous_algebraMap R S |>.comp continuous_induced_dom
SpectrumRestricts.homeomorph.description: The definition establishes a homeomorphism between the spectra of two algebras induced by the restriction condition of an element in the larger algebra to a smaller scalar ring.

QuasispectrumRestricts.nonUnitalStarAlgH.fullDefinition: def nonUnitalStarAlgHom {R : Type u} {S : Type v} {A : Type w} [Semifield R]     [StarRing R] [TopologicalSpace R] [TopologicalSemiring R] [ContinuousStar R] [Field S]     [StarRing S] [TopologicalSpace S] [TopologicalRing S] [ContinuousStar S] [NonUnitalRing A]     [StarRing A] [Algebra R S] [Module R A] [Module S A] [IsScalarTower S A A] [SMulCommClass S A A]     [IsScalarTower R S A] [StarModule R S] [ContinuousSMul R S] {a : A}     (φ : C(σₙ S a, S)₀ →⋆ₙₐ[S] A) {f : C(S, R)} (h : QuasispectrumRestricts a f) :     C(σₙ R a, R)₀ →⋆ₙₐ[R] A :=   (φ.restrictScalars R).comp <|     (nonUnitalStarAlgHom_postcomp (σₙ S a) (StarAlgHom.ofId R S) (algebraMapCLM R S).continuous)       |>.comp <| nonUnitalStarAlgHom_precomp R         ⟨⟨Subtype.map f h.subset_preimage, (map_continuous f).subtype_map           fun x (hx : x ∈ σₙ S a) => h.subset_preimage hx⟩, Subtype.ext h.map_zero⟩

QuasispectrumRestricts.homeomorph.fullDefinition: def homeomorph {R S A : Type*} [Semifield R] [Field S] [NonUnitalRing A]     [Algebra R S] [Module R A] [Module S A] [IsScalarTower R S A] [TopologicalSpace R]     [TopologicalSpace S] [ContinuousSMul R S] [IsScalarTower S A A] [SMulCommClass S A A]     {a : A} {f : C(S, R)} (h : QuasispectrumRestricts a f) :     σₙ S a ≃ₜ σₙ R a where   toFun := MapsTo.restrict f _ _ h.subset_preimage   invFun := MapsTo.restrict (algebraMap R S) _ _ (image_subset_iff.mp h.algebraMap_image.subset)   left_inv x := Subtype.ext <| h.rightInvOn x.2   right_inv x := Subtype.ext <| h.left_inv x   continuous_toFun := continuous_induced_rng.mpr <| f.continuous.comp continuous_induced_dom   continuous_invFun := continuous_induced_rng.mpr <|     continuous_algebraMap R S |>.comp continuous_induced_dom

cfcₙAux.code:
cfcₙAux.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2} [RCLike 𝕜] [NonUnitalNormedRing A] [StarRing A] [NormedSpace 𝕜 A]
  [IsScalarTower 𝕜 A A] [SMulCommClass 𝕜 A A] [StarModule 𝕜 A] {p : A → Prop} {p₁ : Unitization 𝕜 A → Prop}
  (hp₁ : ∀ {x : A}, p₁ ↑x ↔ p x) (a : A) (ha : p a) [ContinuousFunctionalCalculus 𝕜 p₁] :
  C(↑(σₙ 𝕜 a), 𝕜)₀ →⋆ₙₐ[𝕜] Unitization 𝕜 A
cfcₙAux.comment:
This is an auxiliary definition used for constructing an instance of the non-unital continuous
functional calculus given a instance of the unital one on the unitization.

This is the natural non-unital star homomorphism obtained from the chain
```lean
calc
  C(σₙ 𝕜 a, 𝕜)₀ →⋆ₙₐ[𝕜] C(σₙ 𝕜 a, 𝕜) := ContinuousMapZero.toContinuousMapHom
  _             ≃⋆[𝕜] C(σ 𝕜 (↑a : A⁺¹), 𝕜) := Homeomorph.compStarAlgEquiv'
  _             →⋆ₐ[𝕜] A⁺¹ := cfcHom
```
This range of this map is contained in the range of `(↑) : A → A⁺¹` (see `cfcₙAux_mem_range_inr`),
and so we may restrict it to `A` to get the necessary homomorphism for the non-unital continuous
functional calculus.

CstarRing.spectralOrder.comment:
The partial order on a unital C⋆-algebra defined by `x ≤ y` if and only if `y - x` is
selfadjoint and has nonnegative spectrum.

This is not declared as an instance because one may already have a partial order with better
definitional properties. However, it can be useful to invoke this as an instance in proofs.

explanatories.neg_sub: The negation of the difference between two elements in a subtraction monoid is equal to the difference of the second element from the first.

CstarRing.spectralOrder.fullDefinition: def CstarRing.spectralOrder : PartialOrder A where   le x y := IsSelfAdjoint (y - x) ∧ SpectrumRestricts (y - x) ContinuousMap.realToNNReal   le_refl := by     simp only [sub_self, IsSelfAdjoint.zero, true_and, forall_const]     rw [SpectrumRestricts.nnreal_iff]     nontriviality A     simp   le_antisymm x y hxy hyx := by     rw [← sub_eq_zero]     exact hyx.2.eq_zero_of_neg hyx.1 (neg_sub x y ▸ hxy.2)   le_trans x y z hxy hyz :=     ⟨by simpa using hyz.1.add hxy.1, by simpa using hyz.2.nnreal_add hyz.1 hxy.1 hxy.2⟩
CstarRing.spectralOrder.description: This definition describes a partial order on a unital C⋆-algebra where one element is considered less than or equal to another if their difference is self-adjoint and has a non-negative spectrum.

DoubleCentralizer.instStar.fullDefinition: instance instStar : Star 𝓜(𝕜, A) where   star a :=     { fst :=         (((starₗᵢ 𝕜 : A ≃ₗᵢ⋆[𝕜] A) : A →L⋆[𝕜] A).comp a.snd).comp           ((starₗᵢ 𝕜 : A ≃ₗᵢ⋆[𝕜] A) : A →L⋆[𝕜] A)       snd :=         (((starₗᵢ 𝕜 : A ≃ₗᵢ⋆[𝕜] A) : A →L⋆[𝕜] A).comp a.fst).comp           ((starₗᵢ 𝕜 : A ≃ₗᵢ⋆[𝕜] A) : A →L⋆[𝕜] A)       central := fun x y => by         simpa only [star_mul, star_star] using (congr_arg star (a.central (star y) (star x))).symm }

DoubleCentralizer.coeHom.fullDefinition: noncomputable def coeHom [StarRing 𝕜] [StarRing A] [StarModule 𝕜 A] [NormedStarGroup A] :     A →⋆ₙₐ[𝕜] 𝓜(𝕜, A) where   toFun a := a   map_smul' _ _ := ext _ _ _ _ <| Prod.ext (map_smul _ _ _) (map_smul _ _ _)   map_zero' := ext _ _ _ _ <| Prod.ext (map_zero _) (map_zero _)   map_add' _ _ := ext _ _ _ _ <| Prod.ext (map_add _ _ _) (map_add _ _ _)   map_mul' _ _ := ext _ _ _ _ <| Prod.ext     (ContinuousLinearMap.ext fun _ => (mul_assoc _ _ _))     (ContinuousLinearMap.ext fun _ => (mul_assoc _ _ _).symm)   map_star' _ := ext _ _ _ _ <| Prod.ext     (ContinuousLinearMap.ext fun _ => (star_star_mul _ _).symm)     (ContinuousLinearMap.ext fun _ => (star_mul_star _ _).symm)

DoubleCentralizer.instAlgebra.fullDefinition: instance instAlgebra : Algebra 𝕜 𝓜(𝕜, A) where   toFun k :=     { toProd := algebraMap 𝕜 ((A →L[𝕜] A) × (A →L[𝕜] A)) k       central := fun x y => by         simp_rw [Prod.algebraMap_apply, Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one, smul_apply, one_apply,           mul_smul_comm, smul_mul_assoc] }   map_one' := ext (𝕜 := 𝕜) (A := A) _ _ <| map_one <| algebraMap 𝕜 ((A →L[𝕜] A) × (A →L[𝕜] A))   map_mul' k₁ k₂ :=     ext (𝕜 := 𝕜) (A := A) _ _ <|       Prod.ext (map_mul (algebraMap 𝕜 (A →L[𝕜] A)) _ _)         ((map_mul (algebraMap 𝕜 (A →L[𝕜] A)) _ _).trans (Algebra.commutes _ _))   map_zero' := ext (𝕜 := 𝕜) (A := A) _ _ <| map_zero <| algebraMap 𝕜 ((A →L[𝕜] A) × (A →L[𝕜] A))   map_add' _ _ := ext (𝕜 := 𝕜) (A := A) _ _ <|     map_add (algebraMap 𝕜 ((A →L[𝕜] A) × (A →L[𝕜] A))) _ _   commutes' _ _ := ext (𝕜 := 𝕜) (A := A) _ _ <|     Prod.ext (Algebra.commutes _ _) (Algebra.commutes _ _).symm   smul_def' _ _ := ext (𝕜 := 𝕜) (A := A) _ _ <|     Prod.ext (Algebra.smul_def _ _) ((Algebra.smul_def _ _).trans <| Algebra.commutes _ _)

Matrix.toEuclideanCLM.comment:
The natural star algebra equivalence between matrices and continuous linear endomoporphisms
of Euclidean space induced by the orthonormal basis `EuclideanSpace.basisFun`.

This is a more-bundled version of `Matrix.toEuclideanLin`, for the special case of square matrices,
followed by a more-bundled version of `LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap`.

explanatories.EuclideanSpace: This definition describes the standard Euclidean space over either real or complex numbers, parameterized by the dimension represented as a finite type.
explanatories.EuclideanSpace.basisFun: This definition provides a specific orthonormal basis for a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, categorized as an orthonormal basis composed of function-like elements.
explanatories.StarAlgEquiv.trans: This definition establishes that the composition of two star algebra isomorphisms forms another star algebra isomorphism between the respective algebras.
explanatories.LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap: This definition describes a bijection between linear maps from a finite-dimensional vector space to another vector space and the continuous linear maps from the same vector space to the other one, over a nontrivially normed field.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
explanatories.LinearMap.adjoint_toContinuousLinearMap: This theorem shows that converting the adjoint of a linear map into a continuous linear map is equivalent to applying the adjoint operation after first converting the original linear map to a continuous linear map.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.trans: This definition establishes that if there are two linear equivalences between three modules with corresponding ring homomorphisms, then there exists a direct linear equivalence between the first and last modules.

Matrix.toEuclideanCLM.fullDefinition: def toEuclideanCLM :     Matrix n n 𝕜 ≃⋆ₐ[𝕜] (EuclideanSpace 𝕜 n →L[𝕜] EuclideanSpace 𝕜 n) :=   toMatrixOrthonormal (EuclideanSpace.basisFun n 𝕜) |>.symm.trans <|     { toContinuousLinearMap with       map_mul' := fun _ _ ↦ rfl       map_star' := adjoint_toContinuousLinearMap }
Matrix.toEuclideanCLM.description: This definition establishes a natural equivalence between square matrices and continuous linear transformations of Euclidean space that respects the structure of a star algebra.

Matrix.instL2OpMetricSpace.fullDefinition: def instL2OpMetricSpace : MetricSpace (Matrix m n 𝕜) := by   /- We first replace the topology so that we can automatically replace the uniformity using   `UniformAddGroup.toUniformSpace_eq`. -/   letI normed_add_comm_group : NormedAddCommGroup (Matrix m n 𝕜) :=     { l2OpNormedAddCommGroupAux.replaceTopology <|         (toEuclideanLin (𝕜 := 𝕜) (m := m) (n := n)).trans toContinuousLinearMap         |>.toContinuousLinearEquiv.toHomeomorph.inducing.induced with       norm := l2OpNormedAddCommGroupAux.norm       dist_eq := l2OpNormedAddCommGroupAux.dist_eq }   exact normed_add_comm_group.replaceUniformity <| by     congr     rw [← @UniformAddGroup.toUniformSpace_eq _ (Matrix.instUniformSpace m n 𝕜) _ _]     rw [@UniformAddGroup.toUniformSpace_eq _ PseudoEMetricSpace.toUniformSpace _ _]
