  [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] : NormedSpace 𝕜 (Matrix m n 𝕜)
Matrix.instL2OpNormedSpace.comment:
The normed algebra structure on `Matrix n n 𝕜` arising from the operator norm given by the
identification with (continuous) linear endmorphisms of `EuclideanSpace 𝕜 n`.

explanatories.StarAlgEquiv.trans: This definition establishes that the composition of two star algebra isomorphisms forms another star algebra isomorphism between the respective algebras.
explanatories.LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap: This definition describes a bijection between linear maps from a finite-dimensional vector space to another vector space and the continuous linear maps from the same vector space to the other one, over a nontrivially normed field.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.trans: This definition establishes that if there are two linear equivalences between three modules with corresponding ring homomorphisms, then there exists a direct linear equivalence between the first and last modules.
explanatories.Matrix.l2_opNorm_def: This theorem states that the operator norm of a matrix is equal to the norm of its corresponding continuous linear map in Euclidean space.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.map_smul: This theorem states that a linear equivalence preserves scalar multiplication when applied to elements of two modules over the same semiring.
explanatories.norm_smul_le: This theorem states that in a seminormed additive group, the norm of the scalar multiplication of an element by a scalar is less than or equal to the product of the norms of the scalar and the element.

Matrix.instL2OpNormedSpace.fullDefinition: def instL2OpNormedSpace : NormedSpace 𝕜 (Matrix m n 𝕜) where   norm_smul_le r x := by     rw [l2_opNorm_def, LinearEquiv.map_smul]     exact norm_smul_le r ((toEuclideanLin (𝕜 := 𝕜) (m := m) (n := n)).trans toContinuousLinearMap x)
Matrix.instL2OpNormedSpace.description: This definition describes the normed space structure on matrices corresponding to the operator norm derived from their identification with continuous linear transformations of Euclidean space.

Matrix.l2OpNormedRingAux.comment:
An auxiliary definition used only to construct the true `NormedRing` (and `Metric`) structure
provided by `Matrix.instMetricSpaceL2Op` and `Matrix.instNormedRingL2Op`.

explanatories.EuclideanSpace: This definition describes the standard Euclidean space over either real or complex numbers, parameterized by the dimension represented as a finite type.
explanatories.NormedAddCommGroup.induced: An injective group homomorphism from a commutative group to a normed group creates a normed commutative group structure on the original commutative group.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.injective: This theorem asserts that a linear equivalence is injective, meaning its underlying function maps distinct elements to distinct elements.
explanatories.NormedRing.induced: An injective non-unital ring homomorphism from a ring to a normed ring allows the domain to inherit a normed ring structure.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.toNormedRing: This definition establishes that the space of continuous linear maps over a normed space is equipped with the structure of a normed ring using the operator norm.
explanatories.RingEquiv.injective: This theorem asserts that a ring isomorphism is an injective function.

Matrix.l2OpNormedRingAux.fullDefinition: def l2OpNormedRingAux : NormedRing (Matrix n n 𝕜) :=   @NormedRing.induced ((Matrix n n 𝕜) ≃⋆ₐ[𝕜] (EuclideanSpace 𝕜 n →L[𝕜] EuclideanSpace 𝕜 n)) _     _ _ _ ContinuousLinearMap.toNormedRing _ _ toEuclideanCLM.injective
Matrix.l2OpNormedRingAux.description: This definition introduces an auxiliary structure that aids in constructing the true normed ring structure for matrices, which is further defined by other related structures.

Matrix.instL2OpNormedRing.code:

explanatories.NormedRing.dist_eq: This theorem establishes that the distance between two elements in a normed ring is equal to the norm of their difference.
explanatories.NormedRing.norm_mul: This theorem establishes that the norm of the product of two elements in a normed ring is less than or equal to the product of their individual norms.

Matrix.instL2OpNormedRing.fullDefinition: def instL2OpNormedRing : NormedRing (Matrix n n 𝕜) where   dist_eq := l2OpNormedRingAux.dist_eq   norm_mul := l2OpNormedRingAux.norm_mul
Matrix.instL2OpNormedRing.description: This definition establishes a normed ring structure for matrices through the operator norm by recognizing them as continuous linear endomorphisms of a Euclidean space.

explanatories.Function.comp_apply: The composition of two functions applied to an argument is equal to applying the first function to the result of applying the second function to that argument.
explanatories.selfAdjoint: The collection of self-adjoint elements in a star additive group forms an additive subgroup.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.IsSelfAdjoint.val_re_map_spectrum: The theorem demonstrates that the spectrum of a self-adjoint operator in a normed algebra corresponds to the image of its real part under a specific map that outputs real numbers.
explanatories.selfAdjoint.val_re_map_spectrum: The theorem confirms that the spectrum of a given self-adjoint operator in a normed algebra is equivalent to the image of its real part mapped into the complex numbers.
explanatories.StarHomClass.map_star: This theorem asserts that for a star-preserving map between two types with star structures, the star of an element's image is equal to the image of the star of that element.
explanatories.realPart_add_I_smul_imaginaryPart: The theorem demonstrates that any element in a star module over complex numbers can be expressed as the sum of its real part and the product of the imaginary unit with its imaginary part.
explanatories.map_add: There is no theorem or definition provided to summarize.
explanatories.map_smul: This theorem states that a morphism that is equivariant with respect to the actions of a monoid preserves the action when applied to the product of an element from the monoid and an element from the type.
explanatories.StarAddMonoid.star_add: This theorem asserts that in a type with a star addition structure, the star operation commutes with addition, so that the star of the sum of two elements equals the sum of the stars of each element.
explanatories.StarModule.star_smul: This theorem asserts that in a star module, the star operation distributes over scalar multiplication, meaning the star of a scalar multiplied by a vector equals the product of the star of the scalar and the star of the vector.
explanatories.selfAdjoint.star_val_eq: The image of a self-adjoint element under the star operation is equal to the element itself.
explanatories.AlgHom.apply_mem_spectrum: The application of a homomorphism on an algebra element results in an element that belongs to the spectrum of that algebra element.
explanatories.RCLike.star_def: This theorem establishes that the conjugate operation in a relational structure corresponds to the action of a specific endomorphism.

Ideal.toCharacterSpace.code:
Ideal.toCharacterSpace.{u_1} {A : Type u_1} [NormedCommRing A] [NormedAlgebra ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] (I : Ideal A)
  [I.IsMaximal] : ↑(characterSpace ℂ A)
Ideal.toCharacterSpace.comment:
Every maximal ideal in a commutative complex Banach algebra gives rise to a character on that
algebra. In particular, the character, which may be identified as an algebra homomorphism due to
`WeakDual.CharacterSpace.equivAlgHom`, is given by the composition of the quotient map and
the Gelfand-Mazur isomorphism `NormedRing.algEquivComplexOfComplete`.

explanatories.WeakDual.characterSpace: The definition describes the character space of a topological algebra as the subset of weak dual elements that act as algebra homomorphisms.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.NormedRing.algEquivComplexOfComplete: This definition establishes an isomorphism between a complete complex Banach algebra and the complex numbers, under the condition that nonzero elements are units, aligning with the Gelfand-Mazur theorem.
explanatories.Ideal.Quotient.field: The quotient of a commutative ring by a maximal ideal forms a field.
explanatories.isUnit_iff_ne_zero: This theorem states that in a group with zero, an element is a unit if and only if it is not equal to zero.
explanatories.AlgEquiv.symm: This definition indicates that every algebra equivalence has a corresponding inverse that switches the roles of the two algebras involved.
explanatories.AlgHom.comp: This definition describes how to construct a new algebra homomorphism by composing two existing algebra homomorphisms that connect three algebras over a common commutative semiring.
explanatories.Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ: This defines a canonical algebra morphism from an algebra to its quotient by an ideal.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function, where the output of the second function becomes the input of the first.
explanatories.StarAlgHom.comp: This definition describes the process of composing two star algebra homomorphisms to create a new star algebra homomorphism that connects the first algebra to the third through the second.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.comp: This definition describes the composition of two continuous maps, resulting in a new continuous map from the first space to the third space.

WeakDual.CharacterSpace.exists_apply_eq_.comment:
If `a : A` is not a unit, then some character takes the value zero at `a`. This is equivalent
to `gelfandTransform ℂ A a` takes the value zero at some character.

This lemma is used in the proof of `elementalStarAlgebra.isUnit_of_isUnit_of_isStarNormal`,
which in turn is the key to spectral permanence `StarSubalgebra.spectrum_eq`, which is itself
necessary for the continuous functional calculus. Using the continuous functional calculus, this
lemma can be superseded by one that omits the `IsStarNormal` hypothesis.

explanatories.Set.Icc: This definition describes the set of elements that are greater than or equal to one given element and less than or equal to another in a preorder structure, forming a left-closed and right-closed interval.
explanatories.IsUnit.star: This theorem asserts that if an element is a unit in a monoid, then its image under the star operation is also a unit in the same monoid.

spectrum_star_mul_self_of_isStarNormal.description: The theorem demonstrates that the spectrum of the product of an element in a normed star algebra and its adjoint lies within the closed interval from zero to the norm of that product.

established in `StarSubalgebra.spectrum_eq`. This lemma is superseded by

any closed star subalgebra.

explanatories.IsUnit: An element in a monoid is defined as a unit if there exists another element in the monoid that serves as its two-sided inverse.

elementalStarAlgebra.isUnit_of_isUnit_of.description: The theorem asserts that if an element in a normed star algebra is both star normal and a unit, then its associated star algebra element is also a unit.

StarSubalgebra.isUnit_coe_inv_mem.comment:
For `x : A` which is invertible in `A`, the inverse lies in any unital C⋆-subalgebra `S`
containing `x`.

explanatories.IsUnit: An element in a monoid is defined as a unit if there exists another element in the monoid that serves as its two-sided inverse.

StarSubalgebra.isUnit_coe_inv_mem.description: The theorem establishes that if an invertible element belongs to a unital C⋆-subalgebra, then its inverse is also contained within that subalgebra.

StarSubalgebra.coe_isUnit.code:

  [StarModule ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] {S : StarSubalgebra ℂ A} (hS : IsClosed ↑S) {x : ↥S} : IsUnit ↑x ↔ IsUnit x
StarSubalgebra.coe_isUnit.comment:
For a unital C⋆-subalgebra `S` of `A` and `x : S`, if `↑x : A` is invertible in `A`, then
`x` is invertible in `S`.

explanatories.IsUnit: An element in a monoid is defined as a unit if there exists another element in the monoid that serves as its two-sided inverse.

StarSubalgebra.coe_isUnit.description: The theorem states that within a closed unital C⋆-subalgebra, an element is invertible in the subalgebra if and only if its corresponding element in the larger algebra is invertible.

elementalStarAlgebra.characterSpaceToSpe.code:

elementalStarAlgebra.characterSpaceToSpe.comment:
The natural map from `characterSpace ℂ (elementalStarAlgebra ℂ x)` to `spectrum ℂ x` given
by evaluating `φ` at `x`. This is essentially just evaluation of the `gelfandTransform` of `x`,
but because we want something in `spectrum ℂ x`, as opposed to
`spectrum ℂ ⟨x, elementalStarAlgebra.self_mem ℂ x⟩` there is slightly more work to do.

explanatories.AlgHom.apply_mem_spectrum: The application of a homomorphism on an algebra element results in an element that belongs to the spectrum of that algebra element.

  [StarModule ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] (a : A) [IsStarNormal a] : C(↑(spectrum ℂ a), ℂ) ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] ↥(elementalStarAlgebra ℂ a)
continuousFunctionalCalculus.comment:
**Continuous functional calculus.** Given a normal element `a : A` of a unital C⋆-algebra,
the continuous functional calculus is a `StarAlgEquiv` from the complex-valued continuous
functions on the spectrum of `a` to the unital C⋆-subalgebra generated by `a`. Moreover, this
equivalence identifies `(ContinuousMap.id ℂ).restrict (spectrum ℂ a))` with `a`; see
`continuousFunctionalCalculus_map_id`. As such it extends the polynomial functional calculus.

explanatories.elementalStarAlgebra.characterSpaceHomeo: The definition establishes a homeomorphism between the character space of a unital C⋆-subalgebra generated by a normal element and the spectrum of that element.
explanatories.Homeomorph.compStarAlgEquiv': This defines an isomorphism of star algebra homomorphisms between the continuous functions from one topological space to another when the mapping between the spaces is a homeomorphism.
explanatories.StarAlgEquiv.trans: This definition establishes that the composition of two star algebra isomorphisms forms another star algebra isomorphism between the respective algebras.
explanatories.StarAlgEquiv.symm: This definition asserts that the inverse of a star algebra isomorphism between two algebras is itself a star algebra isomorphism in the reverse direction.

continuousFunctionalCalculus.fullDefinition: noncomputable def continuousFunctionalCalculus :     C(spectrum ℂ a, ℂ) ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] elementalStarAlgebra ℂ a :=   ((elementalStarAlgebra.characterSpaceHomeo a).compStarAlgEquiv' ℂ ℂ).trans     (gelfandStarTransform (elementalStarAlgebra ℂ a)).symm
continuousFunctionalCalculus.description: The definition provides an isomorphism between the algebra of continuous functions on the spectrum of a normal element in a unital C⋆-algebra and the unital C⋆-subalgebra generated by that element.

continuous_functional_calculus.code:
continuousFunctionalCalculus.{u_1} {A : Type u_1} [NormedRing A] [NormedAlgebra ℂ A] [StarRing A] [CstarRing A]
  [StarModule ℂ A] [CompleteSpace A] (a : A) [IsStarNormal a] : C(↑(spectrum ℂ a), ℂ) ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] ↥(elementalStarAlgebra ℂ a)
continuous_functional_calculus.comment:
**Continuous functional calculus.** Given a normal element `a : A` of a unital C⋆-algebra,
the continuous functional calculus is a `StarAlgEquiv` from the complex-valued continuous
functions on the spectrum of `a` to the unital C⋆-subalgebra generated by `a`. Moreover, this
equivalence identifies `(ContinuousMap.id ℂ).restrict (spectrum ℂ a))` with `a`; see
`continuousFunctionalCalculus_map_id`. As such it extends the polynomial functional calculus.

explanatories.elementalStarAlgebra: The topological closure of the subalgebra generated by a single element in a star algebra is a star subalgebra.
explanatories.HasSubset.Subset.trans: A theorem indicating that this is an alternative name for the transitive property of set inclusion.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Iff.symm: If two propositions are equivalent, then their equivalence can be reversed.
explanatories.elementalStarAlgebra.characterSpaceHomeo: The definition establishes a homeomorphism between the character space of a unital C⋆-subalgebra generated by a normal element and the spectrum of that element.
explanatories.Homeomorph.compStarAlgEquiv': This defines an isomorphism of star algebra homomorphisms between the continuous functions from one topological space to another when the mapping between the spaces is a homeomorphism.
explanatories.StarAlgEquiv.trans: This definition establishes that the composition of two star algebra isomorphisms forms another star algebra isomorphism between the respective algebras.
explanatories.StarAlgEquiv.symm: This definition asserts that the inverse of a star algebra isomorphism between two algebras is itself a star algebra isomorphism in the reverse direction.

continuous_functional_calculus.fullDefinition: noncomputable def continuousFunctionalCalculus :     C(spectrum ℂ a, ℂ) ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] elementalStarAlgebra ℂ a :=   ((elementalStarAlgebra.characterSpaceHomeo a).compStarAlgEquiv' ℂ ℂ).trans     (gelfandStarTransform (elementalStarAlgebra ℂ a)).symm
continuous_functional_calculus.description: The definition provides an isomorphism between the algebra of continuous functions on the spectrum of a normal element in a unital C⋆-algebra and the unital C⋆-subalgebra generated by that element.

explanatories.ContinuousMap.id: This definition describes the identity function as a continuous map from a topological space to itself.
explanatories.ContinuousMap.restrict: This definition describes the process of restricting a continuous function defined on one space to a subset of that space, producing a new continuous function mapping elements from the subset to the target space.

continuousFunctionalCalculus_map_id.description: The theorem demonstrates that the continuous functional calculus applied to the identity function on the spectrum of a normal element results in that element itself in the corresponding unital C⋆-algebra.

explanatories.ContinuousLinearEquiv.ofHomothety: This definition provides a method to create a continuous linear equivalence from a linear equivalence that scales inputs by a positive constant factor in a seminormed space.
explanatories.norm_pos_iff: This theorem establishes that the norm of an element in a normed group is positive if and only if the element is not equal to the identity.
explanatories.Iff.mpr: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.

ContinuousLinearEquiv.toSpanNonzeroSingl.description: This definition describes a continuous linear equivalence between a normed space and the span of a non-zero element in that space.

explanatories.mem_ball_zero_iff: This theorem characterizes membership in a ball centered at one with a specific radius in a seminormed group by stating that an element belongs to the ball if and only if its norm is less than the radius.
explanatories.norm_smul: This theorem states that in a normed division ring acting on a seminormed additive group, the norm of the scalar multiplication of an element by a scalar is equal to the product of the norms of the scalar and the element.
explanatories.one_mul: This theorem asserts that multiplying any element by the identity element in a multiplicative structure results in the element itself.
explanatories.mul_lt_mul': In a strict ordered semiring, if one element is less than or equal to another, another element is greater than a third, and the first is non-negative while the second is positive, then the product of the first two elements is less than the product of the last two elements.
explanatories.mem_closedBall_zero_iff: This theorem establishes that a point belongs to a closed ball centered at the origin with a given radius if and only if its norm is less than or equal to that radius.
explanatories.norm_nonneg: This theorem asserts that the norm of any element in a seminormed group is non-negative.
explanatories.one_pos: One is strictly greater than zero in any type that includes definitions for zero, one, and a partial order, provided that one is not equal to zero.
explanatories.Subtype.ext: This theorem states that two elements of a subtype are equal if their corresponding underlying elements are equal.
explanatories.one_smul: This theorem establishes that multiplying any element by the identity element of a monoid does not change the element itself.
explanatories.MulAction.mul_smul: This theorem states that the action of multiplying two elements behaves associatively with respect to both multiplication and the action on another element.
explanatories.Continuous.smul: The scalar multiplication of two continuous functions results in a continuous function.

explanatories.lt_of_le_of_lt: This theorem asserts that in a preorder, if one element is less than or equal to a second element and the second element is strictly less than a third, then the first element is also strictly less than the third.
explanatories.ENNReal.add_lt_top: This theorem states that the sum of two nonnegative extended real numbers is less than the top element if and only if each of the individual numbers is also less than the top element.
explanatories.ENNReal.mul_lt_top: This theorem states that the product of two nonnegative extended real numbers, neither of which is the top element, will always be less than the top element.
explanatories.LT.lt.ne: A theorem indicating that in a preordered structure, if one element is strictly less than another, then they must be distinct.

riesz_lemma.code:
riesz_lemma.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [NormedField 𝕜] {E : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]
  {F : Subspace 𝕜 E} (hFc : IsClosed ↑F) (hF : ∃ x, x ∉ F) {r : ℝ} (hr : r < 1) : ∃ x₀ ∉ F, ∀ y ∈ F, r * ‖x₀‖ ≤ ‖x₀ - y‖
riesz_lemma.comment:
Riesz's lemma, which usually states that it is possible to find a
vector with norm 1 whose distance to a closed proper subspace is
arbitrarily close to 1. The statement here is in terms of multiples of
norms, since in general the existence of an element of norm exactly 1
is not guaranteed. For a variant giving an element with norm in `[1, R]`, see
`riesz_lemma_of_norm_lt`.

explanatories.Subspace: This definition identifies a subspace of a vector space as essentially equivalent to a submodule within that vector space structure.

riesz_lemma.description: This theorem asserts the existence of a vector outside of a closed proper subspace such that its distance from any vector in that subspace can be controlled by a factor less than one times its norm.

riesz_lemma_of_norm_lt.code:
riesz_lemma_of_norm_lt.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [NormedField 𝕜] {E : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E]
  {c : 𝕜} (hc : 1 < ‖c‖) {R : ℝ} (hR : ‖c‖ < R) {F : Subspace 𝕜 E} (hFc : IsClosed ↑F) (hF : ∃ x, x ∉ F) :
  ∃ x₀, ‖x₀‖ ≤ R ∧ ∀ y ∈ F, 1 ≤ ‖x₀ - y‖
riesz_lemma_of_norm_lt.comment:
A version of Riesz lemma: given a strict closed subspace `F`, one may find an element of norm `≤ R`
which is at distance at least `1` of every element of `F`. Here, `R` is any given constant
strictly larger than the norm of an element of norm `> 1`. For a version without an `R`, see
`riesz_lemma`.

Since we are considering a general nontrivially normed field, there may be a gap in possible norms
(for instance no element of norm in `(1,2)`). Hence, we can not allow `R` arbitrarily close to `1`,
and require `R > ‖c‖` for some `c : 𝕜` with norm `> 1`.

explanatories.Subspace: This definition identifies a subspace of a vector space as essentially equivalent to a submodule within that vector space structure.

riesz_lemma_of_norm_lt.description: This theorem states that for a closed proper subspace, one can find a vector with a norm up to a given bound that maintains a distance of at least one from every vector in the subspace, provided that this bound is strictly greater than the norm of a given element with a norm greater than one.

explanatories.Real.norm_eq_abs: Theorem establishes that the norm of a real number is equal to its absolute value.
explanatories.abs_inv: This theorem states that in a linear ordered field, the absolute value of the reciprocal of an element is equal to the reciprocal of the absolute value of that element.
explanatories.div_eq_inv_mul: The division of one element by another in a commutative division monoid is equal to the product of the first element and the inverse of the second element.
explanatories.div_lt_one: This theorem states that in a linear ordered semifield, an element divided by a positive element is less than one if and only if the original element is less than that positive element.
explanatories.abs_pos: This theorem establishes that the absolute value of an element in an additive group and linear order is positive if and only if the element itself is not zero.
explanatories.Iff.mpr: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.Real.sqrt_ne_zero': The square root of a real number is nonzero if and only if that number is positive.
explanatories.abs_norm: This theorem states that the absolute value of the norm of an element in a seminormed additive group is equal to the norm of that element.
explanatories.sq_lt_sq: The square of one element in a linearly ordered ring is less than the square of another element if and only if the absolute value of the first element is less than the absolute value of the second.
explanatories.Real.sq_sqrt: The square of the square root of a nonnegative real number is equal to the original number itself.
explanatories.LT.lt.le: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if one element is strictly less than a second, then it is also less than or equal to that second element.
explanatories.lt_one_add: This theorem demonstrates that any element in a partially ordered set is always less than one added to that element.
explanatories.trivial: The statement confirms that the proposition asserting truth is indeed valid and can be proven simply.
explanatories.smul_smul: This theorem shows that the action of the product of two elements from a monoid on another element is the same as performing the actions sequentially and is associative.
explanatories.zero_lt_one_add_norm_sq: This theorem asserts that in a seminormed group, the quantity one plus the square of the norm of any element is always positive.
explanatories.LT.lt.ne': A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if one element is strictly less than another, then the two elements cannot be equal.
explanatories.sq_abs: The square of the absolute value of an element in a linearly ordered ring is equal to the square of that element.
explanatories.Real.sqrt_div: The square root of a nonnegative real number divided by another real number equals the quotient of the square root of the first number and the square root of the second number.
explanatories.norm_nonneg: This theorem asserts that the norm of any element in a seminormed group is non-negative.
explanatories.Metric.isOpen_ball: The open ball around a point in a pseudo-metric space is an open set.
explanatories.Continuous.smul: The scalar multiplication of two continuous functions results in a continuous function.
explanatories.continuous_id: The identity function is continuous in any topological space.
explanatories.Continuous.continuousOn: If a function is continuous on its entire domain, it is also continuous on any subset of that domain.
explanatories.Continuous.inv₀: The inverse of a continuous function that never takes zero values is also continuous.
explanatories.ContinuousOn.smul: The scalar multiplication of two functions is continuous on a set if both functions are continuous on that set.
explanatories.ContinuousOn.inv₀: A function remains continuous on a specific set if it is continuous there and does not take the value zero anywhere in that set, allowing for the continuity of its inverse.
explanatories.continuousOn_const: A constant function is continuous on any given set.
explanatories.ContinuousOn.sub: The division of two continuous functions on a set in a topological space is also continuous on that set, provided the denominator is non-zero.
explanatories.continuous_norm: This theorem establishes that the mapping which assigns each element in a seminormed group to its norm is continuous.
explanatories.ContinuousOn.pow: If a function is continuous on a set, then raising its values to a natural number power will also be continuous on that set.
explanatories.ContinuousOn.sqrt: The square root of a continuous function defined on a set remains continuous on that set.
explanatories.continuousOn_id: The identity function is continuous on any given set within a topological space.
explanatories.Homeomorph.Set.univ: This definition states that the universal set of a topological space is homeomorphic to the space itself.
explanatories.PartialEquiv.source: This defines the domain of a partial equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.PartialEquiv.target: This represents the codomain in a partial equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.continuousOn: This theorem demonstrates that the function associated with a partial homeomorphism is continuous on its designated source set.

PartialHomeomorph.univUnitBall.fullDefinition: def PartialHomeomorph.univUnitBall : PartialHomeomorph E E where   toFun x := (√(1 + ‖x‖ ^ 2))⁻¹ • x   invFun y := (√(1 - ‖(y : E)‖ ^ 2))⁻¹ • (y : E)   source := univ   target := ball 0 1   map_source' x _ := by     have : 0 < 1 + ‖x‖ ^ 2 := by positivity     rw [mem_ball_zero_iff, norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_inv, ← _root_.div_eq_inv_mul,       div_lt_one (abs_pos.mpr <| Real.sqrt_ne_zero'.mpr this), ← abs_norm x, ← sq_lt_sq,       abs_norm, Real.sq_sqrt this.le]     exact lt_one_add _   map_target' _ _ := trivial   left_inv' x _ := by     field_simp [norm_smul, smul_smul, (zero_lt_one_add_norm_sq x).ne', sq_abs,       Real.sq_sqrt (zero_lt_one_add_norm_sq x).le, ← Real.sqrt_div (zero_lt_one_add_norm_sq x).le]   right_inv' y hy := by     have : 0 < 1 - ‖y‖ ^ 2 := by nlinarith [norm_nonneg y, mem_ball_zero_iff.1 hy]     field_simp [norm_smul, smul_smul, this.ne', sq_abs, Real.sq_sqrt this.le,       ← Real.sqrt_div this.le]   open_source := isOpen_univ   open_target := isOpen_ball   continuousOn_toFun := by     suffices Continuous fun (x : E) => (√(1 + ‖x‖ ^ 2))⁻¹      from (this.smul continuous_id).continuousOn     refine Continuous.inv₀ ?_ fun x => Real.sqrt_ne_zero'.mpr (by positivity)     continuity   continuousOn_invFun := by     have : ∀ y ∈ ball (0 : E) 1, √(1 - ‖(y : E)‖ ^ 2) ≠ 0 := fun y hy ↦ by       rw [Real.sqrt_ne_zero']       nlinarith [norm_nonneg y, mem_ball_zero_iff.1 hy]     exact ContinuousOn.smul (ContinuousOn.inv₀       (continuousOn_const.sub (continuous_norm.continuousOn.pow _)).sqrt this) continuousOn_id

PartialHomeomorph.unitBallBall.comment:

PartialHomeomorph.unitBallBall.fullDefinition: def unitBallBall (c : P) (r : ℝ) (hr : 0 < r) : PartialHomeomorph E P :=   ((Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero r hr.ne').trans       (IsometryEquiv.vaddConst c).toHomeomorph).toPartialHomeomorphOfImageEq       (ball 0 1) isOpen_ball (ball c r) <| by     change (IsometryEquiv.vaddConst c) ∘ (r • ·) '' ball (0 : E) 1 = ball c r     rw [image_comp, image_smul, smul_unitBall hr.ne', IsometryEquiv.image_ball]     simp [abs_of_pos hr]
PartialHomeomorph.unitBallBall.description: This definition describes a partial homeomorphism that establishes a relationship between a unit ball in a normed space and a ball of a specified radius centered at a point in an affine space.

PartialHomeomorph.univBall.code:
PartialHomeomorph.univBall.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} [SeminormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] {P : Type u_2}
  [PseudoMetricSpace P] [NormedAddTorsor E P] (c : P) (r : ℝ) : PartialHomeomorph E P
PartialHomeomorph.univBall.comment:
If `r > 0`, then `PartialHomeomorph.univBall c r` is a smooth partial homeomorphism
with `source = Set.univ` and `target = Metric.ball c r`.
Otherwise, it is the translation by `c`.
Thus in all cases, it sends `0` to `c`, see `PartialHomeomorph.univBall_apply_zero`.

explanatories.IsometryEquiv.vaddConst: This definition describes an isometric equivalence between the tangent space of a seminormed additive commutative group and a point in a pseudo-metric space, based on vector addition or subtraction from that point.
explanatories.PartialHomeomorph.trans': This definition describes the composition of two partial homeomorphisms when the target of the first one matches the source of the second, resulting in a new partial homeomorphism that relates the first space to the third.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
explanatories.Homeomorph.toPartialHomeomorph: This definition describes how a homeomorphism translates into a partial homeomorphism that applies to the entire space.

PartialHomeomorph.univBall.fullDefinition: def univBall (c : P) (r : ℝ) : PartialHomeomorph E P :=   if h : 0 < r then univUnitBall.trans' (unitBallBall c r h) rfl   else (IsometryEquiv.vaddConst c).toHomeomorph.toPartialHomeomorph
PartialHomeomorph.univBall.description: This definition describes a local homeomorphism that, if the radius is positive, maps a pseudo-metric space's ball to a seminormed space, and in any case, translates the origin to a specified point.

PartialHomeomorph.univBall.eq_1.code:
PartialHomeomorph.univBall.eq_1.{u_1, u_2} {E : Type u_1} [SeminormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] {P : Type u_2}
  [PseudoMetricSpace P] [NormedAddTorsor E P] (c : P) (r : ℝ) :
  univBall c r =
    if h : 0 < r then univUnitBall.trans' (unitBallBall c r h) ⋯
    else (IsometryEquiv.vaddConst c).toHomeomorph.toPartialHomeomorph

  ∃ f, f x₀ = 1 ∧ ∀ x ∈ s, f x < 1
separate_convex_open_set.comment:
Given a set `s` which is a convex neighbourhood of `0` and a point `x₀` outside of it, there is
a continuous linear functional `f` separating `x₀` and `s`, in the sense that it sends `x₀` to 1 and
all of `s` to values strictly below `1`.

explanatories.Convex: This definition characterizes a set as convex if, for any two points within the set, the entire line segment connecting them remains within the set.

separate_convex_open_set.description: This theorem states that for a convex and open set containing the origin, if a point lies outside this set, there exists a continuous linear functional that maps the external point to one and all points in the set to values strictly less than one.

  (disj : Disjoint s t) : ∃ f u, (∀ a ∈ s, f a < u) ∧ ∀ b ∈ t, u ≤ f b
geometric_hahn_banach_open.comment:

ContinuousLinearMap.exist_extension_of_f.comment:
Corollary of the **Hahn-Banach theorem**: if `f : p → F` is a continuous linear map
from a submodule of a normed space `E` over `𝕜`, `𝕜 = ℝ` or `𝕜 = ℂ`,
with a finite dimensional range,
then `f` admits an extension to a continuous linear map `E → F`.

Note that contrary to the case `F = 𝕜`, see `exists_extension_norm_eq`,
we provide no estimates on the norm of the extension.

explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.comp: The composition of bounded linear maps results in another bounded linear map.
explanatories.FiniteDimensional: This definition characterizes vector spaces as finite-dimensional if they can be understood as finite modules over a division ring.
explanatories.LinearMap.range: This definition states that the range of a linear map between modules is a submodule of the codomain module.
explanatories.Submodule.subtypeL: The definition describes a continuous linear map from a submodule to its parent module, highlighting the submodule's structure within the larger module context.

ContinuousLinearMap.exist_extension_of_f.description: This theorem states that for a continuous linear map defined on a finite-dimensional submodule of a normed space, there exists an extension of this map to the whole space while remaining a continuous linear map.

coord_norm'.description: This theorem establishes that for a non-zero vector in a normed space, the norm of the product of the vector's coordinate with a scalar equals one.

the dual element arbitrarily when `x = 0`.
exists_dual_vector'.description: This theorem states that for any element in a normed space, including the zero element, it is possible to find a dual space element with unit norm that evaluates to the norm of the original element, ensuring a suitable dual element can always be chosen.

the dual element has norm at most `1` (this can not be improved for the trivial
vector space).
exists_dual_vector''.description: This theorem states that for any element in a normed space, it is possible to find a dual space element with a norm that does not exceed one, which evaluates to the norm of the original element, accommodating even the zero element.

IsCompactOperator.comment:
A compact operator between two topological vector spaces. This definition is usually
given as "there exists a neighborhood of zero whose image is contained in a compact set",
but we choose a definition which involves fewer existential quantifiers and replaces images
with preimages.

IsCompactOperator.description: This definition describes a compact operator between two topological vector spaces as a function whose preimage of a neighborhood around zero is contained within a compact set.

IsCompactOperator.restrict.comment:
If a compact operator preserves a closed submodule, its restriction to that submodule is
compact.

Note that, following mathlib's convention in linear algebra, `restrict` designates the restriction

normed. The continuity ensures boundedness on a ball of some radius `ε`. The nontriviality of the
norm is then used to rescale any element into an element of norm in `[ε/C, ε]`, whose image has a
controlled norm. The norm control for the original element follows by rescaling.

ContinuousLinearMap.seminorm.comment:
Operator seminorm on the space of continuous (semi)linear maps, as `Seminorm`.

We use this seminorm to define a `SeminormedGroup` structure on `E →SL[σ] F`,
but we have to override the projection `UniformSpace`
so that it is definitionally equal to the one coming from the topologies on `E` and `F`.

explanatories.Norm.norm: This definition describes a function that assigns a real-valued norm to each element of a given type equipped with a norm structure.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_zero: This theorem states that the norm of the zero continuous linear map is equal to zero.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_add_le: This theorem states that the operator norm of the sum of two continuous linear maps is less than or equal to the sum of their individual operator norms, reflecting the triangle inequality.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_smul_le: This theorem asserts that the operator norm of a scaled continuous linear map is bounded by the product of the absolute value of the scaling factor and the operator norm of the map itself.
explanatories.Seminorm.ofSMulLE: This defines an alternative way to construct a seminorm on a module over a normed field, requiring only that the seminorm maps zero to zero and satisfies an inequality for scalar multiplication.

ContinuousLinearMap.seminorm.fullDefinition: protected def seminorm : Seminorm 𝕜₂ (E →SL[σ₁₂] F) :=   .ofSMulLE norm opNorm_zero opNorm_add_le opNorm_smul_le
ContinuousLinearMap.seminorm.description: This definition introduces an operator seminorm on the space of continuous semi-linear maps between two seminormed spaces.

_private.«.lake».packages.mathlib.Mathli.description: This theorem establishes that the uniform structure on the space of continuous linear maps is defined as the infimum of the entourages consisting of pairs of maps that are close to each other within a specified radius.

explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.smul_apply: The scalar multiplication of a continuous linear map applied to an element yields the same result as scaling the image of that element under the continuous linear map.

ContinuousLinearMap.prodMapL.fullDefinition: def prodMapL : (M₁ →L[𝕜] M₂) × (M₃ →L[𝕜] M₄) →L[𝕜] M₁ × M₃ →L[𝕜] M₂ × M₄ :=   ContinuousLinearMap.copy     (have Φ₁ : (M₁ →L[𝕜] M₂) →L[𝕜] M₁ →L[𝕜] M₂ × M₄ :=       ContinuousLinearMap.compL 𝕜 M₁ M₂ (M₂ × M₄) (ContinuousLinearMap.inl 𝕜 M₂ M₄)     have Φ₂ : (M₃ →L[𝕜] M₄) →L[𝕜] M₃ →L[𝕜] M₂ × M₄ :=       ContinuousLinearMap.compL 𝕜 M₃ M₄ (M₂ × M₄) (ContinuousLinearMap.inr 𝕜 M₂ M₄)     have Φ₁' :=       (ContinuousLinearMap.compL 𝕜 (M₁ × M₃) M₁ (M₂ × M₄)).flip (ContinuousLinearMap.fst 𝕜 M₁ M₃)     have Φ₂' :=       (ContinuousLinearMap.compL 𝕜 (M₁ × M₃) M₃ (M₂ × M₄)).flip (ContinuousLinearMap.snd 𝕜 M₁ M₃)     have Ψ₁ : (M₁ →L[𝕜] M₂) × (M₃ →L[𝕜] M₄) →L[𝕜] M₁ →L[𝕜] M₂ :=       ContinuousLinearMap.fst 𝕜 (M₁ →L[𝕜] M₂) (M₃ →L[𝕜] M₄)     have Ψ₂ : (M₁ →L[𝕜] M₂) × (M₃ →L[𝕜] M₄) →L[𝕜] M₃ →L[𝕜] M₄ :=       ContinuousLinearMap.snd 𝕜 (M₁ →L[𝕜] M₂) (M₃ →L[𝕜] M₄)     Φ₁' ∘L Φ₁ ∘L Ψ₁ + Φ₂' ∘L Φ₂ ∘L Ψ₂)     (fun p : (M₁ →L[𝕜] M₂) × (M₃ →L[𝕜] M₄) => p.1.prodMap p.2) (by       apply funext       rintro ⟨φ, ψ⟩       refine ContinuousLinearMap.ext fun ⟨x₁, x₂⟩ => ?_       dsimp       simp)

Choose `C` such that `‖g‖ ≤ C` for all `g ∈ s`.     rcases isBounded_iff_forall_norm_le.1 hs with ⟨C, hC⟩     -- Then `‖g x‖ ≤ C * ‖x‖` for all `g ∈ s`, `x : E`, hence `‖f x‖ ≤ C * ‖x‖` for all `x`.     have : ∀ x, IsClosed { g : E' → F | ‖g x‖ ≤ C * ‖x‖ } := fun x =>       isClosed_Iic.preimage (@continuous_apply E' (fun _ => F) _ x).norm     refine ⟨C, fun x => (this x).closure_subset_iff.2 (image_subset_iff.2 fun g hg => ?_) hf⟩     exact g.le_of_opNorm_le (hC _ hg) _

ContinuousLinearMap.extend.fullDefinition: def extend : Fₗ →SL[σ₁₂] F :=   -- extension of `f` is continuous   have cont := (uniformContinuous_uniformly_extend h_e h_dense f.uniformContinuous).continuous   -- extension of `f` agrees with `f` on the domain of the embedding `e`   have eq := uniformly_extend_of_ind h_e h_dense f.uniformContinuous   { toFun := (h_e.denseInducing h_dense).extend f     map_add' := by       refine h_dense.induction_on₂ ?_ ?_       · exact isClosed_eq (cont.comp continuous_add)           ((cont.comp continuous_fst).add (cont.comp continuous_snd))       · intro x y         simp only [eq, ← e.map_add]         exact f.map_add _ _     map_smul' := fun k => by       refine fun b => h_dense.induction_on b ?_ ?_       · exact isClosed_eq (cont.comp (continuous_const_smul _))           ((continuous_const_smul _).comp cont)       · intro x         rw [← map_smul]         simp only [eq]         exact ContinuousLinearMap.map_smulₛₗ _ _ _     cont }

IsCoercive.code: IsCoercive.{u_4} {E : Type u_4} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] (B : E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ) : Prop
IsCoercive.comment:
A bounded bilinear form `B` in a real normed space is *coercive*
if there is some positive constant C such that `C * ‖u‖ * ‖u‖ ≤ B u u`.
IsCoercive.fullDefinition: def IsCoercive [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] (B : E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ) : Prop :=   ∃ C, 0 < C ∧ ∀ u, C * ‖u‖ * ‖u‖ ≤ B u u
IsCoercive.description: This definition characterizes a bounded bilinear form in a real normed space as coercive if it is bounded below by a positive constant multiplied by the square of the norm of its arguments.

NonUnitalAlgHom.Lmul.comment:
Multiplication on the left in a non-unital normed algebra `𝕜'` as a non-unital algebra
homomorphism into the algebra of *continuous* linear maps. This is the left regular representation
of `A` acting on itself.

This has more algebraic structure than `ContinuousLinearMap.mul`, but there is no longer continuity
bundled in the first coordinate.  An alternative viewpoint is that this upgrades
`NonUnitalAlgHom.lmul` from a homomorphism into linear maps to a homomorphism into *continuous*
linear maps.

explanatories.LinearMap.mul: This definition specifies a bilinear map corresponding to multiplication in a non-unital non-associative algebra, mapping pairs of elements back to the algebra itself.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.mul: This definition describes the multiplication operation in a non-unital normed algebra as a continuous bilinear map.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.ext: If two continuous linear maps between topological modules agree on their outputs for all inputs, then they are identical maps.
explanatories.MulZeroClass.zero_mul: This theorem establishes that multiplying any element by zero results in zero, demonstrating that zero acts as a left absorbing element in multiplication.
explanatories.mul_assoc: This theorem asserts that multiplication in a semigroup is associative, meaning the product of three elements is the same regardless of how they are grouped.
explanatories.Subtype.ext: This theorem states that two elements of a subtype are equal if their corresponding underlying elements are equal.

explanatories.RingHom.id: This definition describes the identity ring homomorphism that maps each element of a semiring to itself.

explanatories.Subtype.ext: This theorem states that two elements of a subtype are equal if their corresponding underlying elements are equal.

explanatories.RCLike.I: This defines an imaginary unit within a relational structure, which is set to zero when the structure corresponds to the real numbers.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_add: This theorem states that a linear map preserves the addition operation by ensuring that the image of the sum of two elements equals the sum of their images.
explanatories.RCLike.ofReal_add: This theorem establishes that the real number addition in a relational structure corresponds to the addition of their respective elements when mapped into that structure.
explanatories.mul_add: This theorem states that in a structure where multiplication is left distributive over addition, the product of an element and the sum of two other elements equals the sum of the products of the first element with each of the other two elements.
explanatories.RCLike.ofReal_mul: This theorem states that the mapping of the product of two real numbers in a relational structure is equal to the product of their corresponding relational structure representations.
explanatories.RCLike.ofReal_alg: This theorem establishes that a real number can be expressed as the product of that number and the identity element in the corresponding relational structure.
explanatories.smul_assoc: This theorem states that in a scalar tower structure involving multiple scalar multiplications, applying the scalars in succession produces the same result as applying the first scalar and then multiplying the outcome by the second scalar.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_smul: This theorem states that a linear map commutes with scalar multiplication, meaning that applying the map to the product of a scalar and a vector is the same as multiplying the image of the vector by the scalar.
explanatories.Algebra.id.smul_eq_mul: This theorem establishes that scalar multiplication by an element in a commutative semiring is equivalent to the usual multiplication of that element with another element from the same semiring.
explanatories.one_smul: This theorem establishes that multiplying any element by the identity element of a monoid does not change the element itself.
explanatories.smul_smul: This theorem shows that the action of the product of two elements from a monoid on another element is the same as performing the actions sequentially and is associative.
explanatories.mul_comm: This theorem states that multiplication is commutative in a certain algebraic structure, meaning that the product of two elements is the same regardless of their order.
explanatories.mul_sub: This theorem expresses the distributive property of multiplication over subtraction in a non-unital non-associative ring.
explanatories.RCLike.I_mul_I_ax: This theorem states that for a specific relational structure, either the imaginary unit is zero or its square equals negative one, highlighting the foundational properties of imaginary numbers.
explanatories.mul_assoc: This theorem asserts that multiplication in a semigroup is associative, meaning the product of three elements is the same regardless of how they are grouped.
explanatories.neg_mul: This theorem states that in an algebraic structure where multiplication and distributive negation are defined, the product of the negation of one element and another element is equal to the negation of their product.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_neg: This theorem establishes that a linear map preserves the negation operation, meaning applying the map to the negative of an element yields the negative of the image of that element.
explanatories.one_mul: This theorem asserts that multiplying any element by the identity element in a multiplicative structure results in the element itself.
explanatories.mul_neg: Multiplication of an element by the negation of another element results in the negation of the product of those two elements in an algebraic structure equipped with multiplication and distributive negation.
explanatories.RCLike.ofReal_neg: This theorem shows that the negation of a real number can be represented as the negation of its corresponding element in a relational structure.
explanatories.neg_smul: This theorem states that negating the scalar before multiplying by an element of a module is equivalent to negating the product of the scalar and the element.
explanatories.sub_neg_eq_add: In a structure with subtraction, subtracting the negative of an element is equivalent to adding that element to another.
explanatories.add_comm: This theorem asserts that the addition operation in a commutative magma is commutative, meaning the sum of two elements does not depend on the order in which they are added.
explanatories.RCLike.re_add_im: This theorem asserts that the sum of the real part and a scaled imaginary part of an element from a relational structure equals the element itself.
explanatories.add_smul: This theorem states that the operation of scalar multiplication distributes over the addition of scalars in a module.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.

LinearMap.extendTo𝕜'.fullDefinition: noncomputable def extendTo𝕜' (fr : F →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) : F →ₗ[𝕜] 𝕜 := by   let fc : F → 𝕜 := fun x => (fr x : 𝕜) - (I : 𝕜) * fr ((I : 𝕜) • x)   have add : ∀ x y : F, fc (x + y) = fc x + fc y := by     intro x y     simp only [fc, smul_add, LinearMap.map_add, ofReal_add]     rw [mul_add]     abel   have A : ∀ (c : ℝ) (x : F), (fr ((c : 𝕜) • x) : 𝕜) = (c : 𝕜) * (fr x : 𝕜) := by     intro c x     rw [← ofReal_mul]     congr 1     rw [RCLike.ofReal_alg, smul_assoc, fr.map_smul, Algebra.id.smul_eq_mul, one_smul]   have smul_ℝ : ∀ (c : ℝ) (x : F), fc ((c : 𝕜) • x) = (c : 𝕜) * fc x := by     intro c x     dsimp only [fc]     rw [A c x, smul_smul, mul_comm I (c : 𝕜), ← smul_smul, A, mul_sub]     ring   have smul_I : ∀ x : F, fc ((I : 𝕜) • x) = (I : 𝕜) * fc x := by     intro x     dsimp only [fc]     cases' @I_mul_I_ax 𝕜 _ with h h     · simp [h]     rw [mul_sub, ← mul_assoc, smul_smul, h]     simp only [neg_mul, LinearMap.map_neg, one_mul, one_smul, mul_neg, ofReal_neg, neg_smul,       sub_neg_eq_add, add_comm]   have smul_𝕜 : ∀ (c : 𝕜) (x : F), fc (c • x) = c • fc x := by     intro c x     rw [← re_add_im c, add_smul, add_smul, add, smul_ℝ, ← smul_smul, smul_ℝ, smul_I, ← mul_assoc]     rfl   exact     { toFun := fc       map_add' := add       map_smul' := smul_𝕜 }

explanatories.RCLike.I: This defines an imaginary unit within a relational structure, which is set to zero when the structure corresponds to the real numbers.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_add: This theorem states that a linear map preserves the addition operation by ensuring that the image of the sum of two elements equals the sum of their images.
explanatories.RCLike.ofReal_add: This theorem establishes that the real number addition in a relational structure corresponds to the addition of their respective elements when mapped into that structure.
explanatories.mul_add: This theorem states that in a structure where multiplication is left distributive over addition, the product of an element and the sum of two other elements equals the sum of the products of the first element with each of the other two elements.
explanatories.RCLike.ofReal_mul: This theorem states that the mapping of the product of two real numbers in a relational structure is equal to the product of their corresponding relational structure representations.
explanatories.RCLike.ofReal_alg: This theorem establishes that a real number can be expressed as the product of that number and the identity element in the corresponding relational structure.
explanatories.smul_assoc: This theorem states that in a scalar tower structure involving multiple scalar multiplications, applying the scalars in succession produces the same result as applying the first scalar and then multiplying the outcome by the second scalar.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_smul: This theorem states that a linear map commutes with scalar multiplication, meaning that applying the map to the product of a scalar and a vector is the same as multiplying the image of the vector by the scalar.
explanatories.Algebra.id.smul_eq_mul: This theorem establishes that scalar multiplication by an element in a commutative semiring is equivalent to the usual multiplication of that element with another element from the same semiring.
explanatories.one_smul: This theorem establishes that multiplying any element by the identity element of a monoid does not change the element itself.
explanatories.smul_smul: This theorem shows that the action of the product of two elements from a monoid on another element is the same as performing the actions sequentially and is associative.
explanatories.mul_comm: This theorem states that multiplication is commutative in a certain algebraic structure, meaning that the product of two elements is the same regardless of their order.
explanatories.mul_sub: This theorem expresses the distributive property of multiplication over subtraction in a non-unital non-associative ring.
explanatories.RCLike.I_mul_I_ax: This theorem states that for a specific relational structure, either the imaginary unit is zero or its square equals negative one, highlighting the foundational properties of imaginary numbers.
explanatories.mul_assoc: This theorem asserts that multiplication in a semigroup is associative, meaning the product of three elements is the same regardless of how they are grouped.
explanatories.neg_mul: This theorem states that in an algebraic structure where multiplication and distributive negation are defined, the product of the negation of one element and another element is equal to the negation of their product.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_neg: This theorem establishes that a linear map preserves the negation operation, meaning applying the map to the negative of an element yields the negative of the image of that element.
explanatories.one_mul: This theorem asserts that multiplying any element by the identity element in a multiplicative structure results in the element itself.
explanatories.mul_neg: Multiplication of an element by the negation of another element results in the negation of the product of those two elements in an algebraic structure equipped with multiplication and distributive negation.
explanatories.RCLike.ofReal_neg: This theorem shows that the negation of a real number can be represented as the negation of its corresponding element in a relational structure.
explanatories.neg_smul: This theorem states that negating the scalar before multiplying by an element of a module is equivalent to negating the product of the scalar and the element.
explanatories.sub_neg_eq_add: In a structure with subtraction, subtracting the negative of an element is equivalent to adding that element to another.
explanatories.add_comm: This theorem asserts that the addition operation in a commutative magma is commutative, meaning the sum of two elements does not depend on the order in which they are added.
explanatories.RCLike.re_add_im: This theorem asserts that the sum of the real part and a scaled imaginary part of an element from a relational structure equals the element itself.
explanatories.add_smul: This theorem states that the operation of scalar multiplication distributes over the addition of scalars in a module.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.

A linear isometry between finite dimensional spaces of equal dimension can be upgraded

explanatories.FiniteDimensional.finrank: The finite rank of a module is defined as a natural number representing its rank, which is considered to be zero when the module has infinite rank.
explanatories.LinearMap.linearEquivOfInjective: This definition establishes an isomorphism between two finite-dimensional vector spaces when there exists an injective linear map between them and they share the same dimension.
explanatories.LinearIsometry.injective: This theorem demonstrates that a linear isometry is an injective function, meaning it maps distinct elements in its domain to distinct elements in its codomain.
explanatories.LinearIsometry.norm_map': This theorem states that for a linear isometry, the norm of an element transformed by the isometry is equal to the norm of the original element.
explanatories.AntilipschitzWith.injective: If a function is Antilipschitz, then it is guaranteed to be injective, meaning that distinct inputs map to distinct outputs.

LinearIsometry.toLinearIsometryEquiv.description: A linear isometry between finite-dimensional vector spaces of the same dimension can be elevated to a linear isometry equivalence.

lipschitzExtensionConstant.comment:
Any `K`-Lipschitz map from a subset `s` of a metric space `α` to a finite-dimensional real
vector space `E'` can be extended to a Lipschitz map on the whole space `α`, with a slightly worse
constant `C * K` where `C` only depends on `E'`. We record a working value for this constant `C`
as `lipschitzExtensionConstant E'`.

explanatories.Asymptotics.IsEquivalent.symm: If two functions are asymptotically equivalent along a specified filter, then these functions are also asymptotically equivalent in the reverse order along that same filter.

lipschitzExtensionConstant.fullDefinition: irreducible_def lipschitzExtensionConstant (E' : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup E'] [NormedSpace ℝ E']   [FiniteDimensional ℝ E'] : ℝ≥0 :=   let A := (Basis.ofVectorSpace ℝ E').equivFun.toContinuousLinearEquiv   max (‖A.symm.toContinuousLinearMap‖₊ * ‖A.toContinuousLinearMap‖₊) 1
lipschitzExtensionConstant.description: The Lipschitz extension constant represents a specific non-negative real number associated with extending a Lipschitz map from a subset of a metric space to the entire space while potentially increasing the Lipschitz constant.

  [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] [CompleteSpace 𝕜] (ι : Type u_1) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] : ((ι → 𝕜) →L[𝕜] E) ≃L[𝕜] ι → E
ContinuousLinearEquiv.piRing.comment:
Continuous linear equivalence between continuous linear functions `𝕜ⁿ → E` and `Eⁿ`.
The spaces `𝕜ⁿ` and `Eⁿ` are represented as `ι → 𝕜` and `ι → E`, respectively,
where `ι` is a finite type.

explanatories.LinearMap.comp: This definition states that the composition of two linear maps, each between different modules over semirings, results in another linear map that connects the first and last modules directly.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function, where the output of the second function becomes the input of the first.
explanatories.LinearMap.comp_apply: This theorem demonstrates that the composition of two linear maps applied to an element yields the same result as applying each map sequentially to that element.
explanatories.norm_smul: This theorem states that in a normed division ring acting on a seminormed additive group, the norm of the scalar multiplication of an element by a scalar is equal to the product of the norms of the scalar and the element.
explanatories.mul_comm: This theorem states that multiplication is commutative in a certain algebraic structure, meaning that the product of two elements is the same regardless of their order.
explanatories.norm_le_pi_norm: The theorem establishes that the norm of an individual component of a family of seminormed groups is less than or equal to the norm of the entire function mapping over that family.
explanatories.continuous_pi: This theorem establishes that if a family of functions from a topological space to another type is continuous for each index, then the overall function defined by these family members is also continuous.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.apply: This definition describes a continuous semilinear map that applies a given continuous semilinear map to a specified vector, resulting in another continuous linear map.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.continuous: A continuous linear map between two topological modules maintains continuity in its associated function.
explanatories.Fintype.card: This definition establishes that for a type that has a finite enumeration, the cardinality or number of elements in that type is a natural number.
explanatories.smul_mul_assoc: This theorem states that when a scalar multiplication and multiplication structure satisfy a certain scalar tower condition, scaling one factor in a product does not affect the result of the product itself.
explanatories.LE.le.trans: A theorem establishing that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second and that second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.
explanatories.DecidableEq: A type is said to have decidable equality if it is possible to determine whether any two elements of that type are equal.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.trans: This definition establishes that if there are two linear equivalences between three modules with corresponding ring homomorphisms, then there exists a direct linear equivalence between the first and last modules.
explanatories.Pi.single: This definition describes a way to create a function that assigns a specific value to one index while defaulting to zero for all other indices in the collection.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.invFun_eq_symm: This theorem asserts that the inverse function of a linear equivalence is equal to the application of the equivalence's symmetric function.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.trans_symm: This theorem demonstrates that the inverse of the composition of two linear equivalences is equal to the composition of their inverses in the reverse order.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.symm_symm: This theorem asserts that taking the inverse of the inverse of a linear equivalence yields the original linear equivalence itself.
explanatories.AddMonoidHomClass.continuous_of_bound: A homomorphism between seminormed groups is continuous if there exists a constant such that the norm of the image of any element is bounded by that constant multiplied by the norm of the original element.
explanatories.nsmul_eq_mul: This theorem establishes that the scalar multiplication of a natural number with an element of a non-associative semiring is equivalent to the multiplication of that natural number cast into the semiring with the element.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound: This theorem shows that if the norm of a continuous linear map is bounded by a constant when applied to any input, then the operator norm of that map is also bounded by the same constant.
explanatories.nsmul_nonneg: This theorem asserts that if an element is non-negative in an additive monoid, then multiplying that element by any non-negative integer also yields a non-negative result.
explanatories.norm_nonneg: This theorem asserts that the norm of any element in a seminormed group is non-negative.
explanatories.LinearMap.coe_comp: This theorem demonstrates that the function corresponding to the composition of two linear maps is equivalent to the composition of their respective functions.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.coe_toLinearMap: This theorem demonstrates that the natural transformation from a linear equivalence to its associated linear map is equal to the linear equivalence itself when viewed as a function.
explanatories.Function.comp_apply: The composition of two functions applied to an argument is equal to applying the first function to the result of applying the second function to that argument.
explanatories.LinearMap.coe_toContinuousLinearMap': This theorem establishes that the evaluation of a linear map in a finite-dimensional topological vector space coincides with the evaluation of its associated continuous linear map.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.piRing_symm_apply: This theorem provides a formula for expressing the action of a linear equivalence's inverse on a function as a sum of products involving the components of the function and a given scalar function.
explanatories.le_trans: This theorem asserts that in a preorder, if one element is less than or equal to a second, and the second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.
explanatories.norm_sum_le: This theorem establishes that the seminorm of the sum of elements over a finite set is less than or equal to the sum of the seminorms of the individual elements.
explanatories.Finset.sum_le_card_nsmul: This theorem establishes that the sum of a function evaluated at elements of a finite set does not exceed the product of the number of elements in the set and a constant bound applicable to each function value.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearEquiv.trans: The composition of two continuous linear equivalences results in another continuous linear equivalence between the first and last spaces.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearEquiv.continuous: A continuous linear equivalence between two modules implies that the corresponding function is continuous.
explanatories.Asymptotics.IsEquivalent.symm: If two functions are asymptotically equivalent along a specified filter, then these functions are also asymptotically equivalent in the reverse order along that same filter.

ContinuousLinearEquiv.piRing.fullDefinition: def ContinuousLinearEquiv.piRing (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :     ((ι → 𝕜) →L[𝕜] E) ≃L[𝕜] ι → E :=   { LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap.symm.trans (LinearEquiv.piRing 𝕜 E ι 𝕜) with     continuous_toFun := by       refine continuous_pi fun i => ?_       exact (ContinuousLinearMap.apply 𝕜 E (Pi.single i 1)).continuous     continuous_invFun := by       simp_rw [LinearEquiv.invFun_eq_symm, LinearEquiv.trans_symm, LinearEquiv.symm_symm]       -- Note: added explicit type and removed `change` that tried to achieve the same       refine AddMonoidHomClass.continuous_of_bound         (LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap.toLinearMap.comp             (LinearEquiv.piRing 𝕜 E ι 𝕜).symm.toLinearMap)         (Fintype.card ι : ℝ) fun g => ?_       rw [← nsmul_eq_mul]       refine opNorm_le_bound _ (nsmul_nonneg (norm_nonneg g) (Fintype.card ι)) fun t => ?_       simp_rw [LinearMap.coe_comp, LinearEquiv.coe_toLinearMap, Function.comp_apply,         LinearMap.coe_toContinuousLinearMap', LinearEquiv.piRing_symm_apply]       apply le_trans (norm_sum_le _ _)       rw [smul_mul_assoc]       refine Finset.sum_le_card_nsmul _ _ _ fun i _ => ?_       rw [norm_smul, mul_comm]       gcongr <;> apply norm_le_pi_norm }
ContinuousLinearEquiv.piRing.description: There is a continuous linear equivalence between the space of continuous linear functions from a finite-dimensional space to another space, and the product of the finite-dimensional spaces themselves.

continuousOn_clm_apply.code:
continuousOn_clm_apply.{u, v, w, u_1} {𝕜 : Type u} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] {E : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] {F : Type w} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F] [CompleteSpace 𝕜] {X : Type u_1}

  [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {f : α → E} : (Summable fun x => ‖f x‖) ↔ Summable f
summable_norm_iff.comment:
In a finite dimensional vector space over `ℝ`, the series `∑ x, ‖f x‖` is unconditionally
summable if and only if the series `∑ x, f x` is unconditionally summable. One implication holds in
any complete normed space, while the other holds only in finite dimensional spaces.

ContinuousLinearMap.exists_approx_preima.comment:
First step of the proof of the Banach open mapping theorem (using completeness of `F`):
by Baire's theorem, there exists a ball in `E` whose image closure has nonempty interior.
Rescaling everything, it follows that any `y ∈ F` is arbitrarily well approached by
images of elements of norm at most `C * ‖y‖`.
For further use, we will only need such an element whose image
is within distance `‖y‖/2` of `y`, to apply an iterative process.

ContinuousLinearMap.nonlinearRightInvers.comment:
A surjective continuous linear map between Banach spaces admits a (possibly nonlinear)
controlled right inverse. In general, it is not possible to ensure that such a right inverse
is linear (take for instance the map from `E` to `E/F` where `F` is a closed subspace of `E`
without a closed complement. Then it doesn't have a continuous linear right inverse.)

explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.range_coprod: The range of the coproduct of two continuous linear maps is equal to the join of their individual ranges.
explanatories.IsCompl.sup_eq_top: If two elements in a lattice are complementary, then their supremum is equal to the top element of the lattice.

ContinuousLinearMap.coprodSubtypeLEquivO.fullDefinition: noncomputable def coprodSubtypeLEquivOfIsCompl {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F]     [CompleteSpace F] (f : E →L[𝕜] F) {G : Submodule 𝕜 F}     (h : IsCompl (LinearMap.range f) G) [CompleteSpace G] (hker : ker f = ⊥) : (E × G) ≃L[𝕜] F :=   ContinuousLinearEquiv.ofBijective (f.coprod G.subtypeL)     (by       rw [ker_coprod_of_disjoint_range]       · rw [hker, Submodule.ker_subtypeL, Submodule.prod_bot]       · rw [Submodule.range_subtypeL]         exact h.disjoint)     (by simp only [range_coprod, Submodule.range_subtypeL, h.sup_eq_top]) set_option linter.uppercaseLean3 false in
ContinuousLinearMap.coprodSubtypeLEquivO.description: This definition establishes an equivalence between a direct sum of two spaces and the codomain of a continuous linear map under specific conditions related to the range and kernel of the map.

banach_steinhaus.comment:
This is the standard Banach-Steinhaus theorem, or Uniform Boundedness Principle.
If a family of continuous linear maps from a Banach space into a normed space is pointwise
bounded, then the norms of these linear maps are uniformly bounded.

See also `WithSeminorms.banach_steinhaus` for the general statement in barrelled spaces.

explanatories.WithSeminorms.banach_steinhaus: In a barrelled space, the Banach-Steinhaus theorem establishes uniform equicontinuity for a family of continuous linear maps when the maps exhibit uniform boundedness defined by a family of seminorms.

banach_steinhaus.description: This theorem asserts that if a family of continuous linear operators from a Banach space to a normed space is pointwise bounded, then there exists a uniform bound for the norms of these operators.

explanatories.AffineMap.decomp: This theorem shows that any affine map can be decomposed into the sum of its linear part and a constant function that maps every point to the value of the affine map at the origin.
explanatories.Pi.add_apply: This theorem examines the behavior of function composition involving a constant function that returns the "one" value.
explanatories.ContinuousAffineMap.decomp: The theorem asserts that any continuous affine map can be decomposed into the sum of its continuous linear part and a constant function evaluated at a specific point.
explanatories.ContinuousAffineMap.coe_add: The sum of two continuous affine maps is shown to be equal to the sum of their respective function representations.
explanatories.ContinuousAffineMap.coe_const: The continuous affine map that assigns a constant value to every point in an affine space is equivalent to the constant function mapping that same value across the space.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.coe_toContinuousAffi: The coercion of a continuous linear map viewed as a continuous affine map is equal to the original linear map's function representation.

continuous_affine_map.to_const_prod_cont.fullDefinition: def toConstProdContinuousLinearMap : (V →ᴬ[𝕜] W) ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] W × (V →L[𝕜] W) where   toFun f := ⟨f 0, f.contLinear⟩   invFun p := p.2.toContinuousAffineMap + const 𝕜 V p.1   left_inv f := by     ext     rw [f.decomp]     simp only [coe_add, ContinuousLinearMap.coe_toContinuousAffineMap, Pi.add_apply, coe_const]   right_inv := by rintro ⟨v, f⟩; ext <;> simp   map_add' _ _ := rfl   map_smul' _ _ := rfl   norm_map' f := rfl
continuous_affine_map.to_const_prod_cont.description: The definition states that the space of continuous affine maps between two normed spaces is linearly isometric to the product of the codomain and the space of linear maps, by associating an affine map's value at zero with its linear part.

MultilinearMap.bound_of_shell_of_norm_map_coord_zero.{u, v, wE, wG} {𝕜 : Type u} {ι : Type v} {E : ι → Type wE}
  {G : Type wG} [Fintype ι] [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [(i : ι) → SeminormedAddCommGroup (E i)]
  [(i : ι) → NormedSpace 𝕜 (E i)] [SeminormedAddCommGroup G] [NormedSpace 𝕜 G] (f : MultilinearMap 𝕜 E G)
  (hf₀ : ∀ {m : (i : ι) → E i} {i : ι}, ‖m i‖ = 0 → ‖f m‖ = 0) {ε : ι → ℝ} {C : ℝ} (hε : ∀ (i : ι), 0 < ε i) {c : ι → 𝕜}
  (hc : ∀ (i : ι), 1 < ‖c i‖)
  (hf : ∀ (m : (i : ι) → E i), (∀ (i : ι), ε i / ‖c i‖ ≤ ‖m i‖) → (∀ (i : ι), ‖m i‖ < ε i) → ‖f m‖ ≤ C * ∏ i : ι, ‖m i‖)
  (m : (i : ι) → E i) : ‖f m‖ ≤ C * ∏ i : ι, ‖m i‖
MultilinearMap.bound_of_shell_of_norm_ma.description: This theorem establishes a bound on the output of a multilinear map in terms of a product of norms of the input vectors, given certain conditions on the inputs and the map.

MultilinearMap.norm_map_coord_zero.comment:
If `f` is a continuous multilinear map in finitely many variables on `E` and `m` is an element
of `∀ i, E i` such that one of the `m i` has norm `0`, then `f m` has norm `0`.

Note that we cannot drop the continuity assumption because `f (m : Unit → E) = f (m ())`,
where the domain has zero norm and the codomain has a nonzero norm
does not satisfy this condition.
MultilinearMap.norm_map_coord_zero.description: This theorem states that if a multilinear map is continuous and at least one of its input components has zero norm, then the output of the map is also zero.

MultilinearMap.bound_of_shell_of_continu.comment:
If a continuous multilinear map in finitely many variables on normed spaces satisfies
the inequality `‖f m‖ ≤ C * ∏ i, ‖m i‖` on a shell `ε i / ‖c i‖ < ‖m i‖ < ε i` for some positive
numbers `ε i` and elements `c i : 𝕜`, `1 < ‖c i‖`, then it satisfies this inequality for all `m`.
MultilinearMap.bound_of_shell_of_continu.description: This theorem demonstrates that if a continuous multilinear map obeys a specific bounding condition within a certain region defined by inequalities involving input norms, it will satisfy the same bounding condition for all inputs.

  [SeminormedAddCommGroup G] [NormedSpace 𝕜 G] (f : MultilinearMap 𝕜 E G) (hf : Continuous ⇑f) :

MultilinearMap.exists_bound_of_continuou.comment:
If a multilinear map in finitely many variables on normed spaces is continuous, then it
satisfies the inequality `‖f m‖ ≤ C * ∏ i, ‖m i‖`, for some `C` which can be chosen to be
positive.
MultilinearMap.exists_bound_of_continuou.description: This theorem asserts that a continuous multilinear map from normed spaces can be bounded by the product of the norms of its inputs multiplied by a positive constant.

MultilinearMap.norm_image_sub_le_of_boun.code:
MultilinearMap.norm_image_sub_le_of_bound'.{u, v, wE, wG} {𝕜 : Type u} {ι : Type v} {E : ι → Type wE} {G : Type wG}
  [Fintype ι] [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [(i : ι) → SeminormedAddCommGroup (E i)] [(i : ι) → NormedSpace 𝕜 (E i)]
  [SeminormedAddCommGroup G] [NormedSpace 𝕜 G] (f : MultilinearMap 𝕜 E G) [DecidableEq ι] {C : ℝ} (hC : 0 ≤ C)
  (H : ∀ (m : (i : ι) → E i), ‖f m‖ ≤ C * ∏ i : ι, ‖m i‖) (m₁ m₂ : (i : ι) → E i) :
  ‖f m₁ - f m₂‖ ≤ C * ∑ i : ι, ∏ j : ι, if j = i then ‖m₁ i - m₂ i‖ else max ‖m₁ j‖ ‖m₂ j‖
MultilinearMap.norm_image_sub_le_of_boun.comment:
If `f` satisfies a boundedness property around `0`, one can deduce a bound on `f m₁ - f m₂`
using the multilinearity. Here, we give a precise but hard to use version. See
`norm_image_sub_le_of_bound` for a less precise but more usable version. The bound reads
`‖f m - f m'‖ ≤
  C * ‖m 1 - m' 1‖ * max ‖m 2‖ ‖m' 2‖ * max ‖m 3‖ ‖m' 3‖ * ... * max ‖m n‖ ‖m' n‖ + ...`,
where the other terms in the sum are the same products where `1` is replaced by any `i`.

explanatories.DecidableEq: A type is said to have decidable equality if it is possible to determine whether any two elements of that type are equal.
explanatories.Max.max: A function computes the maximum of two elements from a specified type.

MultilinearMap.norm_image_sub_le_of_boun.description: This theorem provides a bound on the difference of the outputs of a multilinear map at two points based on their inputs' differences and an upper bound on the outputs, where this relationship incorporates a specified constant and sums over the indices of the inputs.

MultilinearMap.norm_image_sub_le_of_bound.{u, v, wE, wG} {𝕜 : Type u} {ι : Type v} {E : ι → Type wE} {G : Type wG}
  [Fintype ι] [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [(i : ι) → SeminormedAddCommGroup (E i)] [(i : ι) → NormedSpace 𝕜 (E i)]
  [SeminormedAddCommGroup G] [NormedSpace 𝕜 G] (f : MultilinearMap 𝕜 E G) {C : ℝ} (hC : 0 ≤ C)
  (H : ∀ (m : (i : ι) → E i), ‖f m‖ ≤ C * ∏ i : ι, ‖m i‖) (m₁ m₂ : (i : ι) → E i) :
  ‖f m₁ - f m₂‖ ≤ C * ↑(Fintype.card ι) * max ‖m₁‖ ‖m₂‖ ^ (Fintype.card ι - 1) * ‖m₁ - m₂‖

`norm_image_sub_le_of_bound'` for a more precise but less usable version. The bound is
`‖f m - f m'‖ ≤ C * card ι * ‖m - m'‖ * (max ‖m‖ ‖m'‖) ^ (card ι - 1)`.

Operator seminorm on the space of continuous multilinear maps, as `Seminorm`.

We use this seminorm
to define a `SeminormedAddCommGroup` structure on `ContinuousMultilinearMap 𝕜 E G`,
