  [PseudoEMetricSpace α] [PseudoEMetricSpace β] : PseudoEMetricSpace (WithLp p (α × β))
WithLp.prodPseudoEMetricAux.comment:
Endowing the space `WithLp p (α × β)` with the `L^p` pseudoemetric structure. This definition is
not satisfactory, as it does not register the fact that the topology and the uniform structure
coincide with the product one. Therefore, we do not register it as an instance. Using this as a
temporary pseudoemetric space instance, we will show that the uniform structure is equal (but not
defeq) to the product one, and then register an instance in which we replace the uniform structure
by the product one using this pseudoemetric space and `PseudoEMetricSpace.replaceUniformity`.

explanatories.PseudoEMetricSpace.edist_triangle: The triangle inequality for the distance function in a pseudo-metric space asserts that the distance from one point to another is less than or equal to the sum of the distances between the first point to a third point and the second point to that third point.

WithLp.prodPseudoEMetricAux.fullDefinition: def prodPseudoEMetricAux [PseudoEMetricSpace α] [PseudoEMetricSpace β] :     PseudoEMetricSpace (WithLp p (α × β)) where   edist_self := prod_edist_self p   edist_comm := prod_edist_comm p   edist_triangle f g h := by     rcases p.dichotomy with (rfl | hp)     · simp only [prod_edist_eq_sup]       exact sup_le ((edist_triangle _ g.fst _).trans <| add_le_add le_sup_left le_sup_left)         ((edist_triangle _ g.snd _).trans <| add_le_add le_sup_right le_sup_right)     · simp only [prod_edist_eq_add (zero_lt_one.trans_le hp)]       calc         (edist f.fst h.fst ^ p.toReal + edist f.snd h.snd ^ p.toReal) ^ (1 / p.toReal) ≤             ((edist f.fst g.fst + edist g.fst h.fst) ^ p.toReal +               (edist f.snd g.snd + edist g.snd h.snd) ^ p.toReal) ^ (1 / p.toReal) := by           gcongr <;> apply edist_triangle         _ ≤             (edist f.fst g.fst ^ p.toReal + edist f.snd g.snd ^ p.toReal) ^ (1 / p.toReal) +               (edist g.fst h.fst ^ p.toReal + edist g.snd h.snd ^ p.toReal) ^ (1 / p.toReal) := by           have := ENNReal.Lp_add_le {0, 1}             (if · = 0 then edist f.fst g.fst else edist f.snd g.snd)             (if · = 0 then edist g.fst h.fst else edist g.snd h.snd) hp           simp only [Finset.mem_singleton, not_false_eq_true, Finset.sum_insert,             Finset.sum_singleton] at this           exact this

`PseudoMetricSpace.replaceUniformity`, and `PseudoMetricSpace.replaceBornology`.

WithLp.prodPseudoMetricAux.fullDefinition: abbrev prodPseudoMetricAux [PseudoMetricSpace α] [PseudoMetricSpace β] :     PseudoMetricSpace (WithLp p (α × β)) :=   PseudoEMetricSpace.toPseudoMetricSpaceOfDist dist     (fun f g => by       rcases p.dichotomy with (rfl | h)       · exact prod_sup_edist_ne_top_aux f g       · rw [prod_edist_eq_add (zero_lt_one.trans_le h)]         refine ENNReal.rpow_ne_top_of_nonneg (by positivity) (ne_of_lt ?_)         simp [ENNReal.add_lt_top, ENNReal.rpow_lt_top_of_nonneg, edist_ne_top] )     fun f g => by     rcases p.dichotomy with (rfl | h)     · rw [prod_edist_eq_sup, prod_dist_eq_sup]       refine le_antisymm (sup_le ?_ ?_) ?_       · rw [← ENNReal.ofReal_le_iff_le_toReal (prod_sup_edist_ne_top_aux f g),           ← PseudoMetricSpace.edist_dist]         exact le_sup_left       · rw [← ENNReal.ofReal_le_iff_le_toReal (prod_sup_edist_ne_top_aux f g),           ← PseudoMetricSpace.edist_dist]         exact le_sup_right       · refine ENNReal.toReal_le_of_le_ofReal ?_ ?_         · simp only [ge_iff_le, le_sup_iff, dist_nonneg, or_self]         · simp [edist, PseudoMetricSpace.edist_dist, ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal]     · have h1 : edist f.fst g.fst ^ p.toReal ≠ ⊤ :=         ENNReal.rpow_ne_top_of_nonneg (zero_le_one.trans h) (edist_ne_top _ _)       have h2 : edist f.snd g.snd ^ p.toReal ≠ ⊤ :=         ENNReal.rpow_ne_top_of_nonneg (zero_le_one.trans h) (edist_ne_top _ _)       simp only [prod_edist_eq_add (zero_lt_one.trans_le h), dist_edist, ENNReal.toReal_rpow,         prod_dist_eq_add (zero_lt_one.trans_le h), ← ENNReal.toReal_add h1 h2]

explanatories.lp.norm_neg: This theorem demonstrates that the norm of a function in a specific space remains unchanged when the function is negated.
explanatories.AddGroupNorm.toNormedAddCommGroup: This definition constructs a normed group from a given group norm, incorporating the distance and metric space structure defined by the norm's properties.
explanatories.ENNReal.dichotomy: This theorem asserts that for an extended nonnegative real number that is greater than or equal to one, it is either equal to infinity or its standard real number representation is at least one.
explanatories.zero_add: This theorem establishes that adding zero to any element in an additive structure results in that same element.
explanatories.le_refl: This theorem confirms that in a preorder, any element is related to itself under the less than or equal relation.
explanatories.add_mem_upperBounds_add: If two elements are upper bounds of two sets in a preordered structure, then their sum is an upper bound of the sum of those sets.
explanatories.zero_lt_one: Zero is strictly less than one in any type that includes definitions for zero, one, and a partial order, provided that one is not equal to zero.
explanatories.LT.lt.trans_le: A theorem establishing that in a preordered structure, if one element is strictly less than a second and that second element is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also strictly less than the third.
explanatories.Real.Lp_add_le_hasSum_of_nonneg: The p-th power of the sum of two nonnegative functions has a defined sum that is less than or equal to the sum of their individual p-th powers, under specific conditions related to the existence of these sums.
explanatories.Real.rpow_le_rpow_iff: The theorem states that for non-negative real numbers, the inequality of their powers with a positive exponent is equivalent to the inequality of the numbers themselves.
explanatories.hasSum_le: If one series is less than or equal to another series term by term and both have well-defined sums, then the sum of the first series is less than or equal to the sum of the second series.
explanatories.Nonempty.intro: If there exists an element of a type, then that type is considered nonempty.
explanatories.NNReal.rpow_le_rpow_iff: The theorem states that for two nonnegative real numbers, raising them to a positive power results in a comparison where one is less than or equal to the other if and only if the bases are in the same order.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto.norm: This theorem asserts that if a function converges to a limit in a seminormed group, then the norm of that function also converges to the norm of the limit.
explanatories.Continuous.norm: This theorem establishes that the continuity of a function from a topological space to a seminormed group implies the continuity of the function that maps each input to the norm of its output.

lp.normedAddCommGroup.fullDefinition: instance normedAddCommGroup [hp : Fact (1 ≤ p)] : NormedAddCommGroup (lp E p) :=   AddGroupNorm.toNormedAddCommGroup     { toFun := norm       map_zero' := norm_zero       neg' := norm_neg       add_le' := fun f g => by         rcases p.dichotomy with (rfl | hp')         · cases isEmpty_or_nonempty α           · simp only [lp.eq_zero' f, zero_add, norm_zero, le_refl]           refine (lp.isLUB_norm (f + g)).2 ?_           rintro x ⟨i, rfl⟩           refine le_trans ?_ (add_mem_upperBounds_add             (lp.isLUB_norm f).1 (lp.isLUB_norm g).1 ⟨_, ⟨i, rfl⟩, _, ⟨i, rfl⟩, rfl⟩)           exact norm_add_le (f i) (g i)         · have hp'' : 0 < p.toReal := zero_lt_one.trans_le hp'           have hf₁ : ∀ i, 0 ≤ ‖f i‖ := fun i => norm_nonneg _           have hg₁ : ∀ i, 0 ≤ ‖g i‖ := fun i => norm_nonneg _           have hf₂ := lp.hasSum_norm hp'' f           have hg₂ := lp.hasSum_norm hp'' g           -- apply Minkowski's inequality           obtain ⟨C, hC₁, hC₂, hCfg⟩ :=             Real.Lp_add_le_hasSum_of_nonneg hp' hf₁ hg₁ (norm_nonneg' _) (norm_nonneg' _) hf₂ hg₂           refine le_trans ?_ hC₂           rw [← Real.rpow_le_rpow_iff (norm_nonneg' (f + g)) hC₁ hp'']           refine hasSum_le ?_ (lp.hasSum_norm hp'' (f + g)) hCfg           intro i           gcongr           apply norm_add_le       eq_zero_of_map_eq_zero' := fun f => norm_eq_zero_iff.1 }
lp.normedAddCommGroup.description: This definition establishes that a specific structure of a normed additive commutative group is defined for a space of functions given certain conditions on the parameters involved.

explanatories.lp.norm_apply_le_norm: This theorem demonstrates that the norm of an individual component of a function in a specific space does not exceed the overall norm of the function.

lp.nonUnitalNormedRing.fullDefinition: instance nonUnitalNormedRing : NonUnitalNormedRing (lp B ∞) :=   { lp.normedAddCommGroup, lp.nonUnitalRing with     norm_mul := fun f g =>       lp.norm_le_of_forall_le (mul_nonneg (norm_nonneg f) (norm_nonneg g)) fun i =>         calc           ‖(f * g) i‖ ≤ ‖f i‖ * ‖g i‖ := norm_mul_le _ _           _ ≤ ‖f‖ * ‖g‖ :=             mul_le_mul (lp.norm_apply_le_norm ENNReal.top_ne_zero f i)               (lp.norm_apply_le_norm ENNReal.top_ne_zero g i) (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _) }

explanatories.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.

explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.

explanatories.forall_exists_index: The ability to universally quantify over an existence statement implies that for every element satisfying a property, the subsequent property can also be universally quantified in relation to that element.
explanatories.Eq.ndrec: This defines a method to derive properties of a given type from a specific instance of equality, allowing transitions between equal values while preserving a specified motive.

explanatories.dite_eq_right_iff: This theorem shows that a decision-based expression equaling a constant value is equivalent to asserting that the condition implies the given function results in that constant value.
explanatories.Classical.not_forall: The equivalence between the negation of a universal statement and the existence of a counterexample is demonstrated by showing that not all elements satisfy the property if at least one element does not.

lp.single.fullDefinition: protected def single (p) (i : α) (a : E i) : lp E p :=   ⟨fun j => if h : j = i then Eq.ndrec a h.symm else 0, by     refine (memℓp_zero ?_).of_exponent_ge (zero_le p)     refine (Set.finite_singleton i).subset ?_     intro j     simp only [forall_exists_index, Set.mem_singleton_iff, Ne, dite_eq_right_iff,       Set.mem_setOf_eq, not_forall]     rintro rfl     simp⟩

`lp E p`, then it converges to `f` in the `lp E p` topology.

explanatories.Filter.Tendsto: A definition stating that a function converges from one filter to another if the preimage of every neighborhood in the second filter is a neighborhood in the first filter.
explanatories.CauchySeq: A Cauchy sequence is a function defined on a preorder that captures the notion of converging behavior in a uniform space.
explanatories.Filter.atTop: This definition introduces a filter that captures the behavior of elements approaching infinity in an ordered set, generated by all sets containing elements greater than or equal to any given element.

lp.tendsto_lp_of_tendsto_pi.description: This theorem establishes that if a sequence in a specific function space is Cauchy and converges pointwise to an element in that space, then it also converges to that element in the topology of the space.

LipschitzOnWith.coordinate.description: This theorem states that a function defined on a set is Lipschitz continuous with respect to a specified constant if and only if each of its coordinate functions is Lipschitz continuous on that set.

explanatories.LE.le.trans: A theorem establishing that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second and that second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.

WithLp.unitization_addEquiv_prod.fullDefinition: noncomputable def unitization_addEquiv_prod : WithLp 1 (Unitization 𝕜 A) ≃+ WithLp 1 (𝕜 × A) :=   (WithLp.linearEquiv 1 𝕜 (Unitization 𝕜 A)).toAddEquiv.trans <|     (addEquiv 𝕜 A).trans (WithLp.linearEquiv 1 𝕜 (𝕜 × A)).symm.toAddEquiv
WithLp.unitization_addEquiv_prod.description: This definition establishes an equivalence between the one-dimensional Lp space of the unitization of a non-unital normed ring and the one-dimensional Lp space of pairs formed from a normed field and that ring.

explanatories.uniformContinuous_iff: A function between uniform spaces is uniformly continuous if and only if the uniform structure of the codomain space is coarser than the structure induced by the function on the domain space.
explanatories.Iff.mpr: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.le_rfl: This theorem states that every element in a preorder is less than or equal to itself.
explanatories.uniformContinuous_comap': If a composition of two functions is uniformly continuous, then the function from the first space to the intermediate space is also uniformly continuous.
explanatories.uniformContinuous_id: The identity function is uniformly continuous on any uniform space.

WithLp.uniformEquiv_unitization_addEquiv.description: This definition establishes a uniform equivalence between the one-dimensional Lp space of the unitization of a non-unital normed ring and the one-dimensional Lp space of pairs formed from a normed field and that ring.

WithLp.unitization_norm_inr.description: This theorem asserts that the norm of an element from a non-unital normed ring, when converted back through the equivalence to the unitization's Lp space, is equal to the original norm of that element in the ring.

  ((expSeries ℝ ℍ (2 * n)) fun x => q) = ↑((-1) ^ n * ‖q‖ ^ (2 * n) / ↑(2 * n)!)
Quaternion.expSeries_even_of_imaginary.comment: The even terms of `expSeries` are real, and correspond to the series for $\cos ‖q‖$.

Quaternion.hasSum_expSeries_of_imaginary.code:
Quaternion.hasSum_expSeries_of_imaginary {q : ℍ} (hq : q.re = 0) {c s : ℝ}
  (hc : HasSum (fun n => (-1) ^ n * ‖q‖ ^ (2 * n) / ↑(2 * n)!) c)
  (hs : HasSum (fun n => (-1) ^ n * ‖q‖ ^ (2 * n + 1) / ↑(2 * n + 1)!) s) :
  HasSum (fun n => (expSeries ℝ ℍ n) fun x => q) (↑c + (s / ‖q‖) • q)
Quaternion.hasSum_expSeries_of_imaginary.comment:
Auxiliary result; if the power series corresponding to `Real.cos` and `Real.sin` evaluated
at `‖q‖` tend to `c` and `s`, then the exponential series tends to `c + (s / ‖q‖)`.

explanatories.HasSum: An infinite sum on a topological monoid is defined as the limit of sums over increasingly larger finite subsets, and this sum operation is robust against reordering of terms.

spectralRadius.code: spectralRadius.{u_1, u_2} (𝕜 : Type u_1) {A : Type u_2} [NormedField 𝕜] [Ring A] [Algebra 𝕜 A] (a : A) : ℝ≥0∞
spectralRadius.comment:
The *spectral radius* is the supremum of the `nnnorm` (`‖·‖₊`) of elements in the spectrum,
coerced into an element of `ℝ≥0∞`. Note that it is possible for `spectrum 𝕜 a = ∅`. In this
case, `spectralRadius a = 0`. It is also possible that `spectrum 𝕜 a` be unbounded (though
not for Banach algebras, see `spectrum.isBounded`, below).  In this case,
`spectralRadius a = ∞`.

explanatories.spectrum: The spectrum of an element in an algebra is the set of elements in a commutative ring for which subtracting that algebra element from the product of the element and the identity does not yield a unit.

spectralRadius.description: This definition describes the spectral radius as the supremum of the norms of elements in the spectrum of an algebra element, which can be either zero or infinity depending on the existence and boundedness of the spectrum.

NormedRing.algEquivComplexOfComplete.code:
NormedRing.algEquivComplexOfComplete.{u_2} {A : Type u_2} [NormedRing A] [NormedAlgebra ℂ A]
  (hA : ∀ {a : A}, IsUnit a ↔ a ≠ 0) [CompleteSpace A] : ℂ ≃ₐ[ℂ] A
NormedRing.algEquivComplexOfComplete.comment:
**Gelfand-Mazur theorem**: For a complex Banach division algebra, the natural `algebraMap ℂ A`
is an algebra isomorphism whose inverse is given by selecting the (unique) element of
`spectrum ℂ a`. In addition, `algebraMap_isometry` guarantees this map is an isometry.

Note: because `NormedDivisionRing` requires the field `norm_mul' : ∀ a b, ‖a * b‖ = ‖a‖ * ‖b‖`, we
don't use this type class and instead opt for a `NormedRing` in which the nonzero elements are
precisely the units. This allows for the application of this isomorphism in broader contexts, e.g.,
to the quotient of a complex Banach algebra by a maximal ideal. In the case when `A` is actually a
`NormedDivisionRing`, one may fill in the argument `hA` with the lemma `isUnit_iff_ne_zero`.

explanatories.Set.Nonempty.some: The function provides a way to extract an element from a non-empty set, relying on the axiom of choice.

explanatories.Iff.rfl: Any proposition is equivalent to itself.

NormedRing.algEquivComplexOfComplete.fullDefinition: noncomputable def _root_.NormedRing.algEquivComplexOfComplete [CompleteSpace A] : ℂ ≃ₐ[ℂ] A :=   let nt : Nontrivial A := ⟨⟨1, 0, hA.mp ⟨⟨1, 1, mul_one _, mul_one _⟩, rfl⟩⟩⟩   { Algebra.ofId ℂ A with     toFun := algebraMap ℂ A     invFun := fun a => (@spectrum.nonempty _ _ _ _ nt a).some     left_inv := fun z => by       simpa only [@scalar_eq _ _ _ _ _ nt _] using         (@spectrum.nonempty _ _ _ _ nt <| algebraMap ℂ A z).some_mem     right_inv := fun a => algebraMap_eq_of_mem (@hA) (@spectrum.nonempty _ _ _ _ nt a).some_mem }
NormedRing.algEquivComplexOfComplete.description: This definition establishes an isomorphism between a complete complex Banach algebra and the complex numbers, under the condition that nonzero elements are units, aligning with the Gelfand-Mazur theorem.

BoxIntegral.Box.subbox_induction_on'.code:
BoxIntegral.Box.subbox_induction_on'.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} {p : Box ι → Prop} (I : Box ι)
  (H_ind : ∀ J ≤ I, (∀ (s : Set ι), p (J.splitCenterBox s)) → p J)
  (H_nhds :
    ∀ z ∈ Box.Icc I,
      ∃ U ∈ 𝓝[Box.Icc I] z,
        ∀ J ≤ I,
          ∀ (m : ℕ),
            z ∈ Box.Icc J →
              Box.Icc J ⊆ U → (∀ (i : ι), J.upper i - J.lower i = (I.upper i - I.lower i) / 2 ^ m) → p J) :
  p I
BoxIntegral.Box.subbox_induction_on'.comment:
Let `p` be a predicate on `Box ι`, let `I` be a box. Suppose that the following two properties
hold true.

* `H_ind` : Consider a smaller box `J ≤ I`. The hyperplanes passing through the center of `J` split
  it into `2 ^ n` boxes. If `p` holds true on each of these boxes, then it true on `J`.

* `H_nhds` : For each `z` in the closed box `I.Icc` there exists a neighborhood `U` of `z` within
  `I.Icc` such that for every box `J ≤ I` such that `z ∈ J.Icc ⊆ U`, if `J` is homothetic to `I`
  with a coefficient of the form `1 / 2 ^ m`, then `p` is true on `J`.

Then `p I` is true. See also `BoxIntegral.Box.subbox_induction_on` for a version using
`BoxIntegral.Prepartition.splitCenter` instead of `BoxIntegral.Box.splitCenterBox`.

The proof still works if we assume `H_ind` only for subboxes `J ≤ I` that are homothetic to `I` with
a coefficient of the form `2⁻ᵐ` but we do not need this generalization yet.

BoxIntegral.Prepartition.partialOrder.fullDefinition: instance partialOrder : PartialOrder (Prepartition I) where   le := (· ≤ ·)   le_refl π I hI := ⟨I, hI, le_rfl⟩   le_trans π₁ π₂ π₃ h₁₂ h₂₃ I₁ hI₁ :=     let ⟨I₂, hI₂, hI₁₂⟩ := h₁₂ hI₁     let ⟨I₃, hI₃, hI₂₃⟩ := h₂₃ hI₂     ⟨I₃, hI₃, hI₁₂.trans hI₂₃⟩   le_antisymm := by     suffices ∀ {π₁ π₂ : Prepartition I}, π₁ ≤ π₂ → π₂ ≤ π₁ → π₁.boxes ⊆ π₂.boxes from       fun π₁ π₂ h₁ h₂ => injective_boxes (Subset.antisymm (this h₁ h₂) (this h₂ h₁))     intro π₁ π₂ h₁ h₂ J hJ     rcases h₁ hJ with ⟨J', hJ', hle⟩; rcases h₂ hJ' with ⟨J'', hJ'', hle'⟩     obtain rfl : J = J'' := π₁.eq_of_le hJ hJ'' (hle.trans hle')     obtain rfl : J' = J := le_antisymm ‹_› ‹_›     assumption

BoxIntegral.TaggedPrepartition.biUnionPr.code:

  (πi : (J : Box ι) → Prepartition J) : TaggedPrepartition I
BoxIntegral.TaggedPrepartition.biUnionPr.comment:
Given a tagged partition `π` of `I` and a (not tagged) partition `πi J hJ` of each `J ∈ π`,
returns the tagged partition of `I` into all the boxes of all `πi J hJ`. The tag of a box `J`
is defined to be the `π.tag` of the box of the partition `π` that includes `J`.

Note that usually the result is not a Henstock partition.

explanatories.BoxIntegral.Prepartition.biUnionIndex: This definition provides a way to retrieve a specific box from a prepartition based on whether it belongs to the union of boxes defined by another family of prepartitions, returning the original box if it does not belong.
explanatories.BoxIntegral.TaggedPrepartition.tag: The tagged function associated with each box in a tagged prepartition assigns a specific point in the box to every box in a total manner.
explanatories.BoxIntegral.TaggedPrepartition.tag_mem_I: The tag of each box in a tagged prepartition is contained within the interval defined by the larger box.
explanatories.BoxIntegral.Prepartition.IsPartition.biU: The union of a family of partitions derived from an initial prepartition is itself a partition if both the initial prepartition and each derived partition are valid partitions.

BoxIntegral.TaggedPrepartition.biUnionPr.description: A tagged partition of a larger box is created by combining it with a collection of ordinary partitions for each of its constituent boxes, while retaining the tags from the original partition.

BoxIntegral.TaggedPrepartition.IsSubordi.comment:
A tagged partition `π` is subordinate to `r : (ι → ℝ) → ℝ` if each box `J ∈ π` is included in
the closed ball with center `π.tag J` and radius `r (π.tag J)`.

explanatories.Metric.closedBall: The closed ball around a point in a pseudo-metric space consists of all points whose distance from that point is less than or equal to a specified radius.

BoxIntegral.TaggedPrepartition.IsSubordi.fullDefinition: def IsSubordinate [Fintype ι] (π : TaggedPrepartition I) (r : (ι → ℝ) → Ioi (0 : ℝ)) : Prop :=   ∀ J ∈ π, Box.Icc J ⊆ closedBall (π.tag J) (r <| π.tag J)

explanatories.Eq.trans: If one element is equal to a second, and that second is equal to a third, then the first element is also equal to the third, demonstrating the transitive property of equality.

BoxIntegral.TaggedPrepartition.embedBox.description: Every tagged prepartition of a smaller box can be considered as a tagged prepartition of a larger box if the smaller box is contained within the larger one.

BoxIntegral.Box.splitLower.comment:
Given a box `I` and `x ∈ (I.lower i, I.upper i)`, the hyperplane `{y : ι → ℝ | y i = x}` splits
`I` into two boxes. `BoxIntegral.Box.splitLower I i x` is the box `I ∩ {y | y i ≤ x}`
(if it is nonempty). As usual, we represent a box that may be empty as
`WithBot (BoxIntegral.Box ι)`.

explanatories.BoxIntegral.Box.mk': This definition creates a box from a pair of lower and upper corners, yielding either a valid box if all lower bounds are less than their corresponding upper bounds, or a null value otherwise, while also interpreting it as a set of functions that fall within the specified open intervals for each coordinate.

BoxIntegral.Prepartition.not_disjoint_im.comment:
Let `s : Finset (ι × ℝ)` be a set of hyperplanes `{x : ι → ℝ | x i = r}` in `ι → ℝ` encoded as
pairs `(i, r)`. Suppose that this set contains all faces of a box `J`. The hyperplanes of `s` split
a box `I` into subboxes. Let `Js` be one of them. If `J` and `Js` have nonempty intersection, then
`Js` is a subbox of `J`.

BoxIntegral.Prepartition.eventually_not_.comment:
Let `s` be a finite set of boxes in `ℝⁿ = ι → ℝ`. Then there exists a finite set `t₀` of
hyperplanes (namely, the set of all hyperfaces of boxes in `s`) such that for any `t ⊇ t₀`
and any box `I` in `ℝⁿ` the following holds. The hyperplanes from `t` split `I` into subboxes.
Let `J'` be one of them, and let `J` be one of the boxes in `s`. If these boxes have a nonempty
intersection, then `J' ≤ J`.

BoxIntegral.Box.subbox_induction_on.code:
BoxIntegral.Box.subbox_induction_on.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] {p : Box ι → Prop} (I : Box ι)
  (H_ind : ∀ J ≤ I, (∀ J' ∈ splitCenter J, p J') → p J)
  (H_nhds :
    ∀ z ∈ Box.Icc I,
      ∃ U ∈ 𝓝[Box.Icc I] z,
        ∀ J ≤ I,
          ∀ (m : ℕ),
            z ∈ Box.Icc J →
              Box.Icc J ⊆ U → (∀ (i : ι), J.upper i - J.lower i = (I.upper i - I.lower i) / 2 ^ m) → p J) :
  p I
BoxIntegral.Box.subbox_induction_on.comment:
Let `p` be a predicate on `Box ι`, let `I` be a box. Suppose that the following two properties
hold true.

* Consider a smaller box `J ≤ I`. The hyperplanes passing through the center of `J` split it into
  `2 ^ n` boxes. If `p` holds true on each of these boxes, then it true on `J`.
* For each `z` in the closed box `I.Icc` there exists a neighborhood `U` of `z` within `I.Icc` such
  that for every box `J ≤ I` such that `z ∈ J.Icc ⊆ U`, if `J` is homothetic to `I` with a
  coefficient of the form `1 / 2 ^ m`, then `p` is true on `J`.

Then `p I` is true. See also `BoxIntegral.Box.subbox_induction_on'` for a version using
`BoxIntegral.Box.splitCenterBox` instead of `BoxIntegral.Prepartition.splitCenter`.

BoxIntegral.Box.subbox_induction_on.description: If a predicate holds for all smaller boxes resulting from splitting a box and for any neighborhood around points within the original box, then it also holds for the original box itself.

BoxIntegral.Box.exists_taggedPartition_isHenstock_isSubordinate_homothetic.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] (I : Box ι)
  (r : (ι → ℝ) → ↑(Ioi 0)) :
  ∃ π,
    π.IsPartition ∧
      π.IsHenstock ∧
        π.IsSubordinate r ∧
          (∀ J ∈ π, ∃ m, ∀ (i : ι), J.upper i - J.lower i = (I.upper i - I.lower i) / 2 ^ m) ∧
            π.distortion = I.distortion
BoxIntegral.Box.exists_taggedPartition_i.comment:
Given a box `I` in `ℝⁿ` and a function `r : ℝⁿ → (0, ∞)`, there exists a tagged partition `π` of
`I` such that

* `π` is a Henstock partition;
* `π` is subordinate to `r`;
* each box in `π` is homothetic to `I` with coefficient of the form `1 / 2 ^ m`.

This lemma implies that the Henstock filter is nontrivial, hence the Henstock integral is
well-defined.

BoxIntegral.IntegrationParams.toFilterDi.code:
BoxIntegral.IntegrationParams.toFilterDistortion.{u_1} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] (l : IntegrationParams) (I : Box ι)
  (c : ℝ≥0) : Filter (TaggedPrepartition I)
BoxIntegral.IntegrationParams.toFilterDi.comment:
A set `s : Set (TaggedPrepartition I)` belongs to `l.toFilterDistortion I c` if there exists
a function `r : ℝⁿ → (0, ∞)` (or a constant `r` if `l.bRiemann = true`) such that `s` contains each
prepartition `π` such that `l.MemBaseSet I c r π`.

explanatories.Set.Ioi: This definition denotes the set of elements that are strictly greater than a specified element in a preorder structure, resulting in a left-open and right-infinite interval.

BoxIntegral.IntegrationParams.toFilterDi.fullDefinition: def toFilterDistortion (l : IntegrationParams) (I : Box ι) (c : ℝ≥0) :     Filter (TaggedPrepartition I) :=   ⨅ (r : (ι → ℝ) → Ioi (0 : ℝ)) (_ : l.RCond r), 𝓟 { π | l.MemBaseSet I c r π }
BoxIntegral.IntegrationParams.toFilterDi.description: This definition describes a filter of tagged prepartitions that contains those satisfying specific membership criteria based on a function or constant related to the integration parameters and a given box.

A function on `Box ι` is called box additive if for every box `J` and a partition `π` of `J`
we have `f J = ∑ Ji ∈ π.boxes, f Ji`.

explanatories.BoxIntegral.Prepartition.boxes: The collection of boxes associated with a given prepartition is represented as a finite set of boxes.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
explanatories.BoxIntegral.Box.splitLower: The operation takes a box and a point, and splits the box into a new box representing the portion below that point, if such a portion exists.
explanatories.BoxIntegral.Box.splitUpper: This definition describes an operation that splits a box into the portion above a specified point, yielding a new box that may be empty, depending on the conditions of the split.
explanatories.BoxIntegral.Prepartition.sum_split_boxes: The theorem states that the sum over a collection of boxes created by splitting a box at a given point is equal to the sum of function evaluations at the resulting lower and upper box sections.
explanatories.LE.le.trans: A theorem establishing that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second and that second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.
explanatories.Set.Ioo: This definition specifies the set of elements that lie strictly between two given elements in a preorder structure, creating a left-open and right-open interval.
explanatories.BoxIntegral.Box.lower: This defines a function that retrieves the lower coordinates of a box based on the specified indices.
explanatories.BoxIntegral.Box.upper: The upper function of a box retrieves the upper coordinates for its corners.
explanatories.Finset.induction_on: This theorem states that to prove a property for all finite sets, it is sufficient to demonstrate that the property holds for the empty set and that if it holds for any finite set, it also holds when adding an element to that set.
explanatories.BoxIntegral.Prepartition.splitMany_inser: The theorem states that partitioning a box with an additional point results in the intersection of the original partition and the partition created by splitting the box at that point.
explanatories.BoxIntegral.Prepartition.inf_split: This theorem asserts that the intersection of a prepartition with the split of a box at a specified coordinate and point is equal to the union of the splits of each sub-box in the prepartition at the same coordinate and point.
explanatories.BoxIntegral.Prepartition.sum_biUnion_box: The sum of a function over the union of boxes from a prepartition equals the sum of the function over each box in the prepartition and its corresponding sub-prepartitions.
explanatories.Finset.sum_congr: If two finite sets are equal and their corresponding functions yield the same values for all elements, then the sums of those function values over the sets are also equal.
explanatories.WithTop.coe_le_coe: This theorem shows that the comparison of two values in an optional type corresponds directly to the comparison of the original values in their inherent order.
explanatories.BoxIntegral.Prepartition.le_of_mem: Any box from a prepartition is contained within the larger box that defines the prepartition.
explanatories.BoxIntegral.Prepartition.split_of_not_me: The theorem asserts that if a specified point does not lie within the bounds of a box in a given dimension, then partitioning the box at that point results in a single box that encompasses the entire original box.
explanatories.BoxIntegral.Prepartition.top_boxes: The collection of top boxes in a prepartition consists solely of the entire box itself.
explanatories.Finset.sum_singleton: The sum of a function's values over a finite set containing a single element equals the function's value at that element.
explanatories.BoxIntegral.Prepartition.IsPartition.exi: The theorem states that for any partition of a box, there exists a finite set of hyperplanes such that the process of splitting the box at these hyperplanes forms a partition that is less than or equal to the original partition.
explanatories.inf_of_le_right: If one element is less than or equal to another, then their infimum equals the lesser element.
explanatories.BoxIntegral.Prepartition.inf_splitMany: The theorem states that the intersection of a prepartition of a box with the result of splitting many parts of that box is equivalent to the union of the splits from each part of the prepartition.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.

BoxIntegral.BoxAdditiveMap.ofMapSplitAdd.fullDefinition: def ofMapSplitAdd [Finite ι] (f : Box ι → M) (I₀ : WithTop (Box ι))     (hf : ∀ I : Box ι, ↑I ≤ I₀ → ∀ {i x}, x ∈ Ioo (I.lower i) (I.upper i) →       (I.splitLower i x).elim' 0 f + (I.splitUpper i x).elim' 0 f = f I) :     ι →ᵇᵃ[I₀] M := by   refine ⟨f, ?_⟩   replace hf : ∀ I : Box ι, ↑I ≤ I₀ → ∀ s, (∑ J ∈ (splitMany I s).boxes, f J) = f I := by     intro I hI s     induction' s using Finset.induction_on with a s _ ihs     · simp     rw [splitMany_insert, inf_split, ← ihs, biUnion_boxes, sum_biUnion_boxes]     refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun J' hJ' => ?_     by_cases h : a.2 ∈ Ioo (J'.lower a.1) (J'.upper a.1)     · rw [sum_split_boxes]       exact hf _ ((WithTop.coe_le_coe.2 <| le_of_mem _ hJ').trans hI) h     · rw [split_of_not_mem_Ioo h, top_boxes, Finset.sum_singleton]   intro I hI π hπ   have Hle : ∀ J ∈ π, ↑J ≤ I₀ := fun J hJ => (WithTop.coe_le_coe.2 <| π.le_of_mem hJ).trans hI   rcases hπ.exists_splitMany_le with ⟨s, hs⟩   rw [← hf _ hI, ← inf_of_le_right hs, inf_splitMany, biUnion_boxes, sum_biUnion_boxes]   exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun J hJ => (hf _ (Hle _ hJ) _).symm
BoxIntegral.BoxAdditiveMap.ofMapSplitAdd.description: This definition creates a box additive map from a function defined on boxes, asserting that if the function satisfies a specific additive condition on the partitions formed by splitting the box, then the function is globally box additive.

box_integral.box_additive_map.of_map_spl.code:
BoxIntegral.BoxAdditiveMap.ofMapSplitAdd.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [AddCommMonoid M] [Finite ι]
  (f : Box ι → M) (I₀ : WithTop (Box ι))
  (hf :
    ∀ (I : Box ι),
      ↑I ≤ I₀ →
        ∀ {i : ι} {x : ℝ},
          x ∈ Set.Ioo (I.lower i) (I.upper i) →
            Option.elim' 0 f (I.splitLower i x) + Option.elim' 0 f (I.splitUpper i x) = f I) :
  ι →ᵇᵃ[I₀] M
box_integral.box_additive_map.of_map_spl.comment:
If `f : Box ι → M` is box additive on partitions of the form `split I i x`, then it is box
additive.

  (i : Fin (n + 1)) (f : ℝ → Box (Fin n) → G) (fb : ↑(Set.Icc (I₀.lower i) (I₀.upper i)) → Fin n →ᵇᵃ[↑(I₀.face i)] G)
  (hf : ∀ (x : ℝ) (hx : x ∈ Set.Icc (I₀.lower i) (I₀.upper i)) (J : Box (Fin n)), f x J = (fb ⟨x, hx⟩) J) :
  Fin (n + 1) →ᵇᵃ[↑I₀] G
BoxIntegral.BoxAdditiveMap.upperSubLower.comment:
Given a box `I₀` in `ℝⁿ⁺¹`, `f x : Box (Fin n) → G` is a family of functions indexed by a real
`x` and for `x ∈ [I₀.lower i, I₀.upper i]`, `f x` is box-additive on subboxes of the `i`-th face of
`I₀`, then `fun J ↦ f (J.upper i) (J.face i) - f (J.lower i) (J.face i)` is box-additive on subboxes
of `I₀`.

`x` and for `x ∈ [I₀.lower i, I₀.upper i]`, `f x` is box-additive on subboxes of the `i`-th face of
`I₀`, then `fun J ↦ f (J.upper i) (J.face i) - f (J.lower i) (J.face i)` is box-additive on subboxes
of `I₀`.

box_integral.box_additive_map.upper_sub_.fullDefinition: def upperSubLower.{u} {G : Type u} [AddCommGroup G] (I₀ : Box (Fin (n + 1))) (i : Fin (n + 1))     (f : ℝ → Box (Fin n) → G) (fb : Icc (I₀.lower i) (I₀.upper i) → Fin n →ᵇᵃ[I₀.face i] G)     (hf : ∀ (x) (hx : x ∈ Icc (I₀.lower i) (I₀.upper i)) (J), f x J = fb ⟨x, hx⟩ J) :     Fin (n + 1) →ᵇᵃ[I₀] G :=   ofMapSplitAdd (fun J : Box (Fin (n + 1)) => f (J.upper i) (J.face i) - f (J.lower i) (J.face i))     I₀     (by       intro J hJ j x       rw [WithTop.coe_le_coe] at hJ       refine i.succAboveCases (fun hx => ?_) (fun j hx => ?_) j       · simp only [Box.splitLower_def hx, Box.splitUpper_def hx, update_same, ← WithBot.some_eq_coe,           Option.elim', Box.face, (· ∘ ·), update_noteq (Fin.succAbove_ne _ _)]         abel       · have : (J.face i : WithTop (Box (Fin n))) ≤ I₀.face i :=           WithTop.coe_le_coe.2 (face_mono hJ i)         rw [le_iff_Icc, @Box.Icc_eq_pi _ I₀] at hJ         simp only         rw [hf _ (hJ J.upper_mem_Icc _ trivial), hf _ (hJ J.lower_mem_Icc _ trivial),           ← (fb _).map_split_add this j x, ← (fb _).map_split_add this j x]         have hx' : x ∈ Ioo ((J.face i).lower j) ((J.face i).upper j) := hx         simp only [Box.splitLower_def hx, Box.splitUpper_def hx, Box.splitLower_def hx',           Box.splitUpper_def hx', ← WithBot.some_eq_coe, Option.elim', Box.face_mk,           update_noteq (Fin.succAbove_ne _ _).symm, sub_add_sub_comm,           update_comp_eq_of_injective _ (Fin.strictMono_succAbove i).injective j x, ← hf]         simp only [Box.face])

BoxIntegral.hasIntegral_iff.{u, v, w} {ι : Type u} {E : Type v} {F : Type w} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
  [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] {I : Box ι} [Fintype ι] {l : IntegrationParams} {f : (ι → ℝ) → E}
  {vol : ι →ᵇᵃ[⊤] E →L[ℝ] F} {y : F} :
  HasIntegral I l f vol y ↔
    ∀ ε > 0,
      ∃ r,
        (∀ (c : ℝ≥0), l.RCond (r c)) ∧
          ∀ (c : ℝ≥0) (π : TaggedPrepartition I),
            l.MemBaseSet I c (r c) π → π.IsPartition → dist (integralSum f vol π) y ≤ ε

BoxIntegral.Integrable.convergenceR.comment:
If `ε > 0`, then `BoxIntegral.Integrable.convergenceR` is a function `r : ℝ≥0 → ℝⁿ → (0, ∞)`
such that for every `c : ℝ≥0`, for every tagged partition `π` subordinate to `r` (and satisfying
additional distortion estimates if `BoxIntegral.IntegrationParams.bDistortion l = true`), the
corresponding integral sum is `ε`-close to the integral.

If `BoxIntegral.IntegrationParams.bRiemann = true`, then `r c x` does not depend on `x`. If
`ε ≤ 0`, then we use `r c x = 1`.

explanatories.BoxIntegral.hasIntegral_iff: This theorem provides a characterisation of having an integral by stating that it is equivalent to the existence of a condition involving partitions and the approximation of integral sums within any desired precision.
explanatories.BoxIntegral.Integrable.hasIntegral: The theorem states that if a function is integrable over a box with specified parameters and volume, then there exists a unique integral value corresponding to that function under the same conditions.
explanatories.Set.mem_Ioi: This theorem asserts that an element is part of the interval consisting of elements strictly greater than a given element in a preorder structure if and only if it is greater than that element.
explanatories.zero_lt_one: Zero is strictly less than one in any type that includes definitions for zero, one, and a partial order, provided that one is not equal to zero.

BoxIntegral.Integrable.convergenceR.fullDefinition: def convergenceR (h : Integrable I l f vol) (ε : ℝ) : ℝ≥0 → ℝⁿ → Ioi (0 : ℝ) :=   if hε : 0 < ε then (hasIntegral_iff.1 h.hasIntegral ε hε).choose   else fun _ _ => ⟨1, Set.mem_Ioi.2 zero_lt_one⟩
BoxIntegral.Integrable.convergenceR.description: This defines a function that, given an integrable function and a positive epsilon, provides a way to choose a tagged partition ensuring that the corresponding integral sum is as close as desired to the integral value under certain conditions.

BoxIntegral.Integrable.dist_integralSum_.comment:
**Henstock-Sacks inequality**. Let `r₁ r₂ : ℝⁿ → (0, ∞)` be a function such that for any tagged
*partition* of `I` subordinate to `rₖ`, `k=1,2`, the integral sum of `f` over this partition differs
from the integral of `f` by at most `εₖ`. Then for any two tagged *prepartition* `π₁ π₂` subordinate
to `r₁` and `r₂` respectively and covering the same part of `I`, the integral sums of `f` over these
prepartitions differ from each other by at most `ε₁ + ε₂`.

The actual statement

- uses `BoxIntegral.Integrable.convergenceR` instead of a predicate assumption on `r`;
- uses `BoxIntegral.IntegrationParams.MemBaseSet` instead of “subordinate to `r`” to
  account for additional requirements like being a Henstock partition or having a bounded
  distortion.

See also `BoxIntegral.Integrable.dist_integralSum_sum_integral_le_of_memBaseSet_of_iUnion_eq` and
`BoxIntegral.Integrable.dist_integralSum_sum_integral_le_of_memBaseSet`.

represented as a finite union of boxes, the integral sums of `f` over tagged prepartitions that

BoxIntegral.Integrable.dist_integralSum_.comment:
**Henstock-Sacks inequality**. Let `r : ℝⁿ → (0, ∞)` be a function such that for any tagged
*partition* of `I` subordinate to `r`, the integral sum of `f` over this partition differs from the
integral of `f` by at most `ε`. Then for any tagged *prepartition* `π` subordinate to `r`, the
integral sum of `f` over this prepartition differs from the integral of `f` over the part of `I`
covered by `π` by at most `ε`.

The actual statement

- uses `BoxIntegral.Integrable.convergenceR` instead of a predicate assumption on `r`;
- uses `BoxIntegral.IntegrationParams.MemBaseSet` instead of “subordinate to `r`” to
  account for additional requirements like being a Henstock partition or having a bounded
  distortion;
- takes an extra argument `π₀ : prepartition I` and an assumption `π.Union = π₀.Union` instead of
  using `π.to_prepartition`.

explanatories.Dist.dist: A distance function that defines how to measure the separation between elements of a type can be created when the type adheres to the properties of a distance metric.
explanatories.BoxIntegral.Integrable.convergenceR: This defines a function that, given an integrable function and a positive epsilon, provides a way to choose a tagged partition ensuring that the corresponding integral sum is as close as desired to the integral value under certain conditions.
explanatories.BoxIntegral.Prepartition.iUnion: The union of the boxes in a prepartition represents the portion of the larger box that is covered by those boxes.

BoxIntegral.Integrable.sum_integral_cong.comment:
If `f` is integrable on `I`, then `fun J ↦ integral J l f vol` is box-additive on subboxes of
`I`: if `π₁`, `π₂` are two prepartitions of `I` covering the same part of `I`, the sum of integrals
of `f` over the boxes of `π₁` is equal to the sum of integrals of `f` over the boxes of `π₂`.

See also `BoxIntegral.Integrable.toBoxAdditive` for a bundled version.

BoxIntegral.HasIntegral.of_le_Henstock_of_forall_isLittleO.{u, v, w} {ι : Type u} {E : Type v} {F : Type w}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] {I : Box ι} [Fintype ι]
  {l : IntegrationParams} {f : (ι → ℝ) → E} {vol : ι →ᵇᵃ[⊤] E →L[ℝ] F} (hl : l ≤ Henstock) (B : ι →ᵇᵃ[↑I] ℝ)
  (hB0 : ∀ (J : Box ι), 0 ≤ B J) (g : ι →ᵇᵃ[↑I] F) (s : Set (ι → ℝ)) (hs : s.Countable)
  (H₁ :
    ∀ (c : ℝ≥0),
      ∀ x ∈ Box.Icc I ∩ s,
        ∀ ε > 0,
          ∃ δ > 0,
            ∀ J ≤ I,
              Box.Icc J ⊆ Metric.closedBall x δ →
                x ∈ Box.Icc J → (l.bDistortion = true → J.distortion ≤ c) → dist ((vol J) (f x)) (g J) ≤ ε)
  (H₂ :
    ∀ (c : ℝ≥0),
      ∀ x ∈ Box.Icc I \ s,
        ∀ ε > 0,
          ∃ δ > 0,
            ∀ J ≤ I,
              Box.Icc J ⊆ Metric.closedBall x δ →
                x ∈ Box.Icc J → (l.bDistortion = true → J.distortion ≤ c) → dist ((vol J) (f x)) (g J) ≤ ε * B J) :
  HasIntegral I l f vol (g I)
BoxIntegral.HasIntegral.of_le_Henstock_o.comment:
A function `f` has Henstock (or `⊥`) integral over `I` is equal to the value of a box-additive
function `g` on `I` provided that `vol J (f x)` is sufficiently close to `g J` for sufficiently
small boxes `J ∋ x`. This lemma is useful to prove, e.g., to prove the Divergence theorem for
integral along `⊥`.

Let `l` be either `BoxIntegral.IntegrationParams.Henstock` or `⊥`. Let `g` a box-additive function
on subboxes of `I`. Suppose that there exists a nonnegative box-additive function `B` and a
countable set `s` with the following property.

For every `c : ℝ≥0`, a point `x ∈ I.Icc`, and a positive `ε` there exists `δ > 0` such that for any
box `J ≤ I` such that

- `x ∈ J.Icc ⊆ Metric.closedBall x δ`;
- if `l.bDistortion` (i.e., `l = ⊥`), then the distortion of `J` is less than or equal to `c`,

the distance between the term `vol J (f x)` of an integral sum corresponding to `J` and `g J` is
less than or equal to `ε` if `x ∈ s` and is less than or equal to `ε * B J` otherwise.

Then `f` is integrable on `I` along `l` with integral `g I`.

  [NormedSpace ℝ E] {n : ℕ} [CompleteSpace E] (I : Box (Fin (n + 1))) {i : Fin (n + 1)} {f : (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) → E}
  {f' : (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) →L[ℝ] E} (hfc : ContinuousOn f (Box.Icc I)) {x : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ} (hxI : x ∈ Box.Icc I)

          integral (I.face i) ⊥ (f ∘ i.insertNth (I.lower i)) BoxAdditiveMap.volume)‖ ≤
    2 * ε * ↑c * ∏ j : Fin (n + 1), (I.upper j - I.lower j)

BoxIntegral.hasIntegral_GP_pderiv.code:
BoxIntegral.hasIntegral_GP_pderiv.{u} {E : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] {n : ℕ} [CompleteSpace E]
  (I : Box (Fin (n + 1))) (f : (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) → E) (f' : (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) → (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) →L[ℝ] E)
  (s : Set (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ)) (hs : s.Countable) (Hs : ∀ x ∈ s, ContinuousWithinAt f (Box.Icc I) x)
  (Hd : ∀ x ∈ Box.Icc I \ s, HasFDerivWithinAt f (f' x) (Box.Icc I) x) (i : Fin (n + 1)) :
  HasIntegral I GP (fun x => (f' x) (Pi.single i 1)) BoxAdditiveMap.volume
    (integral (I.face i) GP (fun x => f (i.insertNth (I.upper i) x)) BoxAdditiveMap.volume -
      integral (I.face i) GP (fun x => f (i.insertNth (I.lower i) x)) BoxAdditiveMap.volume)
BoxIntegral.hasIntegral_GP_pderiv.comment:
If `f : ℝⁿ⁺¹ → E` is differentiable on a closed rectangular box `I` with derivative `f'`, then
the partial derivative `fun x ↦ f' x (Pi.single i 1)` is Henstock-Kurzweil integrable with integral
equal to the difference of integrals of `f` over the faces `x i = I.upper i` and `x i = I.lower i`.

More precisely, we use a non-standard generalization of the Henstock-Kurzweil integral and
we allow `f` to be non-differentiable (but still continuous) at a countable set of points.

box_integral.has_integral_GP_pderiv.code:
BoxIntegral.hasIntegral_GP_pderiv.{u} {E : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] {n : ℕ} [CompleteSpace E]
  (I : Box (Fin (n + 1))) (f : (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) → E) (f' : (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) → (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) →L[ℝ] E)
  (s : Set (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ)) (hs : s.Countable) (Hs : ∀ x ∈ s, ContinuousWithinAt f (Box.Icc I) x)
  (Hd : ∀ x ∈ Box.Icc I \ s, HasFDerivWithinAt f (f' x) (Box.Icc I) x) (i : Fin (n + 1)) :
  HasIntegral I GP (fun x => (f' x) (Pi.single i 1)) BoxAdditiveMap.volume
    (integral (I.face i) GP (fun x => f (i.insertNth (I.upper i) x)) BoxAdditiveMap.volume -
      integral (I.face i) GP (fun x => f (i.insertNth (I.lower i) x)) BoxAdditiveMap.volume)
box_integral.has_integral_GP_pderiv.comment:
If `f : ℝⁿ⁺¹ → E` is differentiable on a closed rectangular box `I` with derivative `f'`, then
the partial derivative `fun x ↦ f' x (Pi.single i 1)` is Henstock-Kurzweil integrable with integral
equal to the difference of integrals of `f` over the faces `x i = I.upper i` and `x i = I.lower i`.

More precisely, we use a non-standard generalization of the Henstock-Kurzweil integral and
we allow `f` to be non-differentiable (but still continuous) at a countable set of points.

BoxIntegral.hasIntegral_GP_divergence_of.code:
BoxIntegral.hasIntegral_GP_divergence_of_forall_hasDerivWithinAt.{u} {E : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace ℝ E] {n : ℕ} [CompleteSpace E] (I : Box (Fin (n + 1))) (f : (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) → Fin (n + 1) → E)
  (f' : (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) → (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) →L[ℝ] Fin (n + 1) → E) (s : Set (Fin (n + 1) → ℝ)) (hs : s.Countable)
  (Hs : ∀ x ∈ s, ContinuousWithinAt f (Box.Icc I) x)
  (Hd : ∀ x ∈ Box.Icc I \ s, HasFDerivWithinAt f (f' x) (Box.Icc I) x) :
  HasIntegral I GP (fun x => ∑ i : Fin (n + 1), (f' x) (Pi.single i 1) i) BoxAdditiveMap.volume
    (∑ i : Fin (n + 1),
      (integral (I.face i) GP (fun x => f (i.insertNth (I.upper i) x) i) BoxAdditiveMap.volume -
        integral (I.face i) GP (fun x => f (i.insertNth (I.lower i) x) i) BoxAdditiveMap.volume))
BoxIntegral.hasIntegral_GP_divergence_of.comment:
Divergence theorem for a Henstock-Kurzweil style integral.

If `f : ℝⁿ⁺¹ → Eⁿ⁺¹` is differentiable on a closed rectangular box `I` with derivative `f'`, then
the divergence `∑ i, f' x (Pi.single i 1) i` is Henstock-Kurzweil integrable with integral equal to
the sum of integrals of `f` over the faces of `I` taken with appropriate signs.

More precisely, we use a non-standard generalization of the Henstock-Kurzweil integral and
we allow `f` to be non-differentiable (but still continuous) at a countable set of points.

If `f : ℝⁿ → E` is Bochner integrable w.r.t. a locally finite measure `μ` on a rectangular box
`I`, then it is McShane integrable on `I` with the same integral.

Subadditive.comment:
A real-valued sequence is subadditive if it satisfies the inequality `u (m + n) ≤ u m + u n`
for all `m, n`.
Subadditive.fullDefinition: def Subadditive (u : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop :=   ∀ m n, u (m + n) ≤ u m + u n
Subadditive.description: A real-valued sequence is considered subadditive if the value at the sum of any two indices does not exceed the sum of the values at those individual indices.

geom_lt.code: geom_lt {u : ℕ → ℝ} {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c) {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (h : ∀ k < n, c * u k < u (k + 1)) : c ^ n * u 0 < u n
geom_lt.description: If a sequence starts from a non-negative term and is bounded below by a constant multiplied by its preceding terms, then the product of that constant raised to a power and the initial term is less than the term at that power in the sequence.

geom_le.code: geom_le {u : ℕ → ℝ} {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c) (n : ℕ) (h : ∀ k < n, c * u k ≤ u (k + 1)) : c ^ n * u 0 ≤ u n
geom_le.description: Under certain conditions, a sequence grows in a geometric manner, such that the product of a non-negative constant raised to a power and the initial term of the sequence is less than or equal to the term of the sequence at that power.

lt_geom.code: lt_geom {u : ℕ → ℝ} {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c) {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (h : ∀ k < n, u (k + 1) < c * u k) : u n < c ^ n * u 0
lt_geom.description: Under certain conditions, a sequence grows in a strict geometric manner, such that the term of the sequence at a specific index is less than the product of a non-negative constant raised to that index and the initial term of the sequence.

le_geom.code: le_geom {u : ℕ → ℝ} {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c) (n : ℕ) (h : ∀ k < n, u (k + 1) ≤ c * u k) : u n ≤ c ^ n * u 0
le_geom.description: The sequence defined by a non-negative initial term satisfies a geometric bound based on its previous terms and a constant factor for all indices up to a given point.

explanatories.le_of_lt: This theorem asserts that if one element is strictly less than another in a preorder, then it is also less than or equal to that element.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.pow_pos: In a strict ordered semiring, if a positive element is raised to a natural number power, the result remains positive.
explanatories.HasSum: An infinite sum on a topological monoid is defined as the limit of sums over increasingly larger finite subsets, and this sum operation is robust against reordering of terms.
explanatories.Encodable.encode: This defines a method for encoding elements from a specific type into natural numbers.
explanatories.Summable.comp_injective: If a function is summable and there exists an injective function mapping another set to the original function's domain, then the composition of the original function with the injective function is also summable.
explanatories.Encodable.encode_injective: The encoding function is injective, meaning that distinct elements in the original type correspond to distinct natural number encodings.
explanatories.hasSum_geometric_two': The series formed by mapping natural numbers to a specific fraction involving a constant and powers of two converges to that constant.
explanatories.div_pos: This theorem demonstrates that in a linear ordered semifield, the quotient of two positive elements is also positive.
explanatories.half_pos: This theorem asserts that in a linear ordered semifield, if an element is positive, then half of that element is also positive.
explanatories.zero_lt_two: This theorem demonstrates that in any partially ordered set that functions as an additive monoid with one, zero is strictly less than two.
explanatories.HasSum.summable: If a series converges to a specific value, then it is considered summable.
explanatories.hasSum_le_inj: If a function related to one series is injectively mapped to another function where the latter is non-negative outside the image of the first, and the terms of the first series are less than or equal to the corresponding terms of the second, then the sum of the first series is less than or equal to the sum of the second series.
explanatories.le_rfl: This theorem states that every element in a preorder is less than or equal to itself.

posSumOfEncodable.description: For any positive number, this defines a positive sequence indexed by an encodable type such that the sum of the sequence is less than that number.

  (hlim :
    ∀ (a : ℝ),
      1 < a →
        ∃ c,
          (∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop, ↑(c (n + 1)) ≤ a * ↑(c n)) ∧
            Tendsto c atTop atTop ∧ Tendsto (fun n => u (c n) / ↑(c n)) atTop (𝓝 l)) :
  Tendsto (fun n => u n / ↑n) atTop (𝓝 l)

exponential growth rate arbitrarily close to `1`, then `u n / n` tends to `l`.

explanatories.continuous_of_continuousAt_zero: A monoid homomorphism from a topological group to a topological monoid is continuous on the entire space if it is continuous at the identity element.
explanatories.continuousAt_def: A function is continuous at a given point if and only if the preimage of every neighborhood of the function's output at that point is a neighborhood of the input point.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_zero: This theorem demonstrates that a linear map assigns the zero element of its domain to the zero element of its codomain.
explanatories.NormedField.exists_lt_norm: This theorem asserts that in a non-trivially normed field, there exists an element whose norm is greater than a given positive real number.
explanatories.LT.lt.le: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if one element is strictly less than a second, then it is also less than or equal to that second element.
explanatories.norm_pos_iff: This theorem establishes that the norm of an element in a normed group is positive if and only if the element is not equal to the identity.
explanatories.Iff.mp: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.Set.smul_set_mono: The theorem states that if one set is a subset of another, then scaling both sets by a constant results in the scaled version of the first set being a subset of the scaled version of the second set.
explanatories.Set.subset_preimage_image: Any set is a subset of its preimage under the image of a function.
explanatories.Set.preimage_mono: If one set is a subset of another, then the preimage of the first set under any function is a subset of the preimage of the second set.
explanatories.Set.mem_inv_smul_set_iff₀: The theorem describes the relationship between an element belonging to the inverse scalar multiplication of a set and the element resulting from scalar multiplication of that element, asserting that they are equivalent under certain conditions.
explanatories.Set.mem_preimage: An element is in the preimage of a set under a function if and only if the image of that element is in the original set.
explanatories.LinearMap.map_smul: This theorem states that a linear map commutes with scalar multiplication, meaning that applying the map to the product of a scalar and a vector is the same as multiplying the image of the vector by the scalar.
explanatories.inv_smul_smul₀: This theorem states that multiplying an element by a non-zero scalar and then by its inverse returns the original element unchanged.
explanatories.Filter.mem_of_superset: A theorem stating that if a set belongs to a filter and is a subset of another set, then that other set also belongs to the filter.
explanatories.set_smul_mem_nhds_smul: The image of a neighborhood under scalar multiplication by a non-zero constant remains within the neighborhood of the scalar multiplication of its point.
explanatories.inv_ne_zero: This theorem asserts that in a group with zero, the inverse of a nonzero element is also nonzero.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.trans: This theorem demonstrates that in a transitive relation, if the relation holds from the first element to the second and from the second to the third, it must also hold from the first element to the third.
explanatories.map_zero: This theorem asserts a property about a type of morphism that maintains the identity element across two algebraic structures with defined identity elements.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.trivial: The statement confirms that the proposition asserting truth is indeed valid and can be proven simply.
explanatories.True.intro: The statement establishes that the proposition of truth is inherently valid, with a specific proof confirming its truth.
explanatories.UniformContinuous.continuous: If a function between two uniform spaces is uniformly continuous, then it is also continuous in the standard topological sense.

LinearMap.clmOfExistsBoundedImage.fullDefinition: def LinearMap.clmOfExistsBoundedImage (f : E →ₗ[𝕜] F)     (h : ∃ V ∈ 𝓝 (0 : E), Bornology.IsVonNBounded 𝕜 (f '' V)) : E →L[𝕜] F :=   ⟨f, by     -- It suffices to show that `f` is continuous at `0`.     refine continuous_of_continuousAt_zero f ?_     rw [continuousAt_def, f.map_zero]     intro U hU     -- Continuity means that `U ∈ 𝓝 0` implies that `f ⁻¹' U ∈ 𝓝 0`.     rcases h with ⟨V, hV, h⟩     rcases (h hU).exists_pos with ⟨r, hr, h⟩     rcases NormedField.exists_lt_norm 𝕜 r with ⟨x, hx⟩     specialize h x hx.le     -- After unfolding all the definitions, we know that `f '' V ⊆ x • U`. We use this to show the     -- inclusion `x⁻¹ • V ⊆ f⁻¹' U`.     have x_ne := norm_pos_iff.mp (hr.trans hx)     have : x⁻¹ • V ⊆ f ⁻¹' U :=       calc         x⁻¹ • V ⊆ x⁻¹ • f ⁻¹' (f '' V) := Set.smul_set_mono (Set.subset_preimage_image (⇑f) V)         _ ⊆ x⁻¹ • f ⁻¹' (x • U) := Set.smul_set_mono (Set.preimage_mono h)         _ = f ⁻¹' (x⁻¹ • x • U) := by           ext           simp only [Set.mem_inv_smul_set_iff₀ x_ne, Set.mem_preimage, LinearMap.map_smul]         _ ⊆ f ⁻¹' U := by rw [inv_smul_smul₀ x_ne _]     -- Using this inclusion, it suffices to show that `x⁻¹ • V` is in `𝓝 0`, which is trivial.     refine mem_of_superset ?_ this     convert set_smul_mem_nhds_smul hV (inv_ne_zero x_ne)     exact (smul_zero _).symm⟩
LinearMap.clmOfExistsBoundedImage.description: A continuous linear map can be constructed from a linear map if there is a neighborhood around zero in the first space that is mapped by the linear map into a bounded set in the second space.

We use this to show the     -- inclusion `x⁻¹ • V ⊆ f⁻¹' U`.     have x_ne := norm_pos_iff.mp (hr.trans hx)     have : x⁻¹ • V ⊆ f ⁻¹' U :=       calc         x⁻¹ • V ⊆ x⁻¹ • f ⁻¹' (f '' V) := Set.smul_set_mono (Set.subset_preimage_image (⇑f) V)         _ ⊆ x⁻¹ • f ⁻¹' (x • U) := Set.smul_set_mono (Set.preimage_mono h)         _ = f ⁻¹' (x⁻¹ • x • U) := by           ext           simp only [Set.mem_inv_smul_set_iff₀ x_ne, Set.mem_preimage, LinearMap.map_smul]         _ ⊆ f ⁻¹' U := by rw [inv_smul_smul₀ x_ne _]     -- Using this inclusion, it suffices to show that `x⁻¹ • V` is in `𝓝 0`, which is trivial.     refine mem_of_superset ?_ this     convert set_smul_mem_nhds_smul hV (inv_ne_zero x_ne)     exact (smul_zero _).symm⟩

WithSeminorms.equicontinuous_TFAE.code:
WithSeminorms.equicontinuous_TFAE.{u_1, u_2, u_5, u_6, u_9, u_10} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {𝕜₂ : Type u_2} {E : Type u_5}
  {F : Type u_6} {ι' : Type u_9} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [AddCommGroup E] [Module 𝕜 E] [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜₂]
  [AddCommGroup F] [Module 𝕜₂ F] {σ₁₂ : 𝕜 →+* 𝕜₂} [RingHomIsometric σ₁₂] [Nonempty ι'] {κ : Type u_10}
  {q : SeminormFamily 𝕜₂ F ι'} [UniformSpace E] [UniformAddGroup E] [u : UniformSpace F] [hu : UniformAddGroup F]
  (hq : WithSeminorms q) [ContinuousSMul 𝕜 E] (f : κ → E →ₛₗ[σ₁₂] F) :
  [EquicontinuousAt (DFunLike.coe ∘ f) 0, Equicontinuous (DFunLike.coe ∘ f), UniformEquicontinuous (DFunLike.coe ∘ f),
      ∀ (i : ι'), ∃ p, Continuous ⇑p ∧ ∀ (k : κ), (q i).comp (f k) ≤ p,
      ∀ (i : ι'), BddAbove (Set.range fun k => (q i).comp (f k)) ∧ Continuous (⨆ k, ⇑((q i).comp (f k)))].TFAE
WithSeminorms.equicontinuous_TFAE.comment:
Let `E` and `F` be two topological vector spaces over a `NontriviallyNormedField`, and assume
that the topology of `F` is generated by some family of seminorms `q`. For a family `f` of linear
maps from `E` to `F`, the following are equivalent:
* `f` is equicontinuous at `0`.
* `f` is equicontinuous.
* `f` is uniformly equicontinuous.
* For each `q i`, the family of seminorms `k ↦ (q i) ∘ (f k)` is bounded by some continuous
  seminorm `p` on `E`.
* For each `q i`, the seminorm `⊔ k, (q i) ∘ (f k)` is well-defined and continuous.

In particular, if you can determine all continuous seminorms on `E`, that gives you a complete
characterization of equicontinuity for linear maps from `E` to `F`. For example `E` and `F` are
both normed spaces, you get `NormedSpace.equicontinuous_TFAE`.

WithSeminorms.congr.{u_1, u_5, u_8, u_9} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_5} {ι : Type u_8} {ι' : Type u_9} [Nonempty ι]
  [Nonempty ι'] [NormedField 𝕜] [AddCommGroup E] [Module 𝕜 E] {p : SeminormFamily 𝕜 E ι} {q : SeminormFamily 𝕜 E ι'}
  [t : TopologicalSpace E] (hp : WithSeminorms p) (hpq : Seminorm.IsBounded p q LinearMap.id)
  (hqp : Seminorm.IsBounded q p LinearMap.id) : WithSeminorms q
WithSeminorms.congr.comment:
Two families of seminorms `p` and `q` on the same space generate the same topology
if each `p i` is bounded by some `C • Finset.sup s q` and vice-versa.

We formulate these boundedness assumptions as `Seminorm.IsBounded q p LinearMap.id` (and
vice-versa) to reuse the API. Furthermore, we don't actually state it as an equality of topologies
but as a way to deduce `WithSeminorms q` from `WithSeminorms p`, since this should be more
useful in practice.

Seminorm.bound_of_continuous_normedSpace.code:
Seminorm.bound_of_continuous_normedSpace.{u_1, u_6} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {F : Type u_6} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜]
  [SeminormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F] (q : Seminorm 𝕜 F) (hq : Continuous ⇑q) :
  ∃ C, 0 < C ∧ ∀ (x : F), q x ≤ C * ‖x‖
Seminorm.bound_of_continuous_normedSpace.comment:
Let `F` be a semi-`NormedSpace` over a `NontriviallyNormedField`, and let `q` be a
seminorm on `F`. If `q` is continuous, then it is uniformly controlled by the norm, that is there
is some `C > 0` such that `∀ x, q x ≤ C * ‖x‖`.
The continuity ensures boundedness on a ball of some radius `ε`. The nontriviality of the
norm is then used to rescale any element into an element of norm in `[ε/C, ε[`, thus with a
controlled image by `q`. The control of `q` at the original element follows by rescaling.
Seminorm.bound_of_continuous_normedSpace.description: If a seminorm on a semi-normed space is continuous, then there exists a positive constant such that the seminorm is bounded above by that constant multiplied by the norm of any vector in the space.

  (𝓝 0).HasBasis (fun s => s ∈ 𝓝 0 ∧ Balanced 𝕜 s ∧ Convex ℝ s) id

explanatories.Balanced: A set is considered balanced if multiplying its elements by any scalar of norm less than or equal to one results in elements that remain within the set.
explanatories.Convex: This definition characterizes a set as convex if, for any two points within the set, the entire line segment connecting them remains within the set.
explanatories.id: The identity function returns its input unchanged and can be used to explicitly assign a type to an expression for typeclass inference purposes.

nhds_basis_abs_convex.description: The neighborhood of zero in a locally convex space has a basis consisting of sets that are balanced, convex, and contained in the neighborhood of zero.

Asymptotics.IsBigOWith.code:
Asymptotics.IsBigOWith.{u_17, u_18, u_19} {α : Type u_17} {E : Type u_18} {F : Type u_19} [Norm E] [Norm F] (c : ℝ)
  (l : Filter α) (f : α → E) (g : α → F) : Prop
Asymptotics.IsBigOWith.comment:
This version of the Landau notation `IsBigOWith C l f g` where `f` and `g` are two functions on
a type `α` and `l` is a filter on `α`, means that eventually for `l`, `‖f‖` is bounded by `C * ‖g‖`.
In other words, `‖f‖ / ‖g‖` is eventually bounded by `C`, modulo division by zero issues that are
avoided by this definition. Probably you want to use `IsBigO` instead of this relation.
Asymptotics.IsBigOWith.fullDefinition: irreducible_def IsBigOWith (c : ℝ) (l : Filter α) (f : α → E) (g : α → F) : Prop :=   ∀ᶠ x in l, ‖f x‖ ≤ c * ‖g x‖
Asymptotics.IsBigOWith.description: This definition captures a relationship where one function is eventually bounded by a constant multiple of another function, relative to a specified filter.

Asymptotics.IsBigO.code:
Asymptotics.IsBigO.{u_17, u_18, u_19} {α : Type u_17} {E : Type u_18} {F : Type u_19} [Norm E] [Norm F] (l : Filter α)
  (f : α → E) (g : α → F) : Prop
Asymptotics.IsBigO.comment:
The Landau notation `f =O[l] g` where `f` and `g` are two functions on a type `α` and `l` is
a filter on `α`, means that eventually for `l`, `‖f‖` is bounded by a constant multiple of `‖g‖`.
In other words, `‖f‖ / ‖g‖` is eventually bounded, modulo division by zero issues that are avoided
by this definition.

Asymptotics.IsLittleO.code:
Asymptotics.IsLittleO.{u_17, u_18, u_19} {α : Type u_17} {E : Type u_18} {F : Type u_19} [Norm E] [Norm F]
  (l : Filter α) (f : α → E) (g : α → F) : Prop
Asymptotics.IsLittleO.comment:
The Landau notation `f =o[l] g` where `f` and `g` are two functions on a type `α` and `l` is
a filter on `α`, means that eventually for `l`, `‖f‖` is bounded by an arbitrarily small constant
multiple of `‖g‖`. In other words, `‖f‖ / ‖g‖` tends to `0` along `l`, modulo division by zero
issues that are avoided by this definition.

explanatories.Asymptotics.IsBigOWith: This definition captures a relationship where one function is eventually bounded by a constant multiple of another function, relative to a specified filter.

Asymptotics.IsLittleO.fullDefinition: irreducible_def IsLittleO (l : Filter α) (f : α → E) (g : α → F) : Prop :=   ∀ ⦃c : ℝ⦄, 0 < c → IsBigOWith c l f g
Asymptotics.IsLittleO.description: This definition establishes the concept of Little O notation with respect to a filter, indicating that one function becomes negligible relative to another function as the input approaches a certain limit defined by the filter.

Asymptotics.IsEquivalent.code:
Asymptotics.IsEquivalent.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup β] (l : Filter α) (u v : α → β) :
  Prop
Asymptotics.IsEquivalent.comment:
Two functions `u` and `v` are said to be asymptotically equivalent along a filter `l` when
`u x - v x = o(v x)` as `x` converges along `l`.
Asymptotics.IsEquivalent.fullDefinition: def IsEquivalent (l : Filter α) (u v : α → β) :=   (u - v) =o[l] v
Asymptotics.IsEquivalent.description: Two functions are considered asymptotically equivalent along a specified filter if the difference between them becomes negligible compared to one of the functions as the input converges along that filter.

Real.sqrtTwoAddSeries.comment:
the series `sqrtTwoAddSeries x n` is `sqrt(2 + sqrt(2 + ... ))` with `n` square roots,
starting with `x`. We define it here because `cos (pi / 2 ^ (n+1)) = sqrtTwoAddSeries 0 n / 2`
Real.sqrtTwoAddSeries.fullDefinition: noncomputable def sqrtTwoAddSeries (x : ℝ) : ℕ → ℝ   | 0 => x   | n + 1 => √(2 + sqrtTwoAddSeries x n)
Real.sqrtTwoAddSeries.description: This defines a series that calculates the nested square root of two added to itself, starting from a given real number and continuing with a specified number of iterations.

Complex.abs_exp_mul_exp_add_exp_neg_le_o.code:
Complex.abs_exp_mul_exp_add_exp_neg_le_of_abs_im_le {a b : ℝ} (ha : a ≤ 0) {z : ℂ} (hz : |z.im| ≤ b) (hb : b ≤ π / 2) :
  abs (cexp (↑a * (cexp z + cexp (-z)))) ≤ rexp (a * Real.cos b * rexp |z.re|)
Complex.abs_exp_mul_exp_add_exp_neg_le_o.comment:
A supporting lemma for the **Phragmen-Lindelöf principle** in a horizontal strip. If `z : ℂ`
belongs to a horizontal strip `|Complex.im z| ≤ b`, `b ≤ π / 2`, and `a ≤ 0`, then
$$\left|exp^{a\left(e^{z}+e^{-z}\right)}\right| \le e^{a\cos b \exp^{|re z|}}.$$

explanatories.DifferentiableWithinAt.arctan: The theorem establishes that if a function is differentiable within a set at a point, then the composition of the arctangent function with that function is also differentiable within the same set at that point.
explanatories.DifferentiableAt.arctan: The theorem establishes that if a function is differentiable at a point, then the composition of the arctangent function with that function is also differentiable at the same point.
explanatories.DifferentiableOn.arctan: The theorem states that if a function is differentiable on a set, then the arctangent of that function is also differentiable on the same set.
explanatories.Differentiable.arctan: The theorem asserts that if a function is differentiable in a given space, then the arctangent of that function is also differentiable in the same space.
explanatories.ContDiffAt.arctan: The theorem states that if a function is continuously differentiable at a point, then the arctangent of that function is also continuously differentiable at the same point.
explanatories.ContDiff.arctan: The theorem states that if a function is continuously differentiable, then the composition of the arctangent with that function is also continuously differentiable.
explanatories.ContDiffWithinAt.arctan: The theorem states that if a function is continuously differentiable up to a certain order at a point within a set, then the composition of the arctangent function with that function is also continuously differentiable up to the same order at the same point within the set.

cont_diff_on.arctan.description: The theorem states that if a function is continuously differentiable on a set, then the arctangent of that function is also continuously differentiable on the same set.

a simpler proof.

        ∫ (x : ℝ) in 0 ..π / 2, Complex.cos (2 * z * ↑x) * ↑(cos x) ^ (2 * n)) /
      ↑(∫ (x : ℝ) in 0 ..π / 2, cos x ^ (2 * n))

ENNReal.log.comment:
The logarithm function defined on the extended nonnegative reals `ℝ≥0∞`
to the extended reals `EReal`. Coincides with the usual logarithm function
and with `Real.log` on positive reals, and takes values `log 0 = ⊥` and `log ⊤ = ⊤`.
Conventions about multiplication in `ℝ≥0∞` and addition in `EReal` make the identity
`log (x * y) = log x + log y` unconditional.

explanatories.EReal: This definition introduces a type that represents the extended real numbers, which include negative infinity and positive infinity.
explanatories.ENNReal.toReal: This definition describes a function that converts an extended nonnegative real number to a standard real number, returning the original number if it is finite and zero if it represents infinity.
explanatories.EReal.toReal: This definition establishes a mapping from extended real numbers to real numbers, whereby infinities are assigned the value of zero.

ENNReal.log.fullDefinition: noncomputable def log (x : ℝ≥0∞) : EReal :=   if x = 0 then ⊥     else if x = ⊤ then ⊤     else Real.log x.toReal
ENNReal.log.description: The logarithm function is extended to include nonnegative infinite values, where it behaves like the standard logarithm for positive numbers, assigns negative infinity to zero, positive infinity to infinity, and maintains the property of logarithmic addition for multiplication.

Real.abs_log_sub_add_sum_range_le.code:
Real.abs_log_sub_add_sum_range_le {x : ℝ} (h : |x| < 1) (n : ℕ) :
  |∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, x ^ (i + 1) / (↑i + 1) + log (1 - x)| ≤ |x| ^ (n + 1) / (1 - |x|)
Real.abs_log_sub_add_sum_range_le.comment:
A crude lemma estimating the difference between `log (1-x)` and its Taylor series at `0`,
where the main point of the bound is that it tends to `0`. The goal is to deduce the series
expansion of the logarithm, in `hasSum_pow_div_log_of_abs_lt_1`.

real.abs_log_sub_add_sum_range_le.code:
Real.abs_log_sub_add_sum_range_le {x : ℝ} (h : |x| < 1) (n : ℕ) :
  |∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, x ^ (i + 1) / (↑i + 1) + log (1 - x)| ≤ |x| ^ (n + 1) / (1 - |x|)
real.abs_log_sub_add_sum_range_le.comment:
A crude lemma estimating the difference between `log (1-x)` and its Taylor series at `0`,
where the main point of the bound is that it tends to `0`. The goal is to deduce the series
expansion of the logarithm, in `hasSum_pow_div_log_of_abs_lt_1`.

explanatories.Complex.exp_ofReal_re: This theorem states that the real part of the exponential function applied to a real number is equal to the exponential of that real number.
explanatories.Set.mem_setOf: An element is in the set of all elements satisfying a property if and only if that property holds for the element.
explanatories.Complex.log_im: The imaginary part of the logarithm of a complex number is equal to its argument.
explanatories.Set.mem_Ioo: This theorem states that an element belongs to the open interval between two given elements in a preorder structure if and only if it is strictly greater than the first element and strictly less than the second element.
explanatories.Complex.neg_pi_lt_arg: The argument of any complex number is always greater than negative pi.
explanatories.Complex.arg_lt_pi_iff: The argument of a complex number is less than pi if and only if the real part is non-negative or the imaginary part is non-zero.
explanatories.true_and: The theorem demonstrates that the conjunction of a true proposition and any other proposition is equivalent to the other proposition itself.
explanatories.Or.imp_left: The theorem shows that if one proposition implies another, then the disjunction of that proposition with a third proposition implies the disjunction of the second proposition with the same third proposition.
explanatories.le_of_lt: This theorem asserts that if one element is strictly less than another in a preorder, then it is also less than or equal to that element.
explanatories.Complex.log_exp: The logarithm of the exponential of a complex number, when the imaginary part is within the range from negative pi to pi, equals the original complex number.
explanatories.Complex.exp_log: The exponential of the logarithm of a non-zero complex number equals the original complex number.
explanatories.Complex.continuous_exp: The exponential function of complex numbers is continuous.
explanatories.Continuous.continuousOn: If a function is continuous on its entire domain, it is also continuous on any subset of that domain.
explanatories.isOpen_Ioo: This theorem asserts that in a topological space with an order-closed topology, the open interval between two elements is an open set.
explanatories.IsOpen.preimage: The preimage of an open set under a continuous function is also an open set.
explanatories.Complex.continuous_im: The imaginary component of a complex number is a continuous function.

complex.exp_local_homeomorph.fullDefinition: noncomputable def expPartialHomeomorph : PartialHomeomorph ℂ ℂ :=   PartialHomeomorph.ofContinuousOpen     { toFun := exp       invFun := log       source := {z : ℂ | z.im ∈ Ioo (-π) π}       target := slitPlane       map_source' := by         rintro ⟨x, y⟩ ⟨h₁ : -π < y, h₂ : y < π⟩         refine (not_or_of_imp fun hz => ?_).symm         obtain rfl : y = 0 := by           rw [exp_im] at hz           simpa [(Real.exp_pos _).ne', Real.sin_eq_zero_iff_of_lt_of_lt h₁ h₂] using hz         rw [← ofReal_def, exp_ofReal_re]         exact Real.exp_pos x       map_target' := fun z h => by         simp only [mem_setOf, log_im, mem_Ioo, neg_pi_lt_arg, arg_lt_pi_iff, true_and]         exact h.imp_left le_of_lt       left_inv' := fun x hx => log_exp hx.1 (le_of_lt hx.2)       right_inv' := fun x hx => exp_log <| slitPlane_ne_zero hx }     continuous_exp.continuousOn isOpenMap_exp (isOpen_Ioo.preimage continuous_im)

Complex.log_eq_integral.description: The logarithm of a complex number, shifted by one, can be expressed as a product of that number and the integral of its multiplicative inverse over the interval from zero to one, given that the shifted complex number remains in the slit plane.

Complex.logTaylor.fullDefinition: def logTaylor (n : ℕ) : ℂ → ℂ := fun z ↦ ∑ j ∈ Finset.range n, (-1) ^ (j + 1) * z ^ j / j
Complex.logTaylor.description: The nth Taylor polynomial of the logarithm function at one is defined as a complex-valued function.

Complex.logTaylor_zero.description: The zeroth Taylor polynomial of the logarithm function at one is defined to be the constant function that outputs zero for any input.

Complex.logTaylor_succ.code: Complex.logTaylor_succ (n : ℕ) : logTaylor (n + 1) = logTaylor n + fun z => (-1) ^ (n + 1) * z ^ n / ↑n
Complex.logTaylor_succ.description: The (n + 1)th Taylor polynomial of the logarithm function at one can be expressed as the sum of the nth polynomial and a term that involves the input raised to the power of n, divided by n, with a sign dependent on n.

bernstein.z.fullDefinition: def z {n : ℕ} (k : Fin (n + 1)) : I :=   ⟨(k : ℝ) / n, by     cases' n with n     · norm_num     · have h₁ : 0 < (n.succ : ℝ) := mod_cast Nat.succ_pos _       have h₂ : ↑k ≤ n.succ := mod_cast Fin.le_last k       rw [Set.mem_Icc, le_div_iff h₁, div_le_iff h₁]       norm_cast       simp [h₂]⟩
bernstein.z.description: The function maps a finite point within a specified range to its corresponding equally spaced value in the unit interval.

```
∑ k : Fin (n+1), f (k/n : ℝ) * n.choose k * x^k * (1-x)^(n-k)
```
for a continuous function `f : C([0,1], ℝ)` converge uniformly to `f` as `n` tends to infinity.

This is the proof given in [Richard Beals' *Analysis, an introduction*][beals-analysis], §7D,
and reproduced on wikipedia.

For `x > 0`, it is equal to `exp (y log x)`. For `x = 0`, one sets `0 ^ 0=1` and `0 ^ y=0` for
`y ≠ 0`. For `x < 0`, the definition is somewhat arbitrary as it depends on the choice of a complex
determination of the logarithm. With our conventions, it is equal to `exp (y log x) cos (π y)`.

explanatories.Complex.re: This defines a function that extracts the real component from a complex number.

`x = 0` and `y + z = 0`, where the right hand side is `1` while the left hand side can vanish.
The inequality is always true, though, and given in this lemma.

restriction of the real power function. For `x > 0`, it is equal to `exp (y log x)`. For `x = 0`,

ENNReal.rpow.comment:
The real power function `x^y` on extended nonnegative reals, defined for `x : ℝ≥0∞` and
`y : ℝ` as the restriction of the real power function if `0 < x < ⊤`, and with the natural values
for `0` and `⊤` (i.e., `0 ^ x = 0` for `x > 0`, `1` for `x = 0` and `⊤` for `x < 0`, and
`⊤ ^ x = 1 / 0 ^ x`).

explanatories.Prod.snd: This defines a function that retrieves the second element from a given pair of values.
