  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] {ι : Type u_4} [DecidableEq ι] {V : ι → Submodule 𝕜 E}
  (hV : OrthogonalFamily 𝕜 (fun i => ↥(V i)) fun i => (V i).subtypeₗᵢ) (hc : IsComplete ↑(iSup V)) :
  DirectSum.IsInternal V ↔ (iSup V)ᗮ = ⊥
OrthogonalFamily.isInternal_iff_of_isCom.comment:
An orthogonal family of subspaces of `E` satisfies `DirectSum.IsInternal` (that is,
they provide an internal direct sum decomposition of `E`) if and only if their span has trivial
orthogonal complement.

explanatories.IsComplete: A set is complete if every Cauchy filter that contains it converges to a limit within the set.
explanatories.DecidableEq: A type is said to have decidable equality if it is possible to determine whether any two elements of that type are equal.
explanatories.DirectSum.IsInternal: This definition states that a direct sum formed by a collection of additive submonoids is called internal if the natural map from the direct sum to the total monoid is bijective.

OrthogonalFamily.isInternal_iff_of_isCom.description: An orthogonal family of subspaces provides an internal direct sum decomposition if and only if the orthogonal complement of their span is trivial, indicating that the subspaces are independent.

OrthogonalFamily.decomposition.code:
OrthogonalFamily.decomposition.{u_1, u_2, u_4} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [_root_.RCLike 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] {ι : Type u_4} [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι] {V : ι → Submodule 𝕜 E}
  [∀ (i : ι), CompleteSpace ↥(V i)] (hV : OrthogonalFamily 𝕜 (fun i => ↥(V i)) fun i => (V i).subtypeₗᵢ)
  (h : iSup V = ⊤) : Decomposition V
OrthogonalFamily.decomposition.comment:
If a family of submodules is orthogonal and they span the whole space, then the orthogonal
projection provides a means to decompose the space into its submodules.

The projection function is `decompose V x i = orthogonalProjection (V i) x`.

See note [reducible non-instances].

explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Nonempty.intro: If there exists an element of a type, then that type is considered nonempty.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.
explanatories.AddMonoidHom.map_zero: An additive monoid homomorphism maps the zero element of one additive monoid to the zero element of another.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.LinearIsometryEquiv.symm: This definition establishes the inverse of a linear isometry equivalence, enabling a bijection between two seminormed vector spaces that preserves their respective structures when reversed.
explanatories.orthogonalProjection: The orthogonal projection is a linear map that takes a point from an inner product space to its closest point in a complete subspace.
explanatories.LinearIsometryEquiv.apply_symm_apply: This theorem asserts that applying a linear isometry equivalence's inverse to an element in its codomain and then mapping it back yields the original element, confirming the isometry's bijective nature.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.left_inv: This theorem establishes that the inverse function of a linear equivalence acts as a left inverse to the underlying linear map.
explanatories.Submodule.IsOrtho.symm: If two submodules are orthogonal to each other, then they are also orthogonal in reverse.
explanatories.iSup: A function that calculates the supremum of a collection of elements indexed by another set within a framework of ordered structures.
explanatories.True.intro: The statement establishes that the proposition of truth is inherently valid, with a specific proof confirming its truth.
explanatories.DecidableEq: A type is said to have decidable equality if it is possible to determine whether any two elements of that type are equal.
explanatories.Ne.symm: If two elements are not equal to each other, then reversing their order also indicates that they are not equal.
explanatories.map_zero: This theorem asserts a property about a type of morphism that maintains the identity element across two algebraic structures with defined identity elements.
explanatories.OrthogonalFamily.sum_projection_of_mem_i: If a vector belongs to the supremum of an orthogonal family of subspaces, it can be represented as the sum of its projections onto each of those subspaces.
explanatories.DirectSum.coeAddMonoidHom: This definition establishes a canonical additive homomorphism that maps elements from the direct sum of a collection of submonoids into a larger additive commutative monoid.
explanatories.OrthogonalFamily.projection_directSum_co: For an orthogonal family of submodules, the orthogonal projection of a direct sum element onto a specific submodule returns the corresponding component of that element.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.Classical.decEq: This definition asserts that any type has a mechanism for determining equality between its elements in a classical framework.
explanatories.DirectSum.toAddMonoid: This definition describes a natural homomorphism from the direct sum of a family of additive commutative monoids to another additive commutative monoid, which is induced by a collection of homomorphisms from each monoid to the target.
explanatories.DFinsupp.liftAddHom_apply: This definition establishes a bijective correspondence between additive homomorphisms from dependent functions and those from finitely supported functions, under certain conditions.
explanatories.DFinsupp.sumAddHom_apply: This theorem states that applying a sum homomorphism to a finitely supported function produces the same result as summing the mapped values of that function using the homomorphism.
explanatories.DFinsupp.sum_eq_sum_fintype: This theorem establishes that the product of a finitely supported function applied to a mapping is equal to the product of the mapping evaluated at each index in a finite type, under specified conditions for zero values.
explanatories.Equiv.apply_symm_apply: This theorem demonstrates that applying an equivalence and then its inverse to an element returns the original element.
explanatories.AddSubmonoidClass.coe_subtype: The inclusion function for the submonoid associated with a subtype of an additive structure corresponds to the underlying value function of the subtype.
explanatories.Eq.ge: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if two elements are equal, then one is less than or equal to the other.
explanatories.Submodule.mem_top: This theorem states that every element of a module is a member of the entire module itself.
explanatories.DFinsupp.equivFunOnFintype_symm_coe: This theorem asserts that the inverse of the equivalence between functions on a finite type and their corresponding finitely supported functions is equal to the original finitely supported function itself.

OrthogonalFamily.decomposition.fullDefinition: abbrev OrthogonalFamily.decomposition [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι] {V : ι → Submodule 𝕜 E}     [∀ i, CompleteSpace (V i)] (hV : OrthogonalFamily 𝕜 (fun i => V i) fun i => (V i).subtypeₗᵢ)     (h : iSup V = ⊤) : DirectSum.Decomposition V where   decompose' x := DFinsupp.equivFunOnFintype.symm fun i => orthogonalProjection (V i) x   left_inv x := by     dsimp only     letI := fun i => Classical.decEq (V i)     rw [DirectSum.coeAddMonoidHom, DirectSum.toAddMonoid, DFinsupp.liftAddHom_apply]     -- This used to be `rw`, but we need `erw` after leanprover/lean4#2644     erw [DFinsupp.sumAddHom_apply]; rw [DFinsupp.sum_eq_sum_fintype]     · simp_rw [Equiv.apply_symm_apply, AddSubmonoidClass.coe_subtype]       exact hV.sum_projection_of_mem_iSup _ ((h.ge : _) Submodule.mem_top)     · intro i       exact map_zero _   right_inv x := by     dsimp only     simp_rw [hV.projection_directSum_coeAddHom, DFinsupp.equivFunOnFintype_symm_coe]
OrthogonalFamily.decomposition.description: An orthogonal family of submodules that spans the entire space allows the decomposition of vectors within that space into components corresponding to each of the submodules.

orthogonal_family.decomposition.code:
OrthogonalFamily.decomposition.{u_1, u_2, u_4} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [_root_.RCLike 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] {ι : Type u_4} [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι] {V : ι → Submodule 𝕜 E}
  [∀ (i : ι), CompleteSpace ↥(V i)] (hV : OrthogonalFamily 𝕜 (fun i => ↥(V i)) fun i => (V i).subtypeₗᵢ)
  (h : iSup V = ⊤) : Decomposition V
orthogonal_family.decomposition.comment:
If a family of submodules is orthogonal and they span the whole space, then the orthogonal
projection provides a means to decompose the space into its submodules.

The projection function is `decompose V x i = orthogonalProjection (V i) x`.

See note [reducible non-instances].

explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Nonempty.intro: If there exists an element of a type, then that type is considered nonempty.
explanatories.Iff.intro: Two propositions are equivalent if one implies the other in both directions.
explanatories.AddMonoidHom.map_zero: An additive monoid homomorphism maps the zero element of one additive monoid to the zero element of another.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.LinearIsometryEquiv.symm: This definition establishes the inverse of a linear isometry equivalence, enabling a bijection between two seminormed vector spaces that preserves their respective structures when reversed.
explanatories.orthogonalProjection: The orthogonal projection is a linear map that takes a point from an inner product space to its closest point in a complete subspace.
explanatories.LinearIsometryEquiv.apply_symm_apply: This theorem asserts that applying a linear isometry equivalence's inverse to an element in its codomain and then mapping it back yields the original element, confirming the isometry's bijective nature.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.left_inv: This theorem establishes that the inverse function of a linear equivalence acts as a left inverse to the underlying linear map.
explanatories.Submodule.IsOrtho.symm: If two submodules are orthogonal to each other, then they are also orthogonal in reverse.
explanatories.iSup: A function that calculates the supremum of a collection of elements indexed by another set within a framework of ordered structures.
explanatories.True.intro: The statement establishes that the proposition of truth is inherently valid, with a specific proof confirming its truth.
explanatories.DecidableEq: A type is said to have decidable equality if it is possible to determine whether any two elements of that type are equal.
explanatories.Ne.symm: If two elements are not equal to each other, then reversing their order also indicates that they are not equal.
explanatories.map_zero: This theorem asserts a property about a type of morphism that maintains the identity element across two algebraic structures with defined identity elements.
explanatories.OrthogonalFamily.sum_projection_of_mem_i: If a vector belongs to the supremum of an orthogonal family of subspaces, it can be represented as the sum of its projections onto each of those subspaces.
explanatories.DirectSum.coeAddMonoidHom: This definition establishes a canonical additive homomorphism that maps elements from the direct sum of a collection of submonoids into a larger additive commutative monoid.
explanatories.OrthogonalFamily.projection_directSum_co: For an orthogonal family of submodules, the orthogonal projection of a direct sum element onto a specific submodule returns the corresponding component of that element.
explanatories.Equiv.symm: This definition describes the operation that produces the inverse equivalence relation from a given equivalence relation between two types.
explanatories.Classical.decEq: This definition asserts that any type has a mechanism for determining equality between its elements in a classical framework.
explanatories.DirectSum.toAddMonoid: This definition describes a natural homomorphism from the direct sum of a family of additive commutative monoids to another additive commutative monoid, which is induced by a collection of homomorphisms from each monoid to the target.
explanatories.DFinsupp.liftAddHom_apply: This definition establishes a bijective correspondence between additive homomorphisms from dependent functions and those from finitely supported functions, under certain conditions.
explanatories.DFinsupp.sumAddHom_apply: This theorem states that applying a sum homomorphism to a finitely supported function produces the same result as summing the mapped values of that function using the homomorphism.
explanatories.DFinsupp.sum_eq_sum_fintype: This theorem establishes that the product of a finitely supported function applied to a mapping is equal to the product of the mapping evaluated at each index in a finite type, under specified conditions for zero values.
explanatories.Equiv.apply_symm_apply: This theorem demonstrates that applying an equivalence and then its inverse to an element returns the original element.
explanatories.AddSubmonoidClass.coe_subtype: The inclusion function for the submonoid associated with a subtype of an additive structure corresponds to the underlying value function of the subtype.
explanatories.Eq.ge: A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if two elements are equal, then one is less than or equal to the other.
explanatories.Submodule.mem_top: This theorem states that every element of a module is a member of the entire module itself.
explanatories.DFinsupp.equivFunOnFintype_symm_coe: This theorem asserts that the inverse of the equivalence between functions on a finite type and their corresponding finitely supported functions is equal to the original finitely supported function itself.

orthogonal_family.decomposition.fullDefinition: abbrev OrthogonalFamily.decomposition [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι] {V : ι → Submodule 𝕜 E}     [∀ i, CompleteSpace (V i)] (hV : OrthogonalFamily 𝕜 (fun i => V i) fun i => (V i).subtypeₗᵢ)     (h : iSup V = ⊤) : DirectSum.Decomposition V where   decompose' x := DFinsupp.equivFunOnFintype.symm fun i => orthogonalProjection (V i) x   left_inv x := by     dsimp only     letI := fun i => Classical.decEq (V i)     rw [DirectSum.coeAddMonoidHom, DirectSum.toAddMonoid, DFinsupp.liftAddHom_apply]     -- This used to be `rw`, but we need `erw` after leanprover/lean4#2644     erw [DFinsupp.sumAddHom_apply]; rw [DFinsupp.sum_eq_sum_fintype]     · simp_rw [Equiv.apply_symm_apply, AddSubmonoidClass.coe_subtype]       exact hV.sum_projection_of_mem_iSup _ ((h.ge : _) Submodule.mem_top)     · intro i       exact map_zero _   right_inv x := by     dsimp only     simp_rw [hV.projection_directSum_coeAddHom, DFinsupp.equivFunOnFintype_symm_coe]
orthogonal_family.decomposition.description: An orthogonal family of submodules that spans the entire space allows the decomposition of vectors within that space into components corresponding to each of the submodules.

complement of its span is empty.

LinearMap.tendsto_birkhoffAverage_of_ker.code:
LinearMap.tendsto_birkhoffAverage_of_ker_subset_closure.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [RCLike 𝕜]
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] (f : E →ₗ[𝕜] E) (hf : LipschitzWith 1 ⇑f)
  (g : E →L[𝕜] ↥(LinearMap.eqLocus f 1)) (hg_proj : ∀ (x : ↥(LinearMap.eqLocus f 1)), g ↑x = x)
  (hg_ker : ↑(LinearMap.ker g) ⊆ closure ↑(LinearMap.range (f - 1))) (x : E) :
  Tendsto (fun x_1 => birkhoffAverage 𝕜 (⇑f) _root_.id x_1 x) atTop (𝓝 ↑(g x))
LinearMap.tendsto_birkhoffAverage_of_ker.comment:
**Von Neumann Mean Ergodic Theorem**, a version for a normed space.

Let `f : E → E` be a contracting linear self-map of a normed space.
Let `S` be the subspace of fixed points of `f`.
Let `g : E → S` be a continuous linear projection, `g|_S=id`.
If the range of `f - id` is dense in the kernel of `g`,
then for each `x`, the Birkhoff averages
```
birkhoffAverage 𝕜 f id N x = (N : 𝕜)⁻¹ • ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, f^[n] x
```
converge to `g x` as `N → ∞`.

Usually, this fact is not formulated as a separate lemma.
I chose to do it in order to isolate parts of the proof that do not rely
on the inner product space structure.

explanatories.RingHom.id: This definition describes the identity ring homomorphism that maps each element of a semiring to itself.
explanatories.LipschitzWith: A function is Lipschitz continuous with a non-negative constant if the distance between its outputs is bounded by the constant multiplied by the distance between its inputs.
explanatories.LinearMap.eqLocus: This definition describes the set of elements in a module that are mapped to the same value by two given linear maps.
explanatories.LinearMap.ker: The kernel of a linear map is defined as the set of elements in the domain that are mapped to zero in the codomain, and it forms a submodule of the domain.
explanatories.LinearMap.range: This definition states that the range of a linear map between modules is a submodule of the codomain module.
explanatories.Filter.Tendsto: A definition stating that a function converges from one filter to another if the preimage of every neighborhood in the second filter is a neighborhood in the first filter.
explanatories.id: The identity function returns its input unchanged and can be used to explicitly assign a type to an expression for typeclass inference purposes.
explanatories.Filter.atTop: This definition introduces a filter that captures the behavior of elements approaching infinity in an ordered set, generated by all sets containing elements greater than or equal to any given element.
explanatories.Set.range: The range of a function consists of all values that can be obtained by applying the function to elements in its domain.

LinearMap.tendsto_birkhoffAverage_of_ker.description: This theorem establishes that for a contracting linear map in a normed space with a specific projection and dense range conditions, the Birkhoff averages converge to the projection of a point as the number of averages increases.

InnerProductSpace.toDualMap.code:
InnerProductSpace.toDualMap.{u_1, u_2} (𝕜 : Type u_1) (E : Type u_2) [RCLike 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] : E →ₗᵢ⋆[𝕜] NormedSpace.Dual 𝕜 E
InnerProductSpace.toDualMap.comment:
An element `x` of an inner product space `E` induces an element of the dual space `Dual 𝕜 E`,
the map `fun y => ⟪x, y⟫`; moreover this operation is a conjugate-linear isometric embedding of `E`
into `Dual 𝕜 E`.
If `E` is complete, this operation is surjective, hence a conjugate-linear isometric equivalence;
see `toDual`.

InnerProductSpace.toDualMap.description: This definition describes a mapping from an inner product space to its dual space, which is a conjugate-linear isometric embedding of the space into the dual.

InnerProductSpace.toDual.code:
InnerProductSpace.toDual.{u_1, u_2} (𝕜 : Type u_1) (E : Type u_2) [RCLike 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] [CompleteSpace E] : E ≃ₗᵢ⋆[𝕜] NormedSpace.Dual 𝕜 E
InnerProductSpace.toDual.comment:
Fréchet-Riesz representation: any `ℓ` in the dual of a Hilbert space `E` is of the form
`fun u => ⟪y, u⟫` for some `y : E`, i.e. `toDualMap` is surjective.

explanatories.NormedSpace.Dual: This definition describes the topological dual of a seminormed space.
explanatories.Iff.mp: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.coe_injective: The function that converts continuous linear maps to linear maps is injective, meaning distinct continuous linear maps correspond to distinct linear maps.
explanatories.Basis.ext: This theorem asserts that two linear maps are identical if they produce the same output for every basis vector.
explanatories.LinearIsometryEquiv.ofSurjective: This definition formulates the construction of a linear isometry equivalence from a given surjective linear isometry.
explanatories.LinearMap.ker: The kernel of a linear map is defined as the set of elements in the domain that are mapped to zero in the codomain, and it forms a submodule of the domain.
explanatories.LinearMap.ker_eq_top: The kernel of a linear map is equal to the entire space if and only if the map is the zero map.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.coe_zero: The zero element of a continuous linear map is identified with the zero element in its codomain.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.Submodule.orthogonal_eq_bot_iff: The orthogonal complement of a submodule is trivial if and only if the submodule itself is the entire space.
explanatories.Submodule.ne_bot_iff: This theorem indicates that a submodule is non-trivial if and only if there exists at least one non-zero element within it.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.ext: If two continuous linear maps between topological modules agree on their outputs for all inputs, then they are identical maps.
explanatories.LinearMap.mem_ker: An element belongs to the kernel of a linear map if and only if it is mapped to zero by that linear map.
explanatories.map_sub: The theorem states that additive group homomorphisms maintain the result of subtraction between elements.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.map_smul: The application of a continuous linear map to a scalar multiplied by an element yields the same result as multiplying the image of that element by the scalar.
explanatories.Algebra.id.smul_eq_mul: This theorem establishes that scalar multiplication by an element in a commutative semiring is equivalent to the usual multiplication of that element with another element from the same semiring.
explanatories.mul_comm: This theorem states that multiplication is commutative in a certain algebraic structure, meaning that the product of two elements is the same regardless of their order.
explanatories.sub_self: In an additive group, subtracting an element from itself results in the identity element.
explanatories.Submodule.mem_orthogonal': A vector is in the orthogonal complement of a subspace if and only if it is orthogonal to every vector in that subspace when the inner product is taken in the reverse order.
explanatories.inner_sub_right: This theorem states that the inner product of a vector with the difference of two other vectors is equal to the difference of the inner products of the first vector with each of the two other vectors.
explanatories.inner_smul_right: This theorem states that the inner product of a vector with a scalar multiple of another vector is equal to the scalar multiplied by the inner product of the original vectors.
explanatories.sub_eq_zero: In an additive group, the difference between two elements equals zero if and only if the two elements are equal.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.

InnerProductSpace.toDual.fullDefinition: def toDual : E ≃ₗᵢ⋆[𝕜] NormedSpace.Dual 𝕜 E :=   LinearIsometryEquiv.ofSurjective (toDualMap 𝕜 E)     (by       intro ℓ       set Y := LinearMap.ker ℓ       by_cases htriv : Y = ⊤       · have hℓ : ℓ = 0 := by           have h' := LinearMap.ker_eq_top.mp htriv           rw [← coe_zero] at h'           apply coe_injective           exact h'         exact ⟨0, by simp [hℓ]⟩       · rw [← Submodule.orthogonal_eq_bot_iff] at htriv         change Yᗮ ≠ ⊥ at htriv         rw [Submodule.ne_bot_iff] at htriv         obtain ⟨z : E, hz : z ∈ Yᗮ, z_ne_0 : z ≠ 0⟩ := htriv         refine ⟨(starRingEnd (R := 𝕜) (ℓ z) / ⟪z, z⟫) • z, ?_⟩         apply ContinuousLinearMap.ext         intro x         have h₁ : ℓ z • x - ℓ x • z ∈ Y := by           rw [LinearMap.mem_ker, map_sub, ContinuousLinearMap.map_smul,             ContinuousLinearMap.map_smul, Algebra.id.smul_eq_mul, Algebra.id.smul_eq_mul, mul_comm]           exact sub_self (ℓ x * ℓ z)         have h₂ : ℓ z * ⟪z, x⟫ = ℓ x * ⟪z, z⟫ :=           haveI h₃ :=             calc               0 = ⟪z, ℓ z • x - ℓ x • z⟫ := by                 rw [(Y.mem_orthogonal' z).mp hz]                 exact h₁               _ = ⟪z, ℓ z • x⟫ - ⟪z, ℓ x • z⟫ := by rw [inner_sub_right]               _ = ℓ z * ⟪z, x⟫ - ℓ x * ⟪z, z⟫ := by simp [inner_smul_right]           sub_eq_zero.mp (Eq.symm h₃)         have h₄ :=           calc             ⟪(ℓ z† / ⟪z, z⟫) • z, x⟫ = ℓ z / ⟪z, z⟫ * ⟪z, x⟫ := by simp [inner_smul_left, conj_conj]             _ = ℓ z * ⟪z, x⟫ / ⟪z, z⟫ := by rw [← div_mul_eq_mul_div]             _ = ℓ x * ⟪z, z⟫ / ⟪z, z⟫ := by rw [h₂]             _ = ℓ x := by field_simp [inner_self_ne_zero.2 z_ne_0]         exact h₄)

PiLp.innerProductSpace.fullDefinition: instance PiLp.innerProductSpace {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (f : ι → Type*)     [∀ i, NormedAddCommGroup (f i)] [∀ i, InnerProductSpace 𝕜 (f i)] :     InnerProductSpace 𝕜 (PiLp 2 f) where   inner x y := ∑ i, inner (x i) (y i)   norm_sq_eq_inner x := by     simp only [PiLp.norm_sq_eq_of_L2, map_sum, ← norm_sq_eq_inner, one_div]   conj_symm := by     intro x y     unfold inner     rw [map_sum]     apply Finset.sum_congr rfl     rintro z -     apply inner_conj_symm   add_left x y z :=     show (∑ i, inner (x i + y i) (z i)) = (∑ i, inner (x i) (z i)) + ∑ i, inner (y i) (z i) by       simp only [inner_add_left, Finset.sum_add_distrib]   smul_left x y r :=     show (∑ i : ι, inner (r • x i) (y i)) = conj r * ∑ i, inner (x i) (y i) by       simp only [Finset.mul_sum, inner_smul_left]

pi_Lp.inner_product_space.fullDefinition: instance PiLp.innerProductSpace {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (f : ι → Type*)     [∀ i, NormedAddCommGroup (f i)] [∀ i, InnerProductSpace 𝕜 (f i)] :     InnerProductSpace 𝕜 (PiLp 2 f) where   inner x y := ∑ i, inner (x i) (y i)   norm_sq_eq_inner x := by     simp only [PiLp.norm_sq_eq_of_L2, map_sum, ← norm_sq_eq_inner, one_div]   conj_symm := by     intro x y     unfold inner     rw [map_sum]     apply Finset.sum_congr rfl     rintro z -     apply inner_conj_symm   add_left x y z :=     show (∑ i, inner (x i + y i) (z i)) = (∑ i, inner (x i) (z i)) + ∑ i, inner (y i) (z i) by       simp only [inner_add_left, Finset.sum_add_distrib]   smul_left x y r :=     show (∑ i : ι, inner (r • x i) (y i)) = conj r * ∑ i, inner (x i) (y i) by       simp only [Finset.mul_sum, inner_smul_left]

DirectSum.IsInternal.isometryL2OfOrthogo.fullDefinition: def DirectSum.IsInternal.isometryL2OfOrthogonalFamily [DecidableEq ι] {V : ι → Submodule 𝕜 E}     (hV : DirectSum.IsInternal V)     (hV' : OrthogonalFamily 𝕜 (fun i => V i) fun i => (V i).subtypeₗᵢ) :     E ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] PiLp 2 fun i => V i := by   let e₁ := DirectSum.linearEquivFunOnFintype 𝕜 ι fun i => V i   let e₂ := LinearEquiv.ofBijective (DirectSum.coeLinearMap V) hV   refine LinearEquiv.isometryOfInner (e₂.symm.trans e₁) ?_   suffices ∀ (v w : PiLp 2 fun i => V i), ⟪v, w⟫ = ⟪e₂ (e₁.symm v), e₂ (e₁.symm w)⟫ by     intro v₀ w₀     convert this (e₁ (e₂.symm v₀)) (e₁ (e₂.symm w₀)) <;>       simp only [LinearEquiv.symm_apply_apply, LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply]   intro v w   trans ⟪∑ i, (V i).subtypeₗᵢ (v i), ∑ i, (V i).subtypeₗᵢ (w i)⟫   · simp only [sum_inner, hV'.inner_right_fintype, PiLp.inner_apply]   · congr <;> simp

explanatories.OrthogonalFamily.inner_right_fintype: This theorem demonstrates that for a finite orthogonal family of vectors in inner product spaces, the inner product of a specific vector with the sum of projections onto the family equals the inner product of that vector with itself when evaluated at the corresponding basis element.
explanatories.LinearIsometryEquiv.symm: This definition establishes the inverse of a linear isometry equivalence, enabling a bijection between two seminormed vector spaces that preserves their respective structures when reversed.
explanatories.True.intro: The statement establishes that the proposition of truth is inherently valid, with a specific proof confirming its truth.
explanatories.LinearIsometryEquiv.apply_symm_apply: This theorem asserts that applying a linear isometry equivalence's inverse to an element in its codomain and then mapping it back yields the original element, confirming the isometry's bijective nature.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.LinearIsometryEquiv.trans: This definition describes how to construct a new linear isometric equivalence between two seminormed modules by composing two existing linear isometric equivalences.
explanatories.Orthonormal.inner_right_fintype: This theorem states that the inner product of a linear combination of orthonormal vectors with one of those vectors yields the coefficient associated with that vector in the combination.
explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.Eq.trans: If one element is equal to a second, and that second is equal to a third, then the first element is also equal to the third, demonstrating the transitive property of equality.

direct_sum.is_internal.isometry_L2_of_or.fullDefinition: def DirectSum.IsInternal.isometryL2OfOrthogonalFamily [DecidableEq ι] {V : ι → Submodule 𝕜 E}     (hV : DirectSum.IsInternal V)     (hV' : OrthogonalFamily 𝕜 (fun i => V i) fun i => (V i).subtypeₗᵢ) :     E ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] PiLp 2 fun i => V i := by   let e₁ := DirectSum.linearEquivFunOnFintype 𝕜 ι fun i => V i   let e₂ := LinearEquiv.ofBijective (DirectSum.coeLinearMap V) hV   refine LinearEquiv.isometryOfInner (e₂.symm.trans e₁) ?_   suffices ∀ (v w : PiLp 2 fun i => V i), ⟪v, w⟫ = ⟪e₂ (e₁.symm v), e₂ (e₁.symm w)⟫ by     intro v₀ w₀     convert this (e₁ (e₂.symm v₀)) (e₁ (e₂.symm w₀)) <;>       simp only [LinearEquiv.symm_apply_apply, LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply]   intro v w   trans ⟪∑ i, (V i).subtypeₗᵢ (v i), ∑ i, (V i).subtypeₗᵢ (w i)⟫   · simp only [sum_inner, hV'.inner_right_fintype, PiLp.inner_apply]   · congr <;> simp
direct_sum.is_internal.isometry_L2_of_or.description: This definition asserts that a finite collection of mutually orthogonal subspaces that span a vector space induces an isometric isomorphism between that vector space and a product space structured by the L² inner product on those subspaces.

DirectSum.IsInternal.isometryL2OfOrthogonalFamily_symm_apply.{u_1, u_3, u_4} {ι : Type u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_3}
  [_root_.RCLike 𝕜] {E : Type u_4} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
  {V : ι → Submodule 𝕜 E} (hV : IsInternal V) (hV' : OrthogonalFamily 𝕜 (fun i => ↥(V i)) fun i => (V i).subtypeₗᵢ)
  (w : PiLp 2 fun i => ↥(V i)) : (hV.isometryL2OfOrthogonalFamily hV').symm w = ∑ i : ι, ↑(w i)

LinearIsometry.extend.fullDefinition: noncomputable def LinearIsometry.extend (L : S →ₗᵢ[𝕜] V) : V →ₗᵢ[𝕜] V := by   -- Build an isometry from Sᗮ to L(S)ᗮ through `EuclideanSpace`   let d := finrank 𝕜 Sᗮ   let LS := LinearMap.range L.toLinearMap   have E : Sᗮ ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] LSᗮ := by     have dim_LS_perp : finrank 𝕜 LSᗮ = d :=       calc         finrank 𝕜 LSᗮ = finrank 𝕜 V - finrank 𝕜 LS := by           simp only [← LS.finrank_add_finrank_orthogonal, add_tsub_cancel_left]         _ = finrank 𝕜 V - finrank 𝕜 S := by simp only [LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj L.injective]         _ = finrank 𝕜 Sᗮ := by simp only [← S.finrank_add_finrank_orthogonal, add_tsub_cancel_left]

explanatories.Basis.map: This definition introduces a new basis for a module formed by applying a given linear equivalence to the original basis vectors.

explanatories.norm_eq_sqrt_inner: This theorem states that the norm of a vector is equal to the square root of the real part of its inner product with itself.

explanatories.OrthonormalBasis.orthonormal: This theorem states that a given orthonormal basis establishes an orthonormal set in the corresponding inner product space.

explanatories.ne_eq: The theorem demonstrates that the inequality of two elements is equivalent to the negation of their equality.
explanatories.Basis.map_apply: This theorem states that the application of a linear isomorphism to a basis vector can be computed by applying the isomorphism directly to the representation of that basis vector.
explanatories.Basis.prod_apply: This theorem establishes that for a product of two bases, the evaluation at a direct sum index can be expressed as a combination of the evaluations from each individual basis transformed by corresponding linear maps.

explanatories.Function.comp_apply: The composition of two functions applied to an argument is equal to applying the first function to the result of applying the second function to that argument.
explanatories.inner_zero_right: This theorem states that the inner product of any vector with the zero vector in an inner product space is zero.
explanatories.add_zero: This theorem states that in any additive structure with a zero element, adding zero to any element results in that same element.
explanatories.zero_add: This theorem establishes that adding zero to any element in an additive structure results in that same element.
explanatories.Sum.inl.injEq: The equality of two left injections is equivalent to the equality of their respective values.
explanatories.not_false_eq_true: The theorem states that the negation of a false proposition is equivalent to a true proposition.
explanatories.inner_zero_left: This theorem states that the inner product of the zero vector with any other vector is zero.
explanatories.forall_true_left: This theorem states that for any property dependent on a true proposition, it is equivalent to asserting that the property holds for the specific instance of true.
explanatories.implies_true: The theorem shows that any implication from a type to a true proposition is itself equivalent to true.
explanatories.and_true: The theorem asserts that the conjunction of any proposition with a true proposition is equivalent to the original proposition itself.
explanatories.Sum.inr.injEq: The equality of two elements in the right summand of a sum type is equivalent to the equality of the elements themselves.
explanatories.true_and: The theorem demonstrates that the conjunction of a true proposition and any other proposition is equivalent to the other proposition itself.

OrthonormalBasis.prod.fullDefinition: def prod (v : OrthonormalBasis ι₁ 𝕜 E) (w : OrthonormalBasis ι₂ 𝕜 F) :     OrthonormalBasis (ι₁ ⊕ ι₂) 𝕜 (WithLp 2 (E × F)) :=   ((v.toBasis.prod w.toBasis).map (WithLp.linearEquiv 2 𝕜 (E × F)).symm).toOrthonormalBasis   (by     constructor     · simp only [Sum.forall, norm_eq_sqrt_inner (𝕜 := 𝕜), Real.sqrt_eq_one]       simp [← Real.sqrt_eq_one, ← norm_eq_sqrt_inner (𝕜 := 𝕜), v.orthonormal.1, w.orthonormal.1]     · unfold Pairwise       simp only [ne_eq, Basis.map_apply, Basis.prod_apply, LinearMap.coe_inl,         OrthonormalBasis.coe_toBasis, LinearMap.coe_inr, WithLp.linearEquiv_symm_apply,         WithLp.prod_inner_apply, WithLp.equiv_symm_fst, WithLp.equiv_symm_snd, Sum.forall,         Sum.elim_inl, Function.comp_apply, inner_zero_right, add_zero, Sum.elim_inr, zero_add,         Sum.inl.injEq, not_false_eq_true, inner_zero_left, forall_true_left, implies_true, and_true,         Sum.inr.injEq, true_and]       exact ⟨v.orthonormal.2, w.orthonormal.2⟩)
OrthonormalBasis.prod.description: The definition describes how the product of two orthonormal bases results in a new orthonormal basis for the L2-space of the product of two vector spaces.

OrthogonalFamily.linearIsometry.fullDefinition: protected def linearIsometry : lp G 2 →ₗᵢ[𝕜] E where   toFun f := ∑' i, V i (f i)   map_add' f g := by     simp only [tsum_add (hV.summable_of_lp f) (hV.summable_of_lp g), lp.coeFn_add, Pi.add_apply,       LinearIsometry.map_add]   map_smul' c f := by     simpa only [LinearIsometry.map_smul, Pi.smul_apply, lp.coeFn_smul] using       tsum_const_smul c (hV.summable_of_lp f)   norm_map' f := by     classical       -- needed for lattice instance on `Finset ι`, for `Filter.atTop_neBot`       have H : 0 < (2 : ℝ≥0∞).toReal := by norm_num       suffices ‖∑' i : ι, V i (f i)‖ ^ (2 : ℝ≥0∞).toReal = ‖f‖ ^ (2 : ℝ≥0∞).toReal by         exact Real.rpow_left_injOn H.ne' (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _) this       refine tendsto_nhds_unique ?_ (lp.hasSum_norm H f)       convert (hV.summable_of_lp f).hasSum.norm.rpow_const (Or.inr H.le) using 1       ext s       exact mod_cast (hV.norm_sum f s).symm

IsHilbertSum.mk.code:
IsHilbertSum.mk.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {ι : Type u_1} {𝕜 : Type u_2} [RCLike 𝕜] {E : Type u_3} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] [cplt : CompleteSpace E] {G : ι → Type u_4} [(i : ι) → NormedAddCommGroup (G i)]
  [(i : ι) → InnerProductSpace 𝕜 (G i)] {V : (i : ι) → G i →ₗᵢ[𝕜] E} [∀ (i : ι), CompleteSpace (G i)]
  (hVortho : OrthogonalFamily 𝕜 G V) (hVtotal : ⊤ ≤ (⨆ i, LinearMap.range (V i).toLinearMap).topologicalClosure) :
  IsHilbertSum 𝕜 G V
IsHilbertSum.mk.comment:
If `V : Π i, G i →ₗᵢ[𝕜] E` is an orthogonal family such that the supremum of the ranges of
`V i` is dense, then `(E, V)` is a Hilbert sum of `G`.

unitary.linearIsometryEquiv.fullDefinition: noncomputable def linearIsometryEquiv : unitary (H →L[𝕜] H) ≃* (H ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] H) where   toFun u :=     { (u : H →L[𝕜] H) with       norm_map' := norm_map u       invFun := ↑(star u)       left_inv := fun x ↦ congr($(star_mul_self u).val x)       right_inv := fun x ↦ congr($(mul_star_self u).val x) }   invFun e :=     { val := e       property := by         let e' : (H →L[𝕜] H)ˣ :=           { val := (e : H →L[𝕜] H)             inv := (e.symm : H →L[𝕜] H)             val_inv := by ext; simp             inv_val := by ext; simp }         exact IsUnit.mem_unitary_of_star_mul_self ⟨e', rfl⟩ <|           (e : H →L[𝕜] H).norm_map_iff_adjoint_comp_self.mp e.norm_map }   left_inv u := Subtype.ext rfl   right_inv e := LinearIsometryEquiv.ext fun x ↦ rfl   map_mul' u v := by ext; rfl

An operator `T` is a formal adjoint of `S` if for all `x` in the domain of `T` and `y` in the
domain of `S`, we have that `⟪T x, y⟫ = ⟪x, S y⟫`.

explanatories.Submodule.coe_smul_of_tower: This theorem asserts that when an element from a submodule is scaled by a scalar from a larger structure that acts as a scalar tower, the result remains consistent when viewed in both the submodule and the original module.
explanatories.RingHom.id_apply: This theorem states that the identity ring homomorphism returns any element from the semiring unchanged.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.

and `∀ x, 0 ≤ re ⟪T x, x⟫`.

explanatories.le_antisymm: This theorem establishes that in a partial order, if one element is less than or equal to another and vice versa, then the two elements must be equal.
explanatories.eq_or_lt_of_le: A theorem stating that in a partially ordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to another, then it is either equal to or strictly less than the other.
explanatories.norm_nonneg: This theorem asserts that the norm of any element in a seminormed group is non-negative.
explanatories.le_of_mul_le_mul_right: This theorem states that if the product of two terms with a positive element on the right is less than or equal to the product of another two terms, then the first term is less than or equal to the second term.
explanatories.real_inner_self_eq_norm_mul_norm: This theorem states that in a real inner product space, the inner product of a vector with itself equals the square of its norm.

explanatories.Iff.mp: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.Submodule.coe_eq_zero: This theorem establishes that an element in a submodule is zero if and only if its representative in the module is also zero.
explanatories.norm_pos_iff: This theorem establishes that the norm of an element in a normed group is positive if and only if the element is not equal to the identity.
explanatories.abs_real_inner_le_norm: This theorem states that the absolute value of the inner product of two vectors in a real inner product space is less than or equal to the product of their norms, demonstrating the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality.

Orientation.rightAngleRotationAux₂.fullDefinition: def rightAngleRotationAux₂ : E →ₗᵢ[ℝ] E :=   { o.rightAngleRotationAux₁ with     norm_map' := fun x => by       dsimp       refine le_antisymm ?_ ?_       · cases' eq_or_lt_of_le (norm_nonneg (o.rightAngleRotationAux₁ x)) with h h         · rw [← h]           positivity         refine le_of_mul_le_mul_right ?_ h         rw [← real_inner_self_eq_norm_mul_norm, o.inner_rightAngleRotationAux₁_left]         exact o.areaForm_le x (o.rightAngleRotationAux₁ x)       · let K : Submodule ℝ E := ℝ ∙ x         have : Nontrivial Kᗮ := by           apply @FiniteDimensional.nontrivial_of_finrank_pos ℝ           have : finrank ℝ K ≤ Finset.card {x} := by             rw [← Set.toFinset_singleton]             exact finrank_span_le_card ({x} : Set E)           have : Finset.card {x} = 1 := Finset.card_singleton x           have : finrank ℝ K + finrank ℝ Kᗮ = finrank ℝ E := K.finrank_add_finrank_orthogonal           have : finrank ℝ E = 2 := Fact.out           linarith         obtain ⟨w, hw₀⟩ : ∃ w : Kᗮ, w ≠ 0 := exists_ne 0         have hw' : ⟪x, (w : E)⟫ = 0 := Submodule.mem_orthogonal_singleton_iff_inner_right.mp w.2         have hw : (w : E) ≠ 0 := fun h => hw₀ (Submodule.coe_eq_zero.mp h)         refine le_of_mul_le_mul_right ?_ (by rwa [norm_pos_iff] : 0 < ‖(w : E)‖)         rw [← o.abs_areaForm_of_orthogonal hw']         rw [← o.inner_rightAngleRotationAux₁_left x w]         exact abs_real_inner_le_norm (o.rightAngleRotationAux₁ x) w }

orientation.right_angle_rotation_aux₂.fullDefinition: def rightAngleRotationAux₂ : E →ₗᵢ[ℝ] E :=   { o.rightAngleRotationAux₁ with     norm_map' := fun x => by       dsimp       refine le_antisymm ?_ ?_       · cases' eq_or_lt_of_le (norm_nonneg (o.rightAngleRotationAux₁ x)) with h h         · rw [← h]           positivity         refine le_of_mul_le_mul_right ?_ h         rw [← real_inner_self_eq_norm_mul_norm, o.inner_rightAngleRotationAux₁_left]         exact o.areaForm_le x (o.rightAngleRotationAux₁ x)       · let K : Submodule ℝ E := ℝ ∙ x         have : Nontrivial Kᗮ := by           apply @FiniteDimensional.nontrivial_of_finrank_pos ℝ           have : finrank ℝ K ≤ Finset.card {x} := by             rw [← Set.toFinset_singleton]             exact finrank_span_le_card ({x} : Set E)           have : Finset.card {x} = 1 := Finset.card_singleton x           have : finrank ℝ K + finrank ℝ Kᗮ = finrank ℝ E := K.finrank_add_finrank_orthogonal           have : finrank ℝ E = 2 := Fact.out           linarith         obtain ⟨w, hw₀⟩ : ∃ w : Kᗮ, w ≠ 0 := exists_ne 0         have hw' : ⟪x, (w : E)⟫ = 0 := Submodule.mem_orthogonal_singleton_iff_inner_right.mp w.2         have hw : (w : E) ≠ 0 := fun h => hw₀ (Submodule.coe_eq_zero.mp h)         refine le_of_mul_le_mul_right ?_ (by rwa [norm_pos_iff] : 0 < ‖(w : E)‖)         rw [← o.abs_areaForm_of_orthogonal hw']         rw [← o.inner_rightAngleRotationAux₁_left x w]         exact abs_real_inner_le_norm (o.rightAngleRotationAux₁ x) w }

explanatories.LinearEquiv.symm: This definition specifies the symmetry of linear equivalences, indicating that the inverse relationship between two modules can be expressed as a linear equivalence in the opposite direction.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.LinearIsometryEquiv.symm: This definition establishes the inverse of a linear isometry equivalence, enabling a bijection between two seminormed vector spaces that preserves their respective structures when reversed.
explanatories.LinearEquiv.trans: This definition establishes that if there are two linear equivalences between three modules with corresponding ring homomorphisms, then there exists a direct linear equivalence between the first and last modules.
explanatories.LinearIsometryEquiv.trans: This definition describes how to construct a new linear isometric equivalence between two seminormed modules by composing two existing linear isometric equivalences.
explanatories.LinearIsometryEquiv.neg: This definition specifies the negation operation on a normed space as a linear isometry equivalence from the space to itself.

Orientation.kahler.comment:
A complex-valued real-bilinear map on an oriented real inner product space of dimension 2. Its
real part is the inner product and its imaginary part is `Orientation.areaForm`.

On `ℂ` with the standard orientation, `kahler w z = conj w * z`; see `Complex.kahler`.

explanatories.LinearMap.lsmul: This definition describes a bilinear map that represents scalar multiplication, taking a scalar from a commutative semiring and an element from a module to produce a resulting element in the module.
explanatories.LinearMap.flip: This definition describes a process that takes a bilinear map and rearranges the order of its variables to form a new linear map.
explanatories.Complex.inner: This theorem states that the inner product of two complex numbers equals the real part of their product.

toEuclidean.comment:
If `E` is a finite dimensional space over `ℝ`, then `toEuclidean` is a continuous `ℝ`-linear
equivalence between `E` and the Euclidean space of the same dimension.

explanatories.EuclideanSpace: This definition describes the standard Euclidean space over either real or complex numbers, parameterized by the dimension represented as a finite type.
explanatories.FiniteDimensional.finrank: The finite rank of a module is defined as a natural number representing its rank, which is considered to be zero when the module has infinite rank.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearEquiv.ofFinrankEq: This definition describes a continuous linear equivalence between two finite-dimensional topological vector spaces over a complete normed field when they have the same finite dimension.
explanatories.finrank_euclideanSpace_fin: This theorem reveals that the finite dimension of a Euclidean space over a given field is equal to the dimension defined by a natural number.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearEquiv.symm: The inverse of a continuous linear equivalence between two modules also forms a continuous linear equivalence between those modules.

toEuclidean.description: This definition establishes a continuous linear equivalence between any finite-dimensional real vector space and a corresponding Euclidean space of the same dimension.

ContinuousLinearMap.rayleighQuotient.comment:
The *Rayleigh quotient* of a continuous linear map `T` (over `ℝ` or `ℂ`) at a vector `x` is
the quantity `re ⟪T x, x⟫ / ‖x‖ ^ 2`.

explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.reApplyInnerSelf: This definition describes a method for extracting a real-valued bilinear form from a linear operator by taking the real part of the inner product between the result of the operator applied to a vector and the vector itself.

ContinuousLinearMap.rayleighQuotient.fullDefinition: noncomputable abbrev rayleighQuotient (x : E) := T.reApplyInnerSelf x / ‖(x : E)‖ ^ 2
ContinuousLinearMap.rayleighQuotient.description: This definition describes the Rayleigh quotient associated with a continuous linear map, which is the ratio of the real part of the inner product of the transformed vector and the original vector to the square of the norm of the original vector.

LinearMap.IsSymmetric.directSumDecomposi.code:
LinearMap.IsSymmetric.directSumDecomposition.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [RCLike 𝕜] {E : Type u_2} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] {T : E →ₗ[𝕜] E} [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 E] [hT : Fact T.IsSymmetric] :
  DirectSum.Decomposition fun μ => eigenspace T (↑T μ)
LinearMap.IsSymmetric.directSumDecomposi.comment:
The eigenspaces of a self-adjoint operator on a finite-dimensional inner product space `E` gives
an internal direct sum decomposition of `E`.

Note this takes `hT` as a `Fact` to allow it to be an instance.

explanatories.Module.End.eigenspace: This definition describes the eigenspace associated with a linear map and a scalar, comprising all vectors that are scaled by the scalar when the map is applied to them.

explanatories.Fact.out: This theorem asserts that the property represented by a fact can be retrieved from its corresponding instance.
explanatories.OrthogonalFamily.decomposition: An orthogonal family of submodules that spans the entire space allows the decomposition of vectors within that space into components corresponding to each of the submodules.
explanatories.Submodule.orthogonal_eq_bot_iff: The orthogonal complement of a submodule is trivial if and only if the submodule itself is the entire space.
explanatories.Iff.mp: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.

LinearMap.IsSymmetric.directSumDecomposi.fullDefinition: noncomputable instance directSumDecomposition [hT : Fact T.IsSymmetric] :     DirectSum.Decomposition fun μ : Eigenvalues T => eigenspace T μ :=   haveI h : ∀ μ : Eigenvalues T, CompleteSpace (eigenspace T μ) := fun μ => by infer_instance   hT.out.orthogonalFamily_eigenspaces'.decomposition     (Submodule.orthogonal_eq_bot_iff.mp hT.out.orthogonalComplement_iSup_eigenspaces_eq_bot')
LinearMap.IsSymmetric.directSumDecomposi.description: The eigenspaces of a self-adjoint operator in a finite-dimensional inner product space provide an internal direct sum decomposition of that space.

  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] {T : E →ₗ[𝕜] E} [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 E] [_hT : Fact T.IsSymmetric]

explanatories.HasFDerivAt.fderiv: If a function has a specified derivative at a point, then that derivative is equal to the continuous linear map associated with the function at that point.

explanatories.HasFDerivAt.comp: If a function has a derivative at a point and another function has a derivative at the image of that point, then the composition of these functions also has a derivative at that point with the appropriately derived composition, illustrating the chain rule.
explanatories.ContDiff.comp: The theorem states that the composition of two continuously differentiable functions, each differentiable up to a specified order, is also continuously differentiable to the same order.
explanatories.Differentiable.comp: If two functions are differentiable, then their composition is also differentiable.

Differentiable.fderiv_norm_rpow.description: This theorem asserts that if a differentiable function maps to a normed space, then the derivative of the norm raised to a positive power can be expressed in terms of the derivative of the function itself and its norm.

FormalMultilinearSeries.sum.comment:
Given a formal multilinear series `p` and a vector `x`, then `p.sum x` is the sum `Σ pₙ xⁿ`. A
priori, it only behaves well when `‖x‖ < p.radius`.

explanatories.Finset.sum: This defines a function that computes the sum of a function's values at each element of a finite set.

FormalMultilinearSeries.radius.code:
FormalMultilinearSeries.radius.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {F : Type u_3} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜]
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F]
  (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) : ℝ≥0∞
FormalMultilinearSeries.radius.comment:
The radius of a formal multilinear series is the largest `r` such that the sum `Σ ‖pₙ‖ ‖y‖ⁿ`
converges for all `‖y‖ < r`. This implies that `Σ pₙ yⁿ` converges for all `‖y‖ < r`, but these
definitions are *not* equivalent in general.
FormalMultilinearSeries.radius.fullDefinition: def radius (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) : ℝ≥0∞ :=   ⨆ (r : ℝ≥0) (C : ℝ) (_ : ∀ n, ‖p n‖ * (r : ℝ) ^ n ≤ C), (r : ℝ≥0∞)
FormalMultilinearSeries.radius.description: The radius of a formal multilinear series is defined as the largest value such that the series converges for all input vectors whose norms are less than that value.

formal_multilinear_series.radius.comment:
The radius of a formal multilinear series is the largest `r` such that the sum `Σ ‖pₙ‖ ‖y‖ⁿ`
converges for all `‖y‖ < r`. This implies that `Σ pₙ yⁿ` converges for all `‖y‖ < r`, but these
definitions are *not* equivalent in general.
formal_multilinear_series.radius.fullDefinition: def radius (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) : ℝ≥0∞ :=   ⨆ (r : ℝ≥0) (C : ℝ) (_ : ∀ n, ‖p n‖ * (r : ℝ) ^ n ≤ C), (r : ℝ≥0∞)
formal_multilinear_series.radius.description: The radius of a formal multilinear series is defined as the largest value such that the series converges for all input vectors whose norms are less than that value.

  [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F]

  [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F]
  (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) (k l : ℕ) (s : Finset (Fin (k + l))) (hs : s.card = l) :
  ContinuousMultilinearMap 𝕜 (fun i => E) (ContinuousMultilinearMap 𝕜 (fun i => E) F)
FormalMultilinearSeries.changeOriginSeri.comment:
A term of `FormalMultilinearSeries.changeOriginSeries`.

Given a formal multilinear series `p` and a point `x` in its ball of convergence,
`p.changeOrigin x` is a formal multilinear series such that
`p.sum (x+y) = (p.changeOrigin x).sum y` when this makes sense. Each term of `p.changeOrigin x`
is itself an analytic function of `x` given by the series `p.changeOriginSeries`. Each term in
`changeOriginSeries` is the sum of `changeOriginSeriesTerm`'s over all `s` of cardinality `l`.
The definition is such that `p.changeOriginSeriesTerm k l s hs (fun _ ↦ x) (fun _ ↦ y) =
p (k + l) (s.piecewise (fun _ ↦ x) (fun _ ↦ y))`

explanatories.Fintype.card_fin: This theorem establishes that the cardinality of the finite type representing natural numbers less than a given integer is equal to that integer itself.
explanatories.Finset.card_fin: This theorem states that the cardinality of the universal set of natural numbers up to a finite value equals that finite value.
explanatories.Finset.card: This definition indicates that the cardinality of a finite set represents the total number of its elements.
explanatories.ContinuousMultilinearMap.curryFinFinset: This definition establishes an isomorphism between the space of continuous multilinear maps of a certain number of variables and those that can be expressed as a continuous multilinear map taking values in another continuous multilinear map space defined by the cardinalities of a finite set and its complement.
explanatories.Finset.card_compl: This theorem states that the cardinality of the complement of a finite set is equal to the total number of elements in the type minus the cardinality of the set itself.
explanatories.add_tsub_cancel_right: This theorem asserts that adding one element to another and then subtracting the second element yields the first element.

FormalMultilinearSeries.changeOriginSeri.fullDefinition: def changeOriginSeriesTerm (k l : ℕ) (s : Finset (Fin (k + l))) (hs : s.card = l) :     E[×l]→L[𝕜] E[×k]→L[𝕜] F := by   let a := ContinuousMultilinearMap.curryFinFinset 𝕜 E F hs     (by erw [Finset.card_compl, Fintype.card_fin, hs, add_tsub_cancel_right])   exact a (p (k + l))
FormalMultilinearSeries.changeOriginSeri.description: Each term of a formal multilinear series at a shifted point is defined as a continuous multilinear map that represents the evaluation of the series at the new point in terms of its original series terms.

FormalMultilinearSeries.changeOriginInde.code: FormalMultilinearSeries.changeOriginIndexEquiv : (k : ℕ) × (l : ℕ) × { s // s.card = l } ≃ (n : ℕ) × Finset (Fin n)
FormalMultilinearSeries.changeOriginInde.comment:
An auxiliary equivalence useful in the proofs about
`FormalMultilinearSeries.changeOriginSeries`: the set of triples `(k, l, s)`, where `s` is a
`Finset (Fin (k + l))` of cardinality `l` is equivalent to the set of pairs `(n, s)`, where `s` is a
`Finset (Fin n)`.

The forward map sends `(k, l, s)` to `(k + l, s)` and the inverse map sends `(n, s)` to
`(n - Finset.card s, Finset.card s, s)`. The actual definition is less readable because of problems
with non-definitional equalities.

explanatories.Filter.EventuallyEq.rfl: A theorem stating that a function is considered eventually equal to itself with respect to a given filter.
explanatories.tsub_add_cancel_of_le: This theorem states that if one element is less than or equal to another in an ordered structure, then subtracting the smaller element from the larger element and adding it back to the smaller element will yield the larger element.
explanatories.rfl: An element is equal to itself, with an implicit argument allowing for broader applications of this concept.
explanatories.Eq.symm: Equality is symmetric, meaning that if one element is equal to another, then the second is equal to the first.
explanatories.Set.EqOn.symm: The theorem asserts that if two functions are equal on a specified set, then they are also equal on that set when the order of the functions is reversed.
explanatories.Filter.EventuallyEq.symm: A theorem asserting that if two functions are equal almost everywhere with respect to a filter, then they are also equal almost everywhere in the reverse order with respect to that filter.
explanatories.Ne.symm: If two elements are not equal to each other, then reversing their order also indicates that they are not equal.
explanatories.Finset.card: This definition indicates that the cardinality of a finite set represents the total number of its elements.
explanatories.add_tsub_cancel_right: This theorem asserts that adding one element to another and then subtracting the second element yields the first element.
explanatories.Finset.map: This definition specifies a function that transforms a finite set by mapping its elements through an injective function, ensuring that the resulting set has no duplicates.
explanatories.card_finset_fin_le: This theorem demonstrates that the cardinality of a finite set of elements from a finite space does not exceed the size of that space.
explanatories.Equiv.toEmbedding: An equivalence between two types is transformed into an embedding that retains the injective property of the original function.
explanatories.Finset.card_map: This theorem asserts that the cardinality of the image of a finite set under an injective function is equal to the cardinality of the original set.
explanatories.Subtype.coe_mk: This theorem shows that the value of an element formed by a subtype is equal to the underlying value itself when the property is satisfied.
explanatories.Equiv.refl_toEmbedding: The reflection of an equivalence relation on a type results in a corresponding embedding that remains unchanged.
explanatories.Finset.map_refl: This theorem states that mapping a finite set through the identity function results in the same finite set.
explanatories.eq_self_iff_true: The assertion that an element is equal to itself is logically equivalent to stating that a truth exists.
explanatories.OrderIso.refl_toEquiv: This theorem shows that the reflection property of an order isomorphism coincides with the reflection of the equivalence relation on the same type.
explanatories.and_self_iff: The conjunction of a proposition with itself is equivalent to the proposition itself.

FormalMultilinearSeries.changeOriginInde.fullDefinition: def changeOriginIndexEquiv :     (Σ k l : ℕ, { s : Finset (Fin (k + l)) // s.card = l }) ≃ Σ n : ℕ, Finset (Fin n) where   toFun s := ⟨s.1 + s.2.1, s.2.2⟩   invFun s :=     ⟨s.1 - s.2.card, s.2.card,       ⟨s.2.map         (finCongr <| (tsub_add_cancel_of_le <| card_finset_fin_le s.2).symm).toEmbedding,         Finset.card_map _⟩⟩   left_inv := by     rintro ⟨k, l, ⟨s : Finset (Fin <| k + l), hs : s.card = l⟩⟩     dsimp only [Subtype.coe_mk]     -- Lean can't automatically generalize `k' = k + l - s.card`, `l' = s.card`, so we explicitly     -- formulate the generalized goal     suffices ∀ k' l', k' = k → l' = l → ∀ (hkl : k + l = k' + l') (hs'),         (⟨k', l', ⟨s.map (finCongr hkl).toEmbedding, hs'⟩⟩ :           Σk l : ℕ, { s : Finset (Fin (k + l)) // s.card = l }) = ⟨k, l, ⟨s, hs⟩⟩ by       apply this <;> simp only [hs, add_tsub_cancel_right]     rintro _ _ rfl rfl hkl hs'     simp only [Equiv.refl_toEmbedding, finCongr_refl, Finset.map_refl, eq_self_iff_true,       OrderIso.refl_toEquiv, and_self_iff, heq_iff_eq]   right_inv := by     rintro ⟨n, s⟩     simp [tsub_add_cancel_of_le (card_finset_fin_le s), finCongr_eq_equivCast]
FormalMultilinearSeries.changeOriginInde.description: An auxiliary equivalence relates a set of triples consisting of two non-negative integers and a finite set of a specific size to a set of pairs consisting of a non-negative integer and a finite set with a different size.

hasFPowerSeriesAt_iff.code:
hasFPowerSeriesAt_iff.{u_1, u_2} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] {p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 𝕜 E} {f : 𝕜 → E} {z₀ : 𝕜} :
  HasFPowerSeriesAt f p z₀ ↔ ∀ᶠ (z : 𝕜) in 𝓝 0, HasSum (fun n => z ^ n • p.coeff n) (f (z₀ + z))
hasFPowerSeriesAt_iff.comment:
A function `f : 𝕜 → E` has `p` as power series expansion at a point `z₀` iff it is the sum of
`p` in a neighborhood of `z₀`. This makes some proofs easier by hiding the fact that
`HasFPowerSeriesAt` depends on `p.radius`.

explanatories.HasFPowerSeriesAt: A function is said to have a given formal multilinear series as a power series around a point if it can be expressed as the sum of that series evaluated at perturbed inputs near that point.

hasFPowerSeriesAt_iff.description: A function has a power series representation at a point if and only if it can be expressed as the sum of that series in a neighborhood around that point.

  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F] (f : E → F)
  (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) (x : E) (n : ℕ) : Prop
HasFiniteFPowerSeriesAt.comment:
Given a function `f : E → F`, a formal multilinear series `p` and `n : ℕ`, we say that
`f` has `p` as a finite power series around `x` if `f (x + y) = ∑' pₙ yⁿ` for all `y` in a
neighborhood of `0`and `pₙ = 0` for `n ≤ m`.

HasFiniteFPowerSeriesAt.fullDefinition: def HasFiniteFPowerSeriesAt (f : E → F) (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) (x : E) (n : ℕ) :=   ∃ r, HasFiniteFPowerSeriesOnBall f p x n r
HasFiniteFPowerSeriesAt.description: A function has a formal multilinear series as a finite power series around a point if it agrees with the series in a neighborhood of that point and the coefficients of the series are zero beyond a certain degree.

block of `c`, we may define a function on `fin n → E` by picking the variables in the `i`-th block

explanatories.List.length: This defines a function that computes the number of elements in a list, where the length of an empty list is zero and the length of a non-empty list is one plus the length of its tail.

FormalMultilinearSeries.applyComposition.fullDefinition: def applyComposition (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) {n : ℕ} (c : Composition n) :     (Fin n → E) → Fin c.length → F := fun v i => p (c.blocksFun i) (v ∘ c.embedding i)

  (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) {n : ℕ} (c : Composition n) (j : Fin n) (v : Fin n → E) (z : E) :

Given a formal multilinear series `p`, a composition `c` of `n` and a continuous multilinear
map `f` in `c.length` variables, one may form a continuous multilinear map in `n` variables by
applying the right coefficient of `p` to each block of the composition, and then applying `f` to
the resulting vector. It is called `f.comp_along_composition p c`.

explanatories.Subsingleton.elim: In a subsingleton type, any two elements are equal, demonstrating the uniqueness of elements in such types.
explanatories.ContinuousMultilinearMap.map_add: This theorem establishes that a continuous multilinear map respects the addition operation in its input components when updating them at a specific index.
explanatories.ContinuousMultilinearMap.map_smul: The theorem asserts that applying a continuous multilinear map to a modified input, where one component is scaled by a constant, results in the scaled output of the original map applied to the unmodified input.
explanatories.ContinuousMultilinearMap.cont: The theorem states that a continuous multilinear map from a family of modules to another module is itself continuous with respect to the topology of the involved spaces.
explanatories.Continuous.comp: The composition of two continuous functions in topological spaces is itself continuous.
explanatories.continuous_pi: This theorem establishes that if a family of functions from a topological space to another type is continuous for each index, then the overall function defined by these family members is also continuous.
explanatories.ContinuousMultilinearMap.coe_continuous: The theorem establishes that the action of a continuous multilinear map can be continuously applied when viewed as a function, ensuring continuity in the context of the involved topological spaces.
explanatories.continuous_apply: This theorem states that if each type in a family of types has a topology, then the function that selects the component of a dependent pair based on its index is continuous.
explanatories.List.length: This defines a function that computes the number of elements in a list, where the length of an empty list is zero and the length of a non-empty list is one plus the length of its tail.
explanatories.ContinuousAt.comp: If one function is continuous at a point and another function is continuous at the image of that point under the first function, then their composition is also continuous at that original point.

  [CommRing 𝕜] [AddCommGroup E] [AddCommGroup F] [AddCommGroup G] [Module 𝕜 E] [Module 𝕜 F] [Module 𝕜 G]
  [TopologicalSpace E] [TopologicalSpace F] [TopologicalSpace G] [TopologicalAddGroup E] [ContinuousConstSMul 𝕜 E]
  [TopologicalAddGroup F] [ContinuousConstSMul 𝕜 F] [TopologicalAddGroup G] [ContinuousConstSMul 𝕜 G]
  (q : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 F G) (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E G
FormalMultilinearSeries.comp.comment:
Formal composition of two formal multilinear series. The `n`-th coefficient in the composition
is defined to be the sum of `q.comp_along_composition p c` over all compositions of
`n`. In other words, this term (as a multilinear function applied to `v_0, ..., v_{n-1}`) is
`∑'_{k} ∑'_{i₁ + ... + iₖ = n} qₖ (p_{i_1} (...), ..., p_{i_k} (...))`, where one puts all variables
`v_0, ..., v_{n-1}` in increasing order in the dots.

In general, the composition `q ∘ p` only makes sense when the constant coefficient of `p` vanishes.
We give a general formula but which ignores the value of `p 0` instead.

explanatories.ContinuousAt.comp: If one function is continuous at a point and another function is continuous at the image of that point under the first function, then their composition is also continuous at that original point.

formal_multilinear_series.comp.fullDefinition: protected def comp (q : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 F G) (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) :     FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E G := fun n => ∑ c : Composition n, q.compAlongComposition p c
formal_multilinear_series.comp.description: This definition describes the formal composition of two formal multilinear series, where the \(n\)-th coefficient in the resulting series is expressed as the sum of contributions from applying one series to the results of the other across all possible compositions.

  [CommRing 𝕜] [AddCommGroup E] [AddCommGroup F] [AddCommGroup G] [Module 𝕜 E] [Module 𝕜 F] [Module 𝕜 G]
  [TopologicalSpace E] [TopologicalSpace F] [TopologicalSpace G] [TopologicalAddGroup E] [ContinuousConstSMul 𝕜 E]
  [TopologicalAddGroup F] [ContinuousConstSMul 𝕜 F] [TopologicalAddGroup G] [ContinuousConstSMul 𝕜 G]
  (q : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 F G) (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) (v : Fin 0 → E) (v' : Fin 0 → F) :
  (q.comp p 0) v = (q 0) v'
FormalMultilinearSeries.comp_coeff_zero.comment:
The `0`-th coefficient of `q.comp p` is `q 0`. Since these maps are multilinear maps in zero
variables, but on different spaces, we can not state this directly, so we state it when applied to
arbitrary vectors (which have to be the zero vector).

FormalMultilinearSeries.comp_coeff_zero.description: The theorem asserts that the zero-th coefficient of the composition of two formal multilinear series corresponds to the evaluation of the first series at zero variables, resulting in the value of the second series at its zero-th argument.

FormalMultilinearSeries.compChangeOfVari.code:
FormalMultilinearSeries.compChangeOfVariables_sum.{u_6} {α : Type u_6} [AddCommMonoid α] (m M N : ℕ)
  (f : (n : ℕ) × (Fin n → ℕ) → α) (g : (n : ℕ) × Composition n → α)
  (h :
    ∀ (e : (n : ℕ) × (Fin n → ℕ)) (he : e ∈ compPartialSumSource m M N), f e = g (compChangeOfVariables m M N e he)) :
  ∑ e ∈ compPartialSumSource m M N, f e = ∑ e ∈ compPartialSumTarget m M N, g e
FormalMultilinearSeries.compChangeOfVari.comment:
`comp_change_of_variables m M N` is a bijection between `comp_partial_sum_source m M N`
and `comp_partial_sum_target m M N`, yielding equal sums for functions that correspond to each
other under the bijection. As `comp_change_of_variables m M N` is a dependent function, stating
that it is a bijection is not directly possible, but the consequence on sums can be stated
more easily.

FormalMultilinearSeries.comp_partialSum.code:
FormalMultilinearSeries.comp_partialSum.{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} {F : Type u_3} {G : Type u_4}
  [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F]
  [NormedAddCommGroup G] [NormedSpace 𝕜 G] (q : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 F G) (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F)
  (N : ℕ) (z : E) :
  q.partialSum N (∑ i ∈ Finset.Ico 1 N, (p i) fun _j => z) =
    ∑ i ∈ compPartialSumTarget 0 N N, (q.compAlongComposition p i.snd) fun _j => z
FormalMultilinearSeries.comp_partialSum.comment:
Composing the partial sums of two multilinear series coincides with the sum over all
compositions in `comp_partial_sum_target 0 N N`. This is precisely the motivation for the
definition of `comp_partial_sum_target`.

Composition.gather.code: Composition.gather {n : ℕ} (a : Composition n) (b : Composition a.length) : Composition n
Composition.gather.comment:
When `a` is a composition of `n` and `b` is a composition of `a.length`, `a.gather b` is the
composition of `n` obtained by gathering all the blocks of `a` corresponding to a block of `b`.
For instance, if `a = [6, 5, 3, 5, 2]` and `b = [2, 3]`, one should gather together
the first two blocks of `a` and its last three blocks, giving `a.gather b = [11, 10]`.

Composition.gather.fullDefinition: def gather (a : Composition n) (b : Composition a.length) : Composition n where   blocks := (a.blocks.splitWrtComposition b).map sum   blocks_pos := by     rw [forall_mem_map_iff]     intro j hj     suffices H : ∀ i ∈ j, 1 ≤ i by calc       0 < j.length := length_pos_of_mem_splitWrtComposition hj       _ ≤ j.sum := length_le_sum_of_one_le _ H     intro i hi     apply a.one_le_blocks     rw [← a.blocks.join_splitWrtComposition b]     exact mem_join_of_mem hj hi   blocks_sum := by rw [← sum_join, join_splitWrtComposition, a.blocks_sum]

Composition.sizeUpTo_sizeUpTo_add.code:
Composition.sizeUpTo_sizeUpTo_add {n : ℕ} (a : Composition n) (b : Composition a.length) {i j : ℕ} (hi : i < b.length)
  (hj : j < b.blocksFun ⟨i, hi⟩) :
  a.sizeUpTo (b.sizeUpTo i + j) = (a.gather b).sizeUpTo i + (a.sigmaCompositionAux b ⟨i, ⋯⟩).sizeUpTo j
Composition.sizeUpTo_sizeUpTo_add.comment:
Auxiliary lemma to prove that the composition of formal multilinear series is associative.

Consider a composition `a` of `n` and a composition `b` of `a.length`. Grouping together some
blocks of `a` according to `b` as in `a.gather b`, one can compute the total size of the blocks
of `a` up to an index `size_up_to b i + j` (where the `j` corresponds to a set of blocks of `a`
that do not fill a whole block of `a.gather b`). The first part corresponds to a sum of blocks
in `a.gather b`, and the second one to a sum of blocks in the next block of
`sigma_composition_aux a b`. This is the content of this lemma.

Composition.sigmaEquivSigmaPi.code:
Composition.sigmaEquivSigmaPi (n : ℕ) :
  (a : Composition n) × Composition a.length ≃ (c : Composition n) × ((i : Fin c.length) → Composition (c.blocksFun i))
Composition.sigmaEquivSigmaPi.comment:
Natural equivalence between `(Σ (a : composition n), composition a.length)` and
`(Σ (c : composition n), Π (i : fin c.length), composition (c.blocks_fun i))`, that shows up as a
change of variables in the proof that composition of formal multilinear series is associative.

Consider a composition `a` of `n` and a composition `b` of `a.length`. Then `b` indicates how to
group together some blocks of `a`, giving altogether `b.length` blocks of blocks. These blocks of
blocks can be called `d₀, ..., d_{a.length - 1}`, and one obtains a composition `c` of `n` by
saying that each `dᵢ` is one single block. The map `⟨a, b⟩ → ⟨c, (d₀, ..., d_{a.length - 1})⟩` is
the direct map in the equiv.

Conversely, if one starts from `c` and the `dᵢ`s, one can join the `dᵢ`s to obtain a composition
`a` of `n`, and register the lengths of the `dᵢ`s in a composition `b` of `a.length`. This is the
inverse map of the equiv.

Composition.sigmaEquivSigmaPi.fullDefinition: def sigmaEquivSigmaPi (n : ℕ) :     (Σ a : Composition n, Composition a.length) ≃       Σ c : Composition n, ∀ i : Fin c.length, Composition (c.blocksFun i) where   toFun i := ⟨i.1.gather i.2, i.1.sigmaCompositionAux i.2⟩   invFun i :=     ⟨{  blocks := (ofFn fun j => (i.2 j).blocks).join         blocks_pos := by           simp only [and_imp, List.mem_join, exists_imp, forall_mem_ofFn_iff]           exact @fun i j hj => Composition.blocks_pos _ hj         blocks_sum := by simp [sum_ofFn, Composition.blocks_sum, Composition.sum_blocksFun] },       { blocks := ofFn fun j => (i.2 j).length         blocks_pos := by           intro k hk           refine ((forall_mem_ofFn_iff (P := fun i => 0 < i)).2 fun j => ?_) k hk           exact Composition.length_pos_of_pos _ (Composition.blocks_pos' _ _ _)         blocks_sum := by dsimp only [Composition.length]; simp [sum_ofFn] }⟩   left_inv := by     -- the fact that we have a left inverse is essentially `join_split_wrt_composition`,     -- but we need to massage it to take care of the dependent setting.     rintro ⟨a, b⟩     rw [sigma_composition_eq_iff]     dsimp     constructor     · conv_rhs =>         rw [← join_splitWrtComposition a.blocks b, ← ofFn_get (splitWrtComposition a.blocks b)]       have A : length (gather a b) = List.length (splitWrtComposition a.blocks b) := by         simp only [length, gather, length_map, length_splitWrtComposition]       congr! 2       exact (Fin.heq_fun_iff A (α := List ℕ)).2 fun i => rfl     · have B : Composition.length (Composition.gather a b) = List.length b.blocks :=         Composition.length_gather _ _       conv_rhs => rw [← ofFn_getElem b.blocks]       congr 1       refine (Fin.heq_fun_iff B).2 fun i => ?_       rw [sigmaCompositionAux, Composition.length, List.getElem_map_rev List.length,         List.getElem_of_eq (map_length_splitWrtComposition _ _)]   right_inv := by     -- the fact that we have a right inverse is essentially `splitWrtComposition_join`,     -- but we need to massage it to take care of the dependent setting.     rintro ⟨c, d⟩     have : map List.sum (ofFn fun i : Fin (Composition.length c) => (d i).blocks) = c.blocks := by       simp [map_ofFn, (· ∘ ·), Composition.blocks_sum, Composition.ofFn_blocksFun]     rw [sigma_pi_composition_eq_iff]     dsimp     congr! 1     · congr       ext1       dsimp [Composition.gather]       rwa [splitWrtComposition_join]       simp only [map_ofFn]       rfl     · rw [Fin.heq_fun_iff]       · intro i         dsimp [Composition.sigmaCompositionAux]         rw [getElem_of_eq (splitWrtComposition_join _ _ _)]         · simp only [getElem_ofFn]         · simp only [map_ofFn]           rfl       · congr
Composition.sigmaEquivSigmaPi.description: This definition establishes a natural equivalence between two structures representing compositions, linking a composition of a size to its corresponding blocks and their arrangements.

ContinuousLinearMap.uncurryBilinear.comment:
Reinterpret a bilinear map `f : E →L[𝕜] F →L[𝕜] G` as a multilinear map
`(E × F) [×2]→L[𝕜] G`. This multilinear map is the second term in the formal
multilinear series expansion of `uncurry f`. It is given by
`f.uncurryBilinear ![(x, y), (x', y')] = f x y'`.

explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.uncurryLeft: This definition describes a process that takes a continuous linear map from a single variable and produces a corresponding continuous multilinear map that operates on one additional variable by merging it with the input sequence of variables.
explanatories.LinearIsometryEquiv.symm: This definition establishes the inverse of a linear isometry equivalence, enabling a bijection between two seminormed vector spaces that preserves their respective structures when reversed.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.comp: The composition of bounded linear maps results in another bounded linear map.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.bilinearComp: This definition describes how to construct a new continuous linear map by combining a bilinear map with two preceding continuous linear maps.

FormalMultilinearSeries.leftInv.comment:
The left inverse of a formal multilinear series, where the `n`-th term is defined inductively
in terms of the previous ones to make sure that `(leftInv p i) ∘ p = id`. For this, the linear term
`p₁` in `p` should be invertible. In the definition, `i` is a linear isomorphism that should
coincide with `p₁`, so that one can use its inverse in the construction. The definition does not
use that `i = p₁`, but proofs that the definition is well-behaved do.

The `n`-th term in `q ∘ p` is `∑ qₖ (p_{j₁}, ..., p_{jₖ})` over `j₁ + ... + jₖ = n`. In this
expression, `qₙ` appears only once, in `qₙ (p₁, ..., p₁)`. We adjust the definition so that this
term compensates the rest of the sum, using `i⁻¹` as an inverse to `p₁`.

These formulas only make sense when the constant term `p₀` vanishes. The definition we give is
general, but it ignores the value of `p₀`.

explanatories.FormalMultilinearSeries.compAlongComposi: This definition outlines a method for creating a continuous multilinear map from two formal multilinear series and a specified composition by applying coefficients from one series to each block of the composition before using the other series on the resulting vector.

term compensates the rest of the sum, using `i⁻¹` as an inverse to `p₁`.
