formal_multilinear_series.comp_right_inv.code:
FormalMultilinearSeries.comp_rightInv_aux1.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] {E : Type u_2}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] {F : Type u_3} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F] {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n)
  (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) (q : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 F E) (v : Fin n → F) :
  (p.comp q n) v = ∑ c ∈ {c | 1 < c.length}.toFinset, (p c.length) (q.applyComposition c v) + (p 1) fun x => (q n) v

FormalMultilinearSeries.comp_rightInv_aux2.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {𝕜 : Type u_1} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] {E : Type u_2}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] {F : Type u_3} [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F]
  (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) (i : E ≃L[𝕜] F) (n : ℕ) (v : Fin (n + 2) → F) :
  ∑ c ∈ {c | 1 < c.length}.toFinset,
      (p c.length) (applyComposition (fun k => if k < n + 2 then p.rightInv i k else 0) c v) =
    ∑ c ∈ {c | 1 < c.length}.toFinset, (p c.length) ((p.rightInv i).applyComposition c v)

  (p : FormalMultilinearSeries 𝕜 E F) (i : E ≃L[𝕜] F) (h : p 1 = (continuousMultilinearCurryFin1 𝕜 E F).symm ↑i) :
  p.leftInv i = p.rightInv i
FormalMultilinearSeries.leftInv_eq_right.comment:
The left inverse and the right inverse of a formal multilinear series coincide. This is not at
all obvious from their definition, but it follows from uniqueness of inverses (which comes from the
fact that composition is associative on formal multilinear series).

FormalMultilinearSeries.radius_right_inv_pos_of_radius_pos_aux1 (n : ℕ) (p : ℕ → ℝ) (hp : ∀ (k : ℕ), 0 ≤ p k) {r a : ℝ}
  (hr : 0 ≤ r) (ha : 0 ≤ a) :
  ∑ k ∈ Ico 2 (n + 1), a ^ k * ∑ c ∈ {c | 1 < c.length}.toFinset, r ^ c.length * ∏ j : Fin c.length, p (c.blocksFun j) ≤
    ∑ j ∈ Ico 2 (n + 1), r ^ j * (∑ k ∈ Ico 1 n, a ^ k * p k) ^ j
FormalMultilinearSeries.radius_right_inv.comment:
First technical lemma to control the growth of coefficients of the inverse. Bound the explicit
expression for `∑_{k<n+1} aᵏ Qₖ` in terms of a sum of powers of the same sum one step before,
in a general abstract setup.

AnalyticAt.eventually_eq_zero_or_eventua.comment:
The *principle of isolated zeros* for an analytic function, local version: if a function is
analytic at `z₀`, then either it is identically zero in a neighborhood of `z₀`, or it does not
vanish in a punctured neighborhood of `z₀`.
AnalyticAt.eventually_eq_zero_or_eventua.description: If a function is analytic at a point, then it is either identically zero in a neighborhood around that point or non-zero in a punctured neighborhood around that point.

vanish in a punctured neighborhood of `z₀`.

analytic_at.eventually_eq_or_eventually_.description: If two functions are analytic at a common point, then they are either equal in a neighborhood of that point or they are distinct in a neighborhood excluding that point.

AnalyticAt.frequently_zero_iff_eventuall.description: If a function is analytic at a point, then the condition that it is frequently zero in a neighborhood around that point is equivalent to it being eventually zero in that same neighborhood.

analytic_at.frequently_zero_iff_eventual.description: If a function is analytic at a point, then the condition that it is frequently zero in a neighborhood around that point is equivalent to it being eventually zero in that same neighborhood.

AnalyticAt.unique_eventuallyEq_zpow_smul.comment:
For a function `f` on `𝕜`, and `z₀ ∈ 𝕜`, there exists at most one `n` such that on a punctured
neighbourhood of `z₀` we have `f z = (z - z₀) ^ n • g z`, with `g` analytic and nonvanishing at
`z₀`. We formulate this with `n : ℤ`, and deduce the case `n : ℕ` later, for applications to
meromorphic functions.
AnalyticAt.unique_eventuallyEq_zpow_smul.description: If a function can be expressed in terms of a nonvanishing analytic function multiplied by a power of the difference from a point around that point in two different ways, then the powers must be equal.

AnalyticAt.exists_eventuallyEq_pow_smul_.comment:
If `f` is analytic at `z₀`, then exactly one of the following two possibilities occurs: either
`f` vanishes identically near `z₀`, or locally around `z₀` it has the form `z ↦ (z - z₀) ^ n • g z`
for some `n` and some `g` which is analytic and non-vanishing at `z₀`.
AnalyticAt.exists_eventuallyEq_pow_smul_.description: For a function that is analytic at a point, it either vanishes identically in a neighborhood of that point or can be expressed locally as a product of a power of the difference from that point and another analytic function that is non-zero at the point.

AnalyticAt.order.comment:
The order of vanishing of `f` at `z₀`, as an element of `ℕ∞`.

This is defined to be `∞` if `f` is identically 0 on a neighbourhood of `z₀`, and otherwise the
unique `n` such that `f z = (z - z₀) ^ n • g z` with `g` analytic and non-vanishing at `z₀`. See
`AnalyticAt.order_eq_top_iff` and `AnalyticAt.order_eq_nat_iff` for these equivalences.

AnalyticAt.unique_eventuallyEq_pow_smul_.description: If a function has two different expressions involving non-vanishing analytic functions multiplied by distinct powers of the difference from a point, then those powers must be the same.

A sequence `u` has the property that its ratio of successive differences is bounded
when there is a positive real number `C` such that, for all n ∈ ℕ,
(u (n + 2) - u (n + 1)) ≤ C * (u (n + 1) - u n)

le_gronwallBound_of_liminf_deriv_right_l.code:
le_gronwallBound_of_liminf_deriv_right_le {f f' : ℝ → ℝ} {δ K ε a b : ℝ} (hf : ContinuousOn f (Icc a b))
  (hf' : ∀ x ∈ Ico a b, ∀ (r : ℝ), f' x < r → ∃ᶠ (z : ℝ) in 𝓝[>] x, (z - x)⁻¹ * (f z - f x) < r) (ha : f a ≤ δ)
  (bound : ∀ x ∈ Ico a b, f' x ≤ K * f x + ε) (x : ℝ) : x ∈ Icc a b → f x ≤ gronwallBound δ K ε (x - a)
le_gronwallBound_of_liminf_deriv_right_l.comment:
A Grönwall-like inequality: if `f : ℝ → ℝ` is continuous on `[a, b]` and satisfies
the inequalities `f a ≤ δ` and
`∀ x ∈ [a, b), liminf_{z→x+0} (f z - f x)/(z - x) ≤ K * (f x) + ε`, then `f x`
is bounded by `gronwallBound δ K ε (x - a)` on `[a, b]`.

See also `norm_le_gronwallBound_of_norm_deriv_right_le` for a version bounding `‖f x‖`,
`f : ℝ → E`.

  {s : ℝ → Set E} {K : ℝ≥0} {f g f' g' : ℝ → E} {a b εf εg δ : ℝ} (hv : ∀ (t : ℝ), LipschitzOnWith K (v t) (s t))
  (hf : ContinuousOn f (Icc a b)) (hf' : ∀ t ∈ Ico a b, HasDerivWithinAt f (f' t) (Ici t) t)
  (f_bound : ∀ t ∈ Ico a b, dist (f' t) (v t (f t)) ≤ εf) (hfs : ∀ t ∈ Ico a b, f t ∈ s t)
  (hg : ContinuousOn g (Icc a b)) (hg' : ∀ t ∈ Ico a b, HasDerivWithinAt g (g' t) (Ici t) t)
  (g_bound : ∀ t ∈ Ico a b, dist (g' t) (v t (g t)) ≤ εg) (hgs : ∀ t ∈ Ico a b, g t ∈ s t) (ha : dist (f a) (g a) ≤ δ)
  (t : ℝ) : t ∈ Icc a b → dist (f t) (g t) ≤ gronwallBound δ (↑K) (εf + εg) (t - a)
dist_le_of_approx_trajectories_ODE_of_me.comment:
If `f` and `g` are two approximate solutions of the same ODE, then the distance between them
can't grow faster than exponentially. This is a simple corollary of Grönwall's inequality, and some
people call this Grönwall's inequality too.

This version assumes all inequalities to be true in some time-dependent set `s t`,
and assumes that the solutions never leave this set.

PicardLindelof.FunSpace.vComp.comment:
Given a curve $γ \colon [t_{\min}, t_{\max}] → E$, `PicardLindelof.vComp` is the function
$F(t)=v(π t, γ(π t))$, where `π` is the projection $ℝ → [t_{\min}, t_{\max}]$. The integral of this
function is the image of `γ` under the contracting map we are going to define below.

explanatories.PicardLindelof.proj: This definition describes a projection function that maps real numbers to a closed interval, assigning values below the minimum to the minimum and values above the maximum to the maximum.

PicardLindelof.FunSpace.vComp.fullDefinition: def vComp (t : ℝ) : E :=   v (v.proj t) (f (v.proj t))

explanatories.intervalIntegral.integral_same: The integral of a function over an interval where the endpoints are the same is always equal to zero with respect to the given measure.
explanatories.add_zero: This theorem states that in any additive structure with a zero element, adding zero to any element results in that same element.
explanatories.LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul: If a function is Lipschitz continuous with a non-negative constant, then the distance between the images of any two points is at most that constant multiplied by the distance between the points themselves.
explanatories.dist_add_left: The distance between the products of a fixed element and two other elements in a pseudo-metric space is equal to the distance between those two other elements.
explanatories.dist_eq_norm: This theorem establishes that the distance between two elements in a seminormed additive group is equal to the seminorm of their difference.
explanatories.intervalIntegral.integral_interval_sub_l: The difference between the integrals of a function over two intervals can be expressed as the integral of the same function over the interval defined by the two original intervals.
explanatories.intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_of_nor: The norm of the integral of a function over a closed interval is bounded by the product of a constant and the length of the interval if the function's norm is bounded by that constant throughout the interval.

MeasureTheory.ConvolutionExistsAt.comment:
The convolution of `f` and `g` exists at `x` when the function `t ↦ L (f t) (g (x - t))` is
integrable. There are various conditions on `f` and `g` to prove this.

MeasureTheory.ConvolutionExistsAt.description: This defines the condition under which the convolution of two functions exists at a specific point, based on the integrability of the function resulting from applying a linear map to their combination.

BddAbove.convolutionExistsAt.code:
BddAbove.convolutionExistsAt.{u𝕜, uG, uE, uE', uF} {𝕜 : Type u𝕜} {G : Type uG} {E : Type uE} {E' : Type uE'}
  {F : Type uF} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedAddCommGroup E'] [NormedAddCommGroup F] {f : G → E} {g : G → E'}
  [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E'] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F] (L : E →L[𝕜] E' →L[𝕜] F)
  [MeasurableSpace G] {μ : Measure G} [AddCommGroup G] [MeasurableNeg G] [μ.IsAddLeftInvariant] [MeasurableAdd₂ G]
  [SFinite μ] {x₀ : G} {s : Set G} (hbg : BddAbove ((fun i => ‖g i‖) '' ((fun t => x₀ - t) ⁻¹' s)))
  (hs : MeasurableSet s) (h2s : (support fun t => (L (f t)) (g (x₀ - t))) ⊆ s) (hf : IntegrableOn f s μ)
  (hmg : AEStronglyMeasurable g μ) : ConvolutionExistsAt f g x₀ L μ
BddAbove.convolutionExistsAt.comment:
A sufficient condition to prove that `f ⋆[L, μ] g` exists.
We assume that the integrand has compact support and `g` is bounded on this support (note that
both properties hold if `g` is continuous with compact support). We also require that `f` is
integrable on the support of the integrand, and that both functions are strongly measurable.

This is a variant of `BddAbove.convolutionExistsAt'` in an abelian group with a left-invariant
measure. This allows us to state the boundedness and measurability of `g` in a more natural way.

MeasureTheory.convolution.comment:
The convolution of two functions `f` and `g` with respect to a continuous bilinear map `L` and
measure `μ`. It is defined to be `(f ⋆[L, μ] g) x = ∫ t, L (f t) (g (x - t)) ∂μ`.

  {E : Type uE} {E' : Type uE'} {F : Type uF} {P : Type uP} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedAddCommGroup E']
  [NormedAddCommGroup F] {f : G → E} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E'] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F]
  (L : E →L[𝕜] E' →L[𝕜] F) [MeasurableSpace G] {μ : Measure G} [NormedSpace ℝ F] [AddGroup G] [TopologicalSpace G]
  [TopologicalAddGroup G] [BorelSpace G] [TopologicalSpace P] {g : P → G → E'} {s : Set P} {k : Set G}
  (hk : IsCompact k) (hgs : ∀ (p : P) (x : G), p ∈ s → x ∉ k → g p x = 0) (hf : LocallyIntegrable f μ)
  (hg : ContinuousOn (↿g) (s ×ˢ univ)) : ContinuousOn (fun q => (f ⋆[L, μ] g q.1) q.2) (s ×ˢ univ)
MeasureTheory.continuousOn_convolution_r.comment:
The convolution `f * g` is continuous if `f` is locally integrable and `g` is continuous and
compactly supported. Version where `g` depends on an additional parameter in a subset `s` of
a parameter space `P` (and the compact support `k` is independent of the parameter in `s`).

explanatories.Set: This defines a set as a collection of elements belonging to a specific type.
explanatories.MeasureTheory.LocallyIntegrable: A function is defined to be locally integrable if it is integrable in the neighborhood of every point within its domain.
explanatories.IsCompact: This defines the property of a set within a topological space being compact, which requires that for any nontrivial filter containing the set, there is an element within the set such that every set in the filter intersects with every neighborhood of that element.
explanatories.ContinuousOn: This defines a property indicating that a function between topological spaces is continuous at every point of a specified subset.

MeasureTheory.continuousOn_convolution_r.description: If a function is locally integrable and a second function, depending on an additional parameter, is continuous and compactly supported outside a certain set, then their convolution remains continuous with respect to that parameter and any fixed input.

`g x₀` on a ball with the same radius around `x₀`. See `dist_convolution_le` for a special case.

We can simplify the second argument of `dist` further if we add some extra type-classes on `E`
and `𝕜` or if `L` is scalar multiplication.

MeasureTheory.convolution_assoc.comment:
Convolution is associative. This requires that
* all maps are a.e. strongly measurable w.r.t one of the measures
* `f ⋆[L, ν] g` exists almost everywhere
* `‖g‖ ⋆[μ] ‖k‖` exists almost everywhere
* `‖f‖ ⋆[ν] (‖g‖ ⋆[μ] ‖k‖)` exists at `x₀`

  [NormedAddCommGroup E'] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [NormedSpace ℝ E'] [NormedSpace ℝ F] (f : ℝ → E)
  (g : ℝ → E') (L : E →L[ℝ] E' →L[ℝ] F) (ν : Measure ℝ := by volume_tac) : ℝ → F
MeasureTheory.posConvolution.comment:
The forward convolution of two functions `f` and `g` on `ℝ`, with respect to a continuous
bilinear map `L` and measure `ν`. It is defined to be the function mapping `x` to
`∫ t in 0..x, L (f t) (g (x - t)) ∂ν` if `0 < x`, and 0 otherwise.

explanatories.Set.indicator: The definition describes a function that outputs a specified value for an element if it is in a given set, and returns zero otherwise.

MeasureTheory.posConvolution.fullDefinition: noncomputable def posConvolution (f : ℝ → E) (g : ℝ → E') (L : E →L[ℝ] E' →L[ℝ] F)     (ν : Measure ℝ := by volume_tac) : ℝ → F :=   indicator (Ioi (0 : ℝ)) fun x => ∫ t in (0)..x, L (f t) (g (x - t)) ∂ν
MeasureTheory.posConvolution.description: The definition establishes the forward convolution of two functions on the real line, using a continuous bilinear map and a specified measure, resulting in a function that integrates the map applied to the two functions over a specified interval.

MeasureTheory.integral_posConvolution.{uE, uE', uF} {E : Type uE} {E' : Type uE'} {F : Type uF} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedAddCommGroup E'] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [NormedSpace ℝ E'] [NormedSpace ℝ F]
  [CompleteSpace F] [CompleteSpace E] [CompleteSpace E'] {μ ν : Measure ℝ} [SFinite μ] [SFinite ν]
  [μ.IsAddRightInvariant] [NoAtoms ν] {f : ℝ → E} {g : ℝ → E'} (hf : IntegrableOn f (Ioi 0) ν)
  (hg : IntegrableOn g (Ioi 0) μ) (L : E →L[ℝ] E' →L[ℝ] F) :
  ∫ (x : ℝ) in Ioi 0, ∫ (t : ℝ) in 0 ..x, (L (f t)) (g (x - t)) ∂ν ∂μ =
    (L (∫ (x : ℝ) in Ioi 0, f x ∂ν)) (∫ (x : ℝ) in Ioi 0, g x ∂μ)
MeasureTheory.integral_posConvolution.comment:
The integral over `Ioi 0` of a forward convolution of two functions is equal to the product
of their integrals over this set. (Compare `integral_convolution` for the two-sided convolution.)

MeasureTheory.integral_posConvolution.description: The theorem demonstrates that the integral of the convolution of two functions over a positive interval is equal to the product of their individual integrals over the same interval when both functions are integrable.

VectorFourier.fourierSMulRight.comment:
Send a function `f : V → E` to the function `f : V → Hom (W, E)` given by
`v ↦ (w ↦ -2 * π * I * L (v, w) • f v)`. This is designed so that the Fourier transform of
`fourierSMulRight L f` is the derivative of the Fourier transform of `f`.

explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.smulRight: The construction defines a continuous linear map that takes a scalar-valued linear map and an element from a module, producing a new linear map by scaling the output by the given element.

VectorFourier.fourierSMulRight.fullDefinition: def fourierSMulRight (v : V) : (W →L[ℝ] E) := -(2 * π * I) • (L v).smulRight (f v)
VectorFourier.fourierSMulRight.description: This definition establishes a way to associate a function that maps vectors to complex numbers with another function that maps vectors from one space to bounded linear functions, where the transformation incorporates a bilinear operation and a scaling factor related to complex numbers.

VectorFourier.fourierSMulRight.eq_1.description: This theorem states that the specific way of relating a function that maps vectors to complex numbers with a linear function produces an expression equivalent to a particular scaling of a bilinear operation when evaluated at a given vector.

VectorFourier.fourierPowSMulRight.comment:
The formal multilinear series whose `n`-th term is
`(w₁, ..., wₙ) ↦ (-2πI)^n * L v w₁ * ... * L v wₙ • f v`, as a continuous multilinear map in
the space `W [×n]→L[ℝ] E`.

This is designed so that the Fourier transform of `v ↦ fourierPowSMulRight L f v n` is the
`n`-th derivative of the Fourier transform of `f`.

explanatories.FormalMultilinearSeries: A formal multilinear series is defined as a collection of multilinear maps that relate vectors from a source space to a target space over a specified ring.
explanatories.ContinuousMultilinearMap.mkPiRing: This definition describes a continuous multilinear map from a space of indexed scalars to a module that computes the product of its components, scaled by a fixed reference element.
explanatories.ContinuousMultilinearMap.compContinuousL: This definition states that the composition of a continuous multilinear map with a collection of continuous linear maps results in another continuous multilinear map.

VectorFourier.fourierPowSMulRight.fullDefinition: def fourierPowSMulRight (f : V → E) (v : V) : FormalMultilinearSeries ℝ W E := fun n ↦   (- (2 * π * I))^n • ((ContinuousMultilinearMap.mkPiRing ℝ (Fin n) (f v)).compContinuousLinearMap   (fun _ ↦ L v))
VectorFourier.fourierPowSMulRight.description: This definition describes a formal multilinear series associated with a specific combination of bilinear mappings and a function, structured so that its Fourier transform corresponds to the n-th derivative of the Fourier transform of the original function.

VectorFourier.fourierPowSMulRight_eq_com.code:
VectorFourier.fourierPowSMulRight_eq_comp.{u_1, u_2, u_3} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E]
  {V : Type u_2} {W : Type u_3} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace ℝ V] [NormedAddCommGroup W] [NormedSpace ℝ W]
  (L : V →L[ℝ] W →L[ℝ] ℝ) {f : V → E} {v : V} {n : ℕ} :
  VectorFourier.fourierPowSMulRight L f v n =
    (-(2 * ↑π * I)) ^ n •
      ((smulRightL ℝ (fun x => W) E)
          ((ContinuousMultilinearMap.mkPiAlgebra ℝ (Fin n) ℝ).compContinuousLinearMapLRight fun x => L v))
        (f v)
VectorFourier.fourierPowSMulRight_eq_com.comment:
Decomposing `fourierPowSMulRight L f v n` as a composition of continuous bilinear and
multilinear maps, to deduce easily its continuity and differentiability properties.

explanatories.ContinuousMultilinearMap.compContinuousL: This definition describes a continuous multilinear map that is formed by composing a fixed continuous multilinear map with a family of continuous linear maps, resulting in a new continuous multilinear map.
explanatories.ContinuousMultilinearMap.mkPiAlgebra: This definition describes a continuous multilinear map that takes a function which produces elements of a commutative algebra and maps it to the product of those elements over a finite index set.

VectorFourier.fourierPowSMulRight_eq_com.description: This theorem expresses the equality of a specific formal multilinear series associated with a function and a bilinear operation, demonstrating its structure as a composition of continuous maps scaled by a complex coefficient.

SchwartzMap.one_add_le_sup_seminorm_appl.code:
SchwartzMap.one_add_le_sup_seminorm_apply.{u_1, u_4, u_5} {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_4} {F : Type u_5}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] [NormedField 𝕜] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F]
  [SMulCommClass ℝ 𝕜 F] {m : ℕ × ℕ} {k n : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ m.1) (hn : n ≤ m.2) (f : 𝓢(E, F)) (x : E) :
  (1 + ‖x‖) ^ k * ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n (⇑f) x‖ ≤ 2 ^ m.1 * ((Finset.Iic m).sup fun m => SchwartzMap.seminorm 𝕜 m.1 m.2) f
SchwartzMap.one_add_le_sup_seminorm_appl.comment:
A more convenient version of `le_sup_seminorm_apply`.

The set `Finset.Iic m` is the set of all pairs `(k', n')` with `k' ≤ m.1` and `n' ≤ m.2`.
Note that the constant is far from optimal.

explanatories.Finset.Iic: This definition creates a finite set of elements that are less than or equal to a specified element within a locally finite ordered structure.
explanatories.Finset.sup: This definition describes a function that computes the supremum of the images of elements from a finite set under a given function, using a specific order structure that includes a least element.

SchwartzMap.one_add_le_sup_seminorm_appl.description: The theorem shows that a certain bound involving the seminorm and iterated derivatives of a Schwartz function at a point can be expressed in terms of a supremum over a finite set of seminorms, adjusted by a factor related to the norm of the point.

  (h₂ : x ^ (k + l) * f ≤ C₂) : x ^ k * f ≤ 2 ^ l * (C₁ + C₂) * (1 + x) ^ (-↑l)
SchwartzMap.pow_mul_le_of_le_of_pow_mul_.comment:
Pointwise inequality to control `x ^ k * f` in terms of `1 / (1 + x) ^ l` if one controls both
`f` (with a bound `C₁`) and `x ^ (k + l) * f` (with a bound `C₂`). This will be used to check
integrability of `x ^ k * f x` when `f` is a Schwartz function, and to control explicitly its
integral in terms of suitable seminorms of `f`.
SchwartzMap.pow_mul_le_of_le_of_pow_mul_.description: The theorem provides a pointwise inequality that bounds the product of a power of a non-negative variable and a non-negative function in terms of constants and an inverse polynomial decay, facilitating the analysis of integrability for the function when it is a Schwartz function.

explanatories.ContDiff: A function is defined to be continuously differentiable up to a specified order if it has continuous derivatives for all orders up to that specified limit.
explanatories.SchwartzMap.seminorm_le_bound: If a seminorm of a Schwartz function is bounded for all points by a constant, then the seminorm itself is also bounded by that constant.
explanatories.Prod.fst: This defines a function that retrieves the first element from a given pair of values.
explanatories.Prod.snd: This defines a function that retrieves the second element from a given pair of values.
explanatories.Finset.sup: This definition describes a function that computes the supremum of the images of elements from a finite set under a given function, using a specific order structure that includes a least element.
explanatories.schwartz_withSeminorms: This theorem establishes that the family of seminorms associated with Schwartz functions forms a structure compatible with a seminormed space.
explanatories.SchwartzMap.mkLM: A construction is provided for a semilinear map that connects Schwartz spaces through a given operation while satisfying properties such as linearity, continuity, and a specific growth condition.

schwartz_map.mk_clm.fullDefinition: def mkCLM [RingHomIsometric σ] (A : (D → E) → F → G)     (hadd : ∀ (f g : 𝓢(D, E)) (x), A (f + g) x = A f x + A g x)     (hsmul : ∀ (a : 𝕜) (f : 𝓢(D, E)) (x), A (a • f) x = σ a • A f x)     (hsmooth : ∀ f : 𝓢(D, E), ContDiff ℝ ⊤ (A f))     (hbound : ∀ n : ℕ × ℕ, ∃ (s : Finset (ℕ × ℕ)) (C : ℝ), 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ (f : 𝓢(D, E)) (x : F),       ‖x‖ ^ n.fst * ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n.snd (A f) x‖ ≤ C * s.sup (schwartzSeminormFamily 𝕜 D E) f) :     𝓢(D, E) →SL[σ] 𝓢(F, G) where   cont := by     change Continuous (mkLM A hadd hsmul hsmooth hbound : 𝓢(D, E) →ₛₗ[σ] 𝓢(F, G))     refine       Seminorm.continuous_from_bounded (schwartz_withSeminorms 𝕜 D E)         (schwartz_withSeminorms 𝕜' F G) _ fun n => ?_     rcases hbound n with ⟨s, C, hC, h⟩     refine ⟨s, ⟨C, hC⟩, fun f => ?_⟩     exact (mkLM A hadd hsmul hsmooth hbound f).seminorm_le_bound 𝕜' n.1 n.2 (by positivity) (h f)   toLinearMap := mkLM A hadd hsmul hsmooth hbound

explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.le_top: In any ordered type that contains a maximum element, every element is less than or equal to that maximum element.
explanatories.norm_nonneg: This theorem asserts that the norm of any element in a seminormed group is non-negative.
explanatories.mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left: This theorem asserts that multiplying a non-negative element by two other elements, where one is less than or equal to the other, preserves the order relation in a given type.
explanatories.le_trans: This theorem asserts that in a preorder, if one element is less than or equal to a second, and the second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.
explanatories.contDiff_const: The theorem states that a constant function is continuously differentiable to any order in the context of non-trivially normed fields and normed spaces.
explanatories.SchwartzMap.le_seminorm: The theorem establishes that a seminorm provides a bound on the product of a given power of the norm of an input and the norm of its n-th iterated derivative for any fixed element in the domain of a Schwartz function.
explanatories.SchwartzMap.schwartzSeminormFamily_apply: The theorem establishes the equality between the family of seminorms defined for Schwartz functions and the specific seminorm associated with those functions based on given parameters.
explanatories.SchwartzMap.mkCLM: A continuous semilinear map is defined between Schwartz spaces, ensuring that it respects addition, scalar multiplication, and smoothness while providing bounds on its behavior in terms of seminorms.
explanatories.ContDiff.clm_apply: If two functions are continuously differentiable up to a certain order, then the application of a continuously differentiable function to the result of another continuously differentiable function is also continuously differentiable up to that same order.
explanatories.norm_iteratedFDeriv_clm_apply_const: The theorem establishes an inequality for the norm of the iterated derivative of a function evaluated at a constant, relating it to the norm of the constant and the norm of the iterated derivative of the function itself.
explanatories.Finset.sup_singleton: This theorem states that the supremum of the image of a singleton set under a given function is equal to the function's value at that element.
explanatories.BoundedContinuousFunction.evalCLM: The evaluation of a bounded continuous function at a specific point is defined as a continuous linear map from the space of bounded continuous functions to the target space.

SchwartzMap.evalCLM.fullDefinition: protected def evalCLM (m : E) : 𝓢(E, E →L[ℝ] F) →L[𝕜] 𝓢(E, F) :=   mkCLM (fun f x => f x m) (fun _ _ _ => rfl) (fun _ _ _ => rfl)     (fun f => ContDiff.clm_apply f.2 contDiff_const)     (by       rintro ⟨k, n⟩       use {(k, n)}, ‖m‖, norm_nonneg _       intro f x       refine         le_trans           (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (norm_iteratedFDeriv_clm_apply_const f.2 le_top)             (by positivity))           ?_       move_mul [‖m‖]       gcongr ?_ * ‖m‖       simp only [Finset.sup_singleton, schwartzSeminormFamily_apply, le_seminorm])

explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.SchwartzMap.smooth': Every Schwartz function is infinitely differentiable, meaning it is smooth at all orders when regarded as a function from one normed space to another.
explanatories.le_top: In any ordered type that contains a maximum element, every element is less than or equal to that maximum element.
explanatories.one_mul: This theorem asserts that multiplying any element by the identity element in a multiplicative structure results in the element itself.
explanatories.mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left: This theorem asserts that multiplying a non-negative element by two other elements, where one is less than or equal to the other, preserves the order relation in a given type.
explanatories.mul_assoc: This theorem asserts that multiplication in a semigroup is associative, meaning the product of three elements is the same regardless of how they are grouped.
explanatories.le_trans: This theorem asserts that in a preorder, if one element is less than or equal to a second, and the second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.
explanatories.SchwartzMap.smul_apply: The evaluation of a scalar multiplied by a Schwartz function is the same as multiplying the scalar with the value of the function at that point.
explanatories.Pi.smul_apply: This input does not contain any theorem or definition to summarize.
explanatories.SchwartzMap.add_apply: The sum of two Schwartz functions evaluated at a point equals the sum of their evaluations at that point.
explanatories.Prod.snd: This defines a function that retrieves the second element from a given pair of values.
explanatories.Finset.Iic: This definition creates a finite set of elements that are less than or equal to a specified element within a locally finite ordered structure.
explanatories.Finset.sum_mul: The product of the sum of a function evaluated over a finite set and a constant is equal to the sum of the product of the function evaluated at each element of the set with the same constant.
explanatories.Finset.range: This definition describes a finite set consisting of all natural numbers that are less than a specified non-negative integer.
explanatories.Nat.choose: The definition specifies a function that calculates the number of subsets containing a certain number of elements from a set with a specified total number of elements, commonly referred to as binomial coefficients.
explanatories.Finset.mem_range_succ_iff: This theorem establishes that an integer is a member of the set of natural numbers up to the next integer if and only if it is less than or equal to that next integer.
explanatories.le_rfl: This theorem states that every element in a preorder is less than or equal to itself.
explanatories.SchwartzMap.one_add_le_sup_seminorm_appl: The theorem shows that a certain bound involving the seminorm and iterated derivatives of a Schwartz function at a point can be expressed in terms of a supremum over a finite set of seminorms, adjusted by a factor related to the norm of the point.
explanatories.Function.HasTemperateGrowth.norm_iterate: If a function has temperate growth, then its iterated derivatives can be uniformly bounded by a polynomial in the norm of the input, scaled by a constant.
explanatories.Exists.choose: An existential statement guarantees the existence of an element satisfying a property, allowing for the extraction of such an element from the statement.
explanatories.SchwartzMap.mkCLM: A continuous semilinear map is defined between Schwartz spaces, ensuring that it respects addition, scalar multiplication, and smoothness while providing bounds on its behavior in terms of seminorms.
explanatories.map_add: There is no theorem or definition provided to summarize.
explanatories.add_left_inj: The equality of sums with a fixed element on the right side implies the equality of the other two elements in a right-cancelable additive structure.
explanatories.Pi.add_apply: This theorem examines the behavior of function composition involving a constant function that returns the "one" value.
explanatories.eq_self_iff_true: The assertion that an element is equal to itself is logically equivalent to stating that a truth exists.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.add_apply: The sum of two continuous linear maps applied to an input is equal to the sum of each map applied to that input.
explanatories.map_smul: This theorem states that a morphism that is equivariant with respect to the actions of a monoid preserves the action when applied to the product of an element from the monoid and an element from the type.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.coe_smul': The scalar multiplication of a continuous linear map preserves the action of the scalar when evaluated at the map.
explanatories.RingHom.id_apply: This theorem states that the identity ring homomorphism returns any element from the semiring unchanged.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.isBoundedBilinearMap: This theorem confirms that a continuous bilinear map is also a bounded bilinear map.
explanatories.IsBoundedBilinearMap.contDiff: The theorem states that any bounded bilinear map is continuously differentiable up to any order in the context of non-trivially normed fields and normed spaces.
explanatories.ContDiff.restrict_scalars: The theorem states that if a function is continuously differentiable with respect to one field, then it is also continuously differentiable with respect to a subfield at the same order.
explanatories.ContDiff.comp: The theorem states that the composition of two continuously differentiable functions, each differentiable up to a specified order, is also continuously differentiable to the same order.
explanatories.ContDiff.prod: The theorem states that the Cartesian product of two continuously differentiable functions of a specified order is also continuously differentiable of the same order.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.norm_iteratedFDeriv_: The theorem establishes an upper bound on the norm of the iterated derivative of a bilinear map applied to two continuously differentiable functions at a point, related to the norms of their respective iterated derivatives.
explanatories.Finset.mul_sum: The product of a constant and the sum of a function evaluated over a finite set is equal to the sum of the products of that constant with the function evaluated at each element of the set.
explanatories.Finset.sum_le_sum: This theorem asserts that in an ordered additive commutative monoid, if each element of one finite sum is less than or equal to the corresponding element of another, then the total sum of the first set of elements is less than or equal to the total sum of the second set.
explanatories.Nat.choose_le_middle: The theorem asserts that the number of ways to choose a specified number of elements from a set does not exceed the maximum possible number of ways when the number of elements chosen is half the size of the set.
explanatories.tsub_le_self: This theorem states that the result of subtracting one element from another is always less than or equal to the original element being subtracted from.
explanatories.pow_add: This theorem asserts that in a monoidal structure, raising an element to the sum of two exponents equals the product of the element raised to each exponent individually.
explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function, where the output of the second function becomes the input of the first.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.comp: The composition of bounded linear maps results in another bounded linear map.

SchwartzMap.bilinLeftCLM.fullDefinition: def bilinLeftCLM (B : E →L[ℝ] F →L[ℝ] G) {g : D → F} (hg : g.HasTemperateGrowth) :     𝓢(D, E) →L[ℝ] 𝓢(D, G) :=   -- Todo (after port): generalize to `B : E →L[𝕜] F →L[𝕜] G` and `𝕜`-linear     mkCLM     (fun f x => B (f x) (g x))     (fun _ _ _ => by       simp only [map_add, add_left_inj, Pi.add_apply, eq_self_iff_true,         ContinuousLinearMap.add_apply])     (fun _ _ _ => by       simp only [smul_apply, map_smul, ContinuousLinearMap.coe_smul', Pi.smul_apply,         RingHom.id_apply])     (fun f => (B.isBoundedBilinearMap.contDiff.restrict_scalars ℝ).comp (f.smooth'.prod hg.1))     (by       rintro ⟨k, n⟩       rcases hg.norm_iteratedFDeriv_le_uniform_aux n with ⟨l, C, hC, hgrowth⟩       use         Finset.Iic (l + k, n), ‖B‖ * ((n : ℝ) + (1 : ℝ)) * n.choose (n / 2) * (C * 2 ^ (l + k)),         by positivity       intro f x       have hxk : 0 ≤ ‖x‖ ^ k := by positivity       have hnorm_mul :=         ContinuousLinearMap.norm_iteratedFDeriv_le_of_bilinear B f.smooth' hg.1 x (n := n) le_top       refine le_trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hnorm_mul hxk) ?_       move_mul [← ‖B‖]       simp_rw [mul_assoc ‖B‖]       gcongr _ * ?_       rw [Finset.mul_sum]       have : (∑ _x ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), (1 : ℝ)) = n + 1 := by simp       simp_rw [mul_assoc ((n : ℝ) + 1)]       rw [← this, Finset.sum_mul]       refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun i hi => ?_       simp only [one_mul]       move_mul [(Nat.choose n i : ℝ), (Nat.choose n (n / 2) : ℝ)]       gcongr ?_ * ?_       swap       · norm_cast         exact i.choose_le_middle n       specialize hgrowth (n - i) (by simp only [tsub_le_self]) x       refine le_trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hgrowth (by positivity)) ?_       move_mul [C]       gcongr ?_ * C       rw [Finset.mem_range_succ_iff] at hi       change i ≤ (l + k, n).snd at hi       refine le_trans ?_ (one_add_le_sup_seminorm_apply le_rfl hi f x)       rw [pow_add]       move_mul [(1 + ‖x‖) ^ l]       gcongr       simp)
SchwartzMap.bilinLeftCLM.description: A continuous linear map is established from Schwartz functions to another set of Schwartz functions by taking a bilinear map applied to the values of the original function and another function that exhibits temperate growth.

explanatories.Nat.choose_le_middle: The theorem asserts that the number of ways to choose a specified number of elements from a set does not exceed the maximum possible number of ways when the number of elements chosen is half the size of the set.
explanatories.tsub_le_self: This theorem states that the result of subtracting one element from another is always less than or equal to the original element being subtracted from.
explanatories.pow_add: This theorem asserts that in a monoidal structure, raising an element to the sum of two exponents equals the product of the element raised to each exponent individually.
explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function, where the output of the second function becomes the input of the first.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.comp: The composition of bounded linear maps results in another bounded linear map.

schwartz_map.bilin_left_clm.fullDefinition: def bilinLeftCLM (B : E →L[ℝ] F →L[ℝ] G) {g : D → F} (hg : g.HasTemperateGrowth) :     𝓢(D, E) →L[ℝ] 𝓢(D, G) :=   -- Todo (after port): generalize to `B : E →L[𝕜] F →L[𝕜] G` and `𝕜`-linear     mkCLM     (fun f x => B (f x) (g x))     (fun _ _ _ => by       simp only [map_add, add_left_inj, Pi.add_apply, eq_self_iff_true,         ContinuousLinearMap.add_apply])     (fun _ _ _ => by       simp only [smul_apply, map_smul, ContinuousLinearMap.coe_smul', Pi.smul_apply,         RingHom.id_apply])     (fun f => (B.isBoundedBilinearMap.contDiff.restrict_scalars ℝ).comp (f.smooth'.prod hg.1))     (by       rintro ⟨k, n⟩       rcases hg.norm_iteratedFDeriv_le_uniform_aux n with ⟨l, C, hC, hgrowth⟩       use         Finset.Iic (l + k, n), ‖B‖ * ((n : ℝ) + (1 : ℝ)) * n.choose (n / 2) * (C * 2 ^ (l + k)),         by positivity       intro f x       have hxk : 0 ≤ ‖x‖ ^ k := by positivity       have hnorm_mul :=         ContinuousLinearMap.norm_iteratedFDeriv_le_of_bilinear B f.smooth' hg.1 x (n := n) le_top       refine le_trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hnorm_mul hxk) ?_       move_mul [← ‖B‖]       simp_rw [mul_assoc ‖B‖]       gcongr _ * ?_       rw [Finset.mul_sum]       have : (∑ _x ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), (1 : ℝ)) = n + 1 := by simp       simp_rw [mul_assoc ((n : ℝ) + 1)]       rw [← this, Finset.sum_mul]       refine Finset.sum_le_sum fun i hi => ?_       simp only [one_mul]       move_mul [(Nat.choose n i : ℝ), (Nat.choose n (n / 2) : ℝ)]       gcongr ?_ * ?_       swap       · norm_cast         exact i.choose_le_middle n       specialize hgrowth (n - i) (by simp only [tsub_le_self]) x       refine le_trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hgrowth (by positivity)) ?_       move_mul [C]       gcongr ?_ * C       rw [Finset.mem_range_succ_iff] at hi       change i ≤ (l + k, n).snd at hi       refine le_trans ?_ (one_add_le_sup_seminorm_apply le_rfl hi f x)       rw [pow_add]       move_mul [(1 + ‖x‖) ^ l]       gcongr       simp)
schwartz_map.bilin_left_clm.description: A continuous linear map is established from Schwartz functions to another set of Schwartz functions by taking a bilinear map applied to the values of the original function and another function that exhibits temperate growth.

SchwartzMap.compCLM.code:
SchwartzMap.compCLM.{u_1, u_3, u_4, u_5} (𝕜 : Type u_1) {D : Type u_3} {E : Type u_4} {F : Type u_5}
  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] [RCLike 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup D]
  [NormedSpace ℝ D] [NormedSpace 𝕜 F] [SMulCommClass ℝ 𝕜 F] {g : D → E} (hg : Function.HasTemperateGrowth g)
  (hg_upper : ∃ k C, ∀ (x : D), ‖x‖ ≤ C * (1 + ‖g x‖) ^ k) : 𝓢(E, F) →L[𝕜] 𝓢(D, F)
SchwartzMap.compCLM.comment:
Composition with a function on the right is a continuous linear map on Schwartz space
provided that the function is temperate and growths polynomially near infinity.

explanatories.Exists.intro: If there is an element that satisfies a property, then it can be used to demonstrate the existence of at least one such element with that property.
explanatories.And.intro: This states that if two propositions are true, then their conjunction is also true.
explanatories.LE.le.trans: A theorem establishing that in a preordered structure, if one element is less than or equal to a second and that second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.
explanatories.SchwartzMap.smooth': Every Schwartz function is infinitely differentiable, meaning it is smooth at all orders when regarded as a function from one normed space to another.
explanatories.le_top: In any ordered type that contains a maximum element, every element is less than or equal to that maximum element.
explanatories.norm_nonneg: This theorem asserts that the norm of any element in a seminormed group is non-negative.
explanatories.le_div_iff': This theorem provides a criterion for relating the inequality of two elements and their division by a positive element in a linear ordered semifield, stating that one element is less than or equal to another divided by a positive element if and only if the product of that positive element with the first element is less than or equal to the second element.
explanatories.Asymptotics.IsBigO.trans: This theorem establishes that if one function is asymptotically bounded by a second function and that second function is asymptotically bounded by a third, then the first function is also asymptotically bounded by the third under the same specified filter.
explanatories.one_mul: This theorem asserts that multiplying any element by the identity element in a multiplicative structure results in the element itself.
explanatories.zero_le_one: Zero is less than or equal to one in any type that accommodates the notions of zero, one, and comparison.
explanatories.mul_assoc: This theorem asserts that multiplication in a semigroup is associative, meaning the product of three elements is the same regardless of how they are grouped.
explanatories.le_trans: This theorem asserts that in a preorder, if one element is less than or equal to a second, and the second is less than or equal to a third, then the first element is also less than or equal to the third.
explanatories.mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right: This theorem states that if one element is less than or equal to another and a non-negative multiplier is applied, the product of the first element and the multiplier will also be less than or equal to the product of the second element and the multiplier.
explanatories.add_le_add: This theorem states that if two pairs of elements each satisfy an order relation, then the sum of the first pair is less than or equal to the sum of the second pair, preserving the order.
explanatories.SchwartzMap.add_apply: The sum of two Schwartz functions evaluated at a point equals the sum of their evaluations at that point.
explanatories.Prod.snd: This defines a function that retrieves the second element from a given pair of values.
explanatories.Finset.Iic: This definition creates a finite set of elements that are less than or equal to a specified element within a locally finite ordered structure.
explanatories.Finset.sup: This definition describes a function that computes the supremum of the images of elements from a finite set under a given function, using a specific order structure that includes a least element.
explanatories.le_rfl: This theorem states that every element in a preorder is less than or equal to itself.
explanatories.SchwartzMap.one_add_le_sup_seminorm_appl: The theorem shows that a certain bound involving the seminorm and iterated derivatives of a Schwartz function at a point can be expressed in terms of a supremum over a finite set of seminorms, adjusted by a factor related to the norm of the point.
explanatories.mul_le_mul: This theorem establishes that if one element is less than or equal to another, and a second element is also less than or equal to a positive element, then the product of the first element with the second is less than or equal to the product of the larger element with the same second element.
explanatories.Function.HasTemperateGrowth.norm_iterate: If a function has temperate growth, then its iterated derivatives can be uniformly bounded by a polynomial in the norm of the input, scaled by a constant.
explanatories.norm_zero: Theorem states that in a seminormed group, the norm of the identity element equals zero.
explanatories.SchwartzMap.mkCLM: A continuous semilinear map is defined between Schwartz spaces, ensuring that it respects addition, scalar multiplication, and smoothness while providing bounds on its behavior in terms of seminorms.
explanatories.add_left_inj: The equality of sums with a fixed element on the right side implies the equality of the other two elements in a right-cancelable additive structure.
explanatories.Pi.add_apply: This theorem examines the behavior of function composition involving a constant function that returns the "one" value.
explanatories.eq_self_iff_true: The assertion that an element is equal to itself is logically equivalent to stating that a truth exists.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.add_apply: The sum of two continuous linear maps applied to an input is equal to the sum of each map applied to that input.
explanatories.ContDiff.comp: The theorem states that the composition of two continuously differentiable functions, each differentiable up to a specified order, is also continuously differentiable to the same order.
explanatories.pow_add: This theorem asserts that in a monoidal structure, raising an element to the sum of two exponents equals the product of the element raised to each exponent individually.
explanatories.le_add_of_nonneg_right: This theorem states that if one element is non-negative, then any element is less than or equal to the sum of itself and that non-negative element.
explanatories.nonneg_of_mul_nonneg_left: If the product of two numbers is nonnegative and one of the numbers is positive, then the other number must also be nonnegative.
explanatories.pow_mul: This theorem states that for any element in a monoid, raising it to the product of two natural numbers is equivalent to first raising it to one of those numbers and then raising the result to the other number.
explanatories.mul_pow: In a commutative monoid, the power of a product of two elements equals the product of their individual powers.
explanatories.add_mul: This theorem defines the right distributive property of multiplication over addition in a specific algebraic structure.
explanatories.one_le_pow_of_one_le: In an ordered semiring, if an element is greater than or equal to one, then raising it to any non-negative power results in a value that is also greater than or equal to one.
explanatories.le_add_iff_nonneg_right: This theorem states that a quantity is less than or equal to the sum of itself and another quantity if and only if the other quantity is non-negative.
explanatories.lt_of_lt_of_le: This theorem shows that if one element is less than a second element, and the second element is less than or equal to a third element, then the first element is also less than the third element in a preorder.
explanatories.zero_lt_one: Zero is strictly less than one in any type that includes definitions for zero, one, and a partial order, provided that one is not equal to zero.
explanatories.LT.lt.ne': A theorem stating that in a preordered structure, if one element is strictly less than another, then the two elements cannot be equal.
explanatories.le_self_pow: A number greater than or equal to one is less than or equal to its non-zero power in an ordered semiring.
explanatories.norm_iteratedFDeriv_comp_le: The theorem establishes that if the derivatives of one function are bounded at the image of another function, along with bounds on the derivatives of that second function, then the n-th derivative of their composition is also bounded by a specified expression involving factorial and powers of the bounds.
explanatories.pow_le_pow_left: In an ordered semiring, if a non-negative number is less than or equal to another number, then raising both numbers to the same power results in the first raised number being less than or equal to the second.
explanatories.le_add_iff_nonneg_left: This theorem indicates that a given element is less than or equal to the sum of itself and another element if and only if that other element is non-negative.
explanatories.div_le_iff: This theorem establishes a condition that relates the division of one element by a positive element to the inequality involving the product of that positive element and another element, indicating that the first quotient is less than or equal to a third element if and only if the first element is less than or equal to the product of that third element and the positive element.
explanatories.NonnegHomClass.apply_nonneg: This theorem asserts that the image of any element is always non-negative.
explanatories.Function.comp: Function composition combines two functions into a new function, where the output of the second function becomes the input of the first.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.comp: The composition of bounded linear maps results in another bounded linear map.

SchwartzMap.compCLM.fullDefinition: def compCLM {g : D → E} (hg : g.HasTemperateGrowth)     (hg_upper : ∃ (k : ℕ) (C : ℝ), ∀ x, ‖x‖ ≤ C * (1 + ‖g x‖) ^ k) : 𝓢(E, F) →L[𝕜] 𝓢(D, F) :=   mkCLM (fun f x => f (g x))     (fun _ _ _ => by simp only [add_left_inj, Pi.add_apply, eq_self_iff_true]) (fun _ _ _ => rfl)     (fun f => f.smooth'.comp hg.1)     (by       rintro ⟨k, n⟩       rcases hg.norm_iteratedFDeriv_le_uniform_aux n with ⟨l, C, hC, hgrowth⟩       rcases hg_upper with ⟨kg, Cg, hg_upper'⟩       have hCg : 1 ≤ 1 + Cg := by         refine le_add_of_nonneg_right ?_         specialize hg_upper' 0         rw [norm_zero] at hg_upper'         exact nonneg_of_mul_nonneg_left hg_upper' (by positivity)       let k' := kg * (k + l * n)       use Finset.Iic (k', n), (1 + Cg) ^ (k + l * n) * ((C + 1) ^ n * n ! * 2 ^ k'), by positivity       intro f x       let seminorm_f := ((Finset.Iic (k', n)).sup (schwartzSeminormFamily 𝕜 _ _)) f       have hg_upper'' : (1 + ‖x‖) ^ (k + l * n) ≤ (1 + Cg) ^ (k + l * n) * (1 + ‖g x‖) ^ k' := by         rw [pow_mul, ← mul_pow]         gcongr         rw [add_mul]         refine add_le_add ?_ (hg_upper' x)         nth_rw 1 [← one_mul (1 : ℝ)]         gcongr         apply one_le_pow_of_one_le         simp only [le_add_iff_nonneg_right, norm_nonneg]       have hbound :         ∀ i, i ≤ n → ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ i f (g x)‖ ≤ 2 ^ k' * seminorm_f / (1 + ‖g x‖) ^ k' := by         intro i hi         have hpos : 0 < (1 + ‖g x‖) ^ k' := by positivity         rw [le_div_iff' hpos]         change i ≤ (k', n).snd at hi         exact one_add_le_sup_seminorm_apply le_rfl hi _ _       have hgrowth' : ∀ N : ℕ, 1 ≤ N → N ≤ n →           ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ N g x‖ ≤ ((C + 1) * (1 + ‖x‖) ^ l) ^ N := by         intro N hN₁ hN₂         refine (hgrowth N hN₂ x).trans ?_         rw [mul_pow]         have hN₁' := (lt_of_lt_of_le zero_lt_one hN₁).ne'         gcongr         · exact le_trans (by simp [hC]) (le_self_pow (by simp [hC]) hN₁')         · refine le_self_pow (one_le_pow_of_one_le ?_ l) hN₁'           simp only [le_add_iff_nonneg_right, norm_nonneg]       have := norm_iteratedFDeriv_comp_le f.smooth' hg.1 le_top x hbound hgrowth'       have hxk : ‖x‖ ^ k ≤ (1 + ‖x‖) ^ k :=         pow_le_pow_left (norm_nonneg _) (by simp only [zero_le_one, le_add_iff_nonneg_left]) _       refine le_trans (mul_le_mul hxk this (by positivity) (by positivity)) ?_       have rearrange :         (1 + ‖x‖) ^ k *             (n ! * (2 ^ k' * seminorm_f / (1 + ‖g x‖) ^ k') * ((C + 1) * (1 + ‖x‖) ^ l) ^ n) =           (1 + ‖x‖) ^ (k + l * n) / (1 + ‖g x‖) ^ k' *             ((C + 1) ^ n * n ! * 2 ^ k' * seminorm_f) := by         rw [mul_pow, pow_add, ← pow_mul]         ring       rw [rearrange]       have hgxk' : 0 < (1 + ‖g x‖) ^ k' := by positivity       rw [← div_le_iff hgxk'] at hg_upper''       have hpos : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (C + 1) ^ n * n ! * 2 ^ k' * seminorm_f := by         have : 0 ≤ seminorm_f := apply_nonneg _ _         positivity       refine le_trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hg_upper'' hpos) ?_       rw [← mul_assoc])
SchwartzMap.compCLM.description: The operation of composing a temperate function with a Schwartz function results in a continuous linear map from the Schwartz space of one normed space to that of another.

* 2 ^ k'), by positivity       intro f x       let seminorm_f := ((Finset.Iic (k', n)).sup (schwartzSeminormFamily 𝕜 _ _)) f       have hg_upper'' : (1 + ‖x‖) ^ (k + l * n) ≤ (1 + Cg) ^ (k + l * n) * (1 + ‖g x‖) ^ k' := by         rw [pow_mul, ← mul_pow]         gcongr         rw [add_mul]         refine add_le_add ?_ (hg_upper' x)         nth_rw 1 [← one_mul (1 : ℝ)]         gcongr         apply one_le_pow_of_one_le         simp only [le_add_iff_nonneg_right, norm_nonneg]       have hbound :         ∀ i, i ≤ n → ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ i f (g x)‖ ≤ 2 ^ k' * seminorm_f / (1 + ‖g x‖) ^ k' := by         intro i hi         have hpos : 0 < (1 + ‖g x‖) ^ k' := by positivity         rw [le_div_iff' hpos]         change i ≤ (k', n).snd at hi         exact one_add_le_sup_seminorm_apply le_rfl hi _ _       have hgrowth' : ∀ N : ℕ, 1 ≤ N → N ≤ n →           ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ N g x‖ ≤ ((C + 1) * (1 + ‖x‖) ^ l) ^ N := by         intro N hN₁ hN₂         refine (hgrowth N hN₂ x).trans ?_         rw [mul_pow]         have hN₁' := (lt_of_lt_of_le zero_lt_one hN₁).ne'         gcongr         · exact le_trans (by simp [hC]) (le_self_pow (by simp [hC]) hN₁')         · refine le_self_pow (one_le_pow_of_one_le ?_ l) hN₁'           simp only [le_add_iff_nonneg_right, norm_nonneg]       have := norm_iteratedFDeriv_comp_le f.smooth' hg.1 le_top x hbound hgrowth'       have hxk : ‖x‖ ^ k ≤ (1 + ‖x‖) ^ k :=         pow_le_pow_left (norm_nonneg _) (by simp only [zero_le_one, le_add_iff_nonneg_left]) _       refine le_trans (mul_le_mul hxk this (by positivity) (by positivity)) ?_       have rearrange :         (1 + ‖x‖) ^ k *             (n ! * (2 ^ k' * seminorm_f / (1 + ‖g x‖) ^ k') * ((C + 1) * (1 + ‖x‖) ^ l) ^ n) =           (1 + ‖x‖) ^ (k + l * n) / (1 + ‖g x‖) ^ k' *             ((C + 1) ^ n * n ! * 2 ^ k' * seminorm_f) := by         rw [mul_pow, pow_add, ← pow_mul]         ring       rw [rearrange]       have hgxk' : 0 < (1 + ‖g x‖) ^ k' := by positivity       rw [← div_le_iff hgxk'] at hg_upper''       have hpos : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (C + 1) ^ n * n ! * 2 ^ k' * seminorm_f := by         have : 0 ≤ seminorm_f := apply_nonneg _ _         positivity       refine le_trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hg_upper'' hpos) ?_       rw [← mul_assoc])

explanatories.Max.max: A function computes the maximum of two elements from a specified type.
explanatories.le_max_left: This theorem states that in a linear order, any element is less than or equal to the maximum of itself and another element.
explanatories.mul_add: This theorem states that in a structure where multiplication is left distributive over addition, the product of an element and the sum of two other elements equals the sum of the products of the first element with each of the other two elements.
explanatories.add_comm: This theorem asserts that the addition operation in a commutative magma is commutative, meaning the sum of two elements does not depend on the order in which they are added.
explanatories.mul_one: This theorem establishes that multiplying any element in a multiplicative structure by one results in that same element.
explanatories.AntilipschitzWith: A function is classified as an Antilipschitz map if the distance between any two points in the domain is at most a constant multiple of the distance between their images in the codomain.
explanatories.dist_zero_right: This theorem states that in a seminormed group, the distance from any element to one is equal to the norm of that element.
explanatories.dist_eq_norm: This theorem establishes that the distance between two elements in a seminormed additive group is equal to the seminorm of their difference.
explanatories.AntilipschitzWith.le_mul_dist: If a function is Antilipschitz with respect to a constant, then the distance between any two points in the domain is less than or equal to that constant multiplied by the distance between their images in the codomain.
explanatories.norm_sub_le: Theorem shows that the norm of the quotient of two elements in a seminormed group is less than or equal to the sum of the norms of those elements.
explanatories.le_max_right: This theorem asserts that in a linear order, any element is less than or equal to the maximum of itself and another element.
explanatories.pow_one: This theorem states that in a monoid, raising an element to the power of one yields the element itself.
explanatories.add_le_add_iff_left: This theorem states that adding a common element to both sides of an inequality creates an equivalent condition where the relationship between the other addends is preserved.
explanatories.le_mul_of_one_le_right: This theorem demonstrates that if an element is nonnegative and another element is at least one, then the first element is less than or equal to the product of itself and the second element.

SchwartzMap.compCLMOfAntilipschitz.fullDefinition: def compCLMOfAntilipschitz {K : ℝ≥0} {g : D → E}     (hg : g.HasTemperateGrowth) (h'g : AntilipschitzWith K g) :     𝓢(E, F) →L[𝕜] 𝓢(D, F) := by   refine compCLM 𝕜 hg ⟨1, K * max 1 ‖g 0‖, fun x ↦ ?_⟩   calc   ‖x‖ ≤ K * ‖g x - g 0‖ := by     rw [← dist_zero_right, ← dist_eq_norm]     apply h'g.le_mul_dist   _ ≤ K * (‖g x‖ + ‖g 0‖) := by     gcongr     exact norm_sub_le _ _   _ ≤ K * (‖g x‖ + max 1 ‖g 0‖) := by     gcongr     exact le_max_right _ _   _ ≤ (K * max 1 ‖g 0‖ : ℝ) * (1 + ‖g x‖) ^ 1 := by     simp only [mul_add, add_comm (K * ‖g x‖), pow_one, mul_one, add_le_add_iff_left]     gcongr     exact le_mul_of_one_le_right (by positivity) (le_max_left _ _)

explanatories.SchwartzMap.smooth': Every Schwartz function is infinitely differentiable, meaning it is smooth at all orders when regarded as a function from one normed space to another.
explanatories.Differentiable.differentiableAt: If a function is differentiable in a neighborhood, then it is also differentiable at every point within that neighborhood.
explanatories.SchwartzMap.differentiableAt: Every Schwartz function is differentiable at every point in the domain.
explanatories.Iff.mp: If two propositions are equivalent and one of them is true, then the other must also be true.
explanatories.one_mul: This theorem asserts that multiplying any element by the identity element in a multiplicative structure results in the element itself.
explanatories.zero_le_one: Zero is less than or equal to one in any type that accommodates the notions of zero, one, and comparison.
explanatories.SchwartzMap.le_seminorm: The theorem establishes that a seminorm provides a bound on the product of a given power of the norm of an input and the norm of its n-th iterated derivative for any fixed element in the domain of a Schwartz function.
explanatories.SchwartzMap.schwartzSeminormFamily_apply: The theorem establishes the equality between the family of seminorms defined for Schwartz functions and the specific seminorm associated with those functions based on given parameters.
explanatories.contDiff_top_iff_fderiv: A function is infinitely differentiable if and only if it is differentiable and its derivative is also infinitely differentiable.
explanatories.ContinuousLinearMap.fderiv: The derivative of a continuous linear map at a point is equal to the linear map itself.
explanatories.SchwartzMap.mkCLM: A continuous semilinear map is defined between Schwartz spaces, ensuring that it respects addition, scalar multiplication, and smoothness while providing bounds on its behavior in terms of seminorms.
explanatories.Finset.sup_singleton: This theorem states that the supremum of the image of a singleton set under a given function is equal to the function's value at that element.
explanatories.fderiv_add: If two functions are differentiable at a point, then their sum is also differentiable at that point, and the derivative of the sum equals the sum of the derivatives of the individual functions.
explanatories.fderiv_const_smul: If a function is differentiable at a point, then multiplying that function by a constant results in a derivative at that point which is also scaled by that constant.
explanatories.Seminorm.comp_apply: The seminorm of the composition of a linear map and a seminorm is equal to the seminorm evaluated at the image of the input vector under that linear map.
explanatories.one_smul: This theorem establishes that multiplying any element by the identity element of a monoid does not change the element itself.
explanatories.norm_iteratedFDeriv_fderiv: The theorem states that the norm of the n-th iterated derivative of the derivative of a function at a point is equal to the norm of the (n+1)-th iterated derivative of the original function at that point.

SchwartzMap.fderivCLM.fullDefinition: def fderivCLM : 𝓢(E, F) →L[𝕜] 𝓢(E, E →L[ℝ] F) :=   mkCLM (fderiv ℝ) (fun f g _ => fderiv_add f.differentiableAt g.differentiableAt)     (fun a f _ => fderiv_const_smul f.differentiableAt a)     (fun f => (contDiff_top_iff_fderiv.mp f.smooth').2) fun ⟨k, n⟩ =>     ⟨{⟨k, n + 1⟩}, 1, zero_le_one, fun f x => by       simpa only [schwartzSeminormFamily_apply, Seminorm.comp_apply, Finset.sup_singleton,         one_smul, norm_iteratedFDeriv_fderiv, one_mul] using f.le_seminorm 𝕜 k (n + 1) x⟩

explanatories.deriv_add: This theorem states that if two functions are differentiable at a specific point, then the derivative of their sum at that point is equal to the sum of their individual derivatives at that point.
explanatories.deriv_const_smul: This theorem states that if a function is differentiable at a point, then the derivative of that function scaled by a constant at that point equals the product of that constant and the derivative of the original function at the same point.
explanatories.contDiff_top_iff_deriv: The theorem establishes that a function is infinitely continuously differentiable if and only if it is differentiable and its derivative is also infinitely continuously differentiable.
explanatories.iteratedDeriv_succ': The (n+1)-th iterated derivative of a function can be obtained by applying the iterated derivative to its derivative n times.

schwartz_map.deriv_clm.fullDefinition: def derivCLM : 𝓢(ℝ, F) →L[𝕜] 𝓢(ℝ, F) :=   mkCLM (fun f => deriv f) (fun f g _ => deriv_add f.differentiableAt g.differentiableAt)     (fun a f _ => deriv_const_smul a f.differentiableAt)     (fun f => (contDiff_top_iff_deriv.mp f.smooth').2) fun ⟨k, n⟩ =>     ⟨{⟨k, n + 1⟩}, 1, zero_le_one, fun f x => by       simpa only [Real.norm_eq_abs, Finset.sup_singleton, schwartzSeminormFamily_apply, one_mul,         norm_iteratedFDeriv_eq_norm_iteratedDeriv, ← iteratedDeriv_succ'] using         f.le_seminorm' 𝕜 k (n + 1) x⟩

SchwartzMap.integrable_of_le_of_pow_mul_.code:
SchwartzMap.integrable_of_le_of_pow_mul_le.{u_3, u_4} {D : Type u_3} {E : Type u_4} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [NormedAddCommGroup D] [MeasurableSpace D] [BorelSpace D] [SecondCountableTopology D] {μ : Measure D}
  [μ.HasTemperateGrowth] {f : D → E} {C₁ C₂ : ℝ} {k : ℕ} (hf : ∀ (x : D), ‖f x‖ ≤ C₁)
  (h'f : ∀ (x : D), ‖x‖ ^ (k + μ.integrablePower) * ‖f x‖ ≤ C₂) (h''f : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ) :
  Integrable (fun x => ‖x‖ ^ k * ‖f x‖) μ
SchwartzMap.integrable_of_le_of_pow_mul_.comment:
Given a function such that `f` and `x ^ (k + l) * f` are bounded for a suitable `l`, then
`x ^ k * f` is integrable. The bounds are not relevant for the integrability conclusion, but they
are relevant for bounding the integral in `integral_pow_mul_le_of_le_of_pow_mul_le`. We formulate
the two lemmas with the same set of assumptions for ease of applications.

SchwartzMap.integrable_of_le_of_pow_mul_.description: If a function and a certain power of its input multiplied by the function itself satisfy specific boundedness conditions, then the product of the input raised to a power and the function is integrable with respect to a given measure.

SchwartzMap.integralCLM.fullDefinition: def integralCLM : 𝓢(D, V) →L[𝕜] V :=   mkCLMtoNormedSpace (∫ x, · x ∂μ)     (fun f g ↦ by       exact integral_add f.integrable g.integrable)     (integral_smul · ·)     (by       rcases hμ.exists_integrable with ⟨n, h⟩       let m := (n, 0)       use Finset.Iic m, 2 ^ n * ∫ x : D, (1 + ‖x‖) ^ (- (n : ℝ)) ∂μ       refine ⟨by positivity, fun f ↦ (norm_integral_le_integral_norm f).trans ?_⟩       have h' : ∀ x, ‖f x‖ ≤ (1 + ‖x‖) ^ (-(n : ℝ)) *           (2 ^ n * ((Finset.Iic m).sup (fun m' => SchwartzMap.seminorm 𝕜 m'.1 m'.2) f)) := by         intro x         rw [rpow_neg (by positivity), ← div_eq_inv_mul, le_div_iff' (by positivity), rpow_natCast]         simpa using one_add_le_sup_seminorm_apply (m := m) (k := n) (n := 0) le_rfl le_rfl f x       apply (integral_mono (by simpa using f.integrable_pow_mul μ 0) _ h').trans       · rw [integral_mul_right, ← mul_assoc, mul_comm (2 ^ n)]         rfl       apply h.mul_const)

eVariationOn.add_point.code:
eVariationOn.add_point.{u_1, u_2} {α : Type u_1} [LinearOrder α] {E : Type u_2} [PseudoEMetricSpace E] (f : α → E)
  {s : Set α} {x : α} (hx : x ∈ s) (u : ℕ → α) (hu : Monotone u) (us : ∀ (i : ℕ), u i ∈ s) (n : ℕ) :
  ∃ v m,
    Monotone v ∧
      (∀ (i : ℕ), v i ∈ s) ∧
        x ∈ v '' Iio m ∧
          ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, edist (f (u (i + 1))) (f (u i)) ≤ ∑ j ∈ Finset.range m, edist (f (v (j + 1))) (f (v j))
eVariationOn.add_point.comment:
Consider a monotone function `u` parameterizing some points of a set `s`. Given `x ∈ s`, then
one can find another monotone function `v` parameterizing the same points as `u`, with `x` added.
In particular, the variation of a function along `u` is bounded by its variation along `v`.

MeasureTheory.GridLines.T.code:
MeasureTheory.GridLines.T.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} [DecidableEq ι] {A : ι → Type u_2} [(i : ι) → MeasurableSpace (A i)]
  (μ : (i : ι) → Measure (A i)) (p : ℝ) (f : ((i : ι) → A i) → ℝ≥0∞) (s : Finset ι) : ((i : ι) → A i) → ℝ≥0∞
MeasureTheory.GridLines.T.comment:
The "grid-lines operation" (not a standard name) which is central in the inductive proof of the
Sobolev inequality.

For a finite dependent product `Π i : ι, A i` of sigma-finite measure spaces, a finite set `s` of
indices from `ι`, and a (later assumed nonnegative) real number `p`, this operation acts on a
function `f` from `Π i, A i` into the extended nonnegative reals.  The operation is to partially
integrate, in the `s` co-ordinates, the function whose value at `x : Π i, A i` is obtained by
multiplying a certain power of `f` with the product, for each co-ordinate `i` in `s`, of a certain
power of the integral of `f` along the "grid line" in the `i` direction through `x`.

We are most interested in this operation when the set `s` is the universe in `ι`, but as a proxy for
"induction on dimension" we define it for a general set `s` of co-ordinates: the `s`-grid-lines
operation on a function `f` which is constant along the co-ordinates in `sᶜ` is morally (that is, up
to type-theoretic nonsense) the same thing as the universe-grid-lines operation on the associated
function on the "lower-dimensional" space `Π i : s, A i`.

explanatories.Fintype.card: This definition establishes that for a type that has a finite enumeration, the cardinality or number of elements in that type is a natural number.
explanatories.Finset.card: This definition indicates that the cardinality of a finite set represents the total number of its elements.

MeasureTheory.GridLines.T.description: This defines an operation that performs partial integration on functions over a finite product of measurable spaces, focusing on specified coordinate directions for constructing terms relevant to the Sobolev inequality.

MeasureTheory.GridLines.T_insert_le_T_lm.code:
MeasureTheory.GridLines.T_insert_le_T_lmarginal_singleton.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} [DecidableEq ι] {A : ι → Type u_2}
  [(i : ι) → MeasurableSpace (A i)] (μ : (i : ι) → Measure (A i)) [∀ (i : ι), SigmaFinite (μ i)] {p : ℝ} (hp₀ : 0 ≤ p)
  (s : Finset ι) (hp : ↑s.card * p ≤ 1) (i : ι) (hi : i ∉ s) {f : ((i : ι) → A i) → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : Measurable f) :
  T μ p f (insert i s) ≤ T μ p (∫⋯∫⁻_{i}, f ∂μ) s
MeasureTheory.GridLines.T_insert_le_T_lm.comment:
The main inductive step in the grid-lines lemma for the Gagliardo-Nirenberg-Sobolev inequality.

The grid-lines operation `GridLines.T` on a nonnegative function on a finitary product type is
less than or equal to the grid-lines operation of its partial integral in one co-ordinate
(the latter intuitively considered as a function on a space "one dimension down").

explanatories.Finset.card: This definition indicates that the cardinality of a finite set represents the total number of its elements.
explanatories.Measurable: This definition describes a function between measurable spaces as measurable if it preserves the measurability of sets by ensuring that the preimage of any measurable set is also measurable.

MeasureTheory.GridLines.T_insert_le_T_lm.description: This theorem establishes that the grid-lines operation on a nonnegative function over an augmented finite set is less than or equal to the same operation applied to the partial integral of that function along one coordinate, thereby facilitating the inductive argument for a related inequality.

MeasureTheory.GridLines.T_lmarginal_anti.code:
MeasureTheory.GridLines.T_lmarginal_antitone.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {A : ι → Type u_2}
  [(i : ι) → MeasurableSpace (A i)] (μ : (i : ι) → Measure (A i)) [∀ (i : ι), SigmaFinite (μ i)] {p : ℝ} (hp₀ : 0 ≤ p)
  (hp : (↑#ι - 1) * p ≤ 1) {f : ((i : ι) → A i) → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : Measurable f) :
  Antitone fun s => GridLines.T μ p (∫⋯∫⁻_sᶜ, f ∂μ) s
MeasureTheory.GridLines.T_lmarginal_anti.comment:
Auxiliary result for the grid-lines lemma.  Given a nonnegative function on a finitary product
type indexed by `ι`, and a set `s` in `ι`, consider partially integrating over the variables in
`sᶜ` and performing the "grid-lines operation" (see `GridLines.T`) to the resulting function in the
variables `s`.  This theorem states that this operation decreases as the number of grid-lines taken
increases.

explanatories.Measurable: This definition describes a function between measurable spaces as measurable if it preserves the measurability of sets by ensuring that the preimage of any measurable set is also measurable.
explanatories.Antitone: A function is considered antitone if it reverses the order, meaning that if one input is less than or equal to another, then the output of the larger input will not exceed the output of the smaller input.

MeasureTheory.GridLines.T_lmarginal_anti.description: This theorem asserts that the grid-lines operation applied to the partial integral of a nonnegative function decreases as the number of grid-lines considered increases, indicating an antitonic relationship.

MeasureTheory.lintegral_mul_prod_lintegr.code:
MeasureTheory.lintegral_mul_prod_lintegral_pow_le.{u_1, u_2} {ι : Type u_1} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
  {A : ι → Type u_2} [(i : ι) → MeasurableSpace (A i)] (μ : (i : ι) → Measure (A i)) [∀ (i : ι), SigmaFinite (μ i)]
  {p : ℝ} (hp₀ : 0 ≤ p) (hp : (↑#ι - 1) * p ≤ 1) {f : ((i : ι) → A i) → ℝ≥0∞} (hf : Measurable f) :
  ∫⁻ (x : (i : ι) → A i),
      f x ^ (1 - (↑#ι - 1) * p) * ∏ i : ι, (∫⁻ (xᵢ : A i), f (update x i xᵢ) ∂μ i) ^ p ∂Measure.pi μ ≤
    (∫⁻ (x : (i : ι) → A i), f x ∂Measure.pi μ) ^ (1 + p)
MeasureTheory.lintegral_mul_prod_lintegr.comment:
The "grid-lines lemma" (not a standard name), stated with a general parameter `p` as the
exponent.  Compare with `lintegral_prod_lintegral_pow_le`.

For any finite dependent product `Π i : ι, A i` of sigma-finite measure spaces, for any
nonnegative real number `p` such that `(#ι - 1) * p ≤ 1`, for any function `f` from `Π i, A i` into
the extended nonnegative reals, we consider an associated "grid-lines quantity", the integral of an
associated function from `Π i, A i` into the extended nonnegative reals.  The value of this function
at `x : Π i, A i` is obtained by multiplying a certain power of `f` with the product, for each
co-ordinate `i`, of a certain power of the integral of `f` along the "grid line" in the `i`
direction through `x`.

This lemma bounds the Lebesgue integral of the grid-lines quantity by a power of the Lebesgue
integral of `f`.

explanatories.Measurable: This definition describes a function between measurable spaces as measurable if it preserves the measurability of sets by ensuring that the preimage of any measurable set is also measurable.

MeasureTheory.lintegral_mul_prod_lintegr.description: This theorem provides a bound on the Lebesgue integral of a modified function involving grid-lines quantities in terms of a power of the Lebesgue integral of the original function over a finite product of sigma-finite measure spaces.

MeasureTheory.lintegral_prod_lintegral_p.comment:
Special case of the grid-lines lemma `lintegral_mul_prod_lintegral_pow_le`, taking the extremal

MeasureTheory.lintegral_prod_lintegral_p.description: This theorem states that for a nonnegative measurable function, the integral of the product of its conditional integrals over a finite index set is less than or equal to the integral of the function raised to a specific exponent related to the dimension of the index set, establishing a form of inequality in measure theory.

MeasureTheory.lintegralPowLePowLIntegral.code:
MeasureTheory.lintegralPowLePowLIntegralFDerivConst.{u_5} {E : Type u_5} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
  [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] (μ : Measure E) [μ.IsAddHaarMeasure] (p : ℝ) : ℝ≥0
MeasureTheory.lintegralPowLePowLIntegral.comment:
The constant factor occurring in the conclusion of `lintegral_pow_le_pow_lintegral_fderiv`.
It only depends on `E`, `μ` and `p`.

MeasureTheory.lintegralPowLePowLIntegral.fullDefinition: irreducible_def lintegralPowLePowLIntegralFDerivConst (p : ℝ) : ℝ≥0 := by   let ι := Fin (finrank ℝ E)   have : finrank ℝ E = finrank ℝ (ι → ℝ) := by     rw [finrank_fintype_fun_eq_card, Fintype.card_fin (finrank ℝ E)]   let e : E ≃L[ℝ] ι → ℝ := ContinuousLinearEquiv.ofFinrankEq this   let c := addHaarScalarFactor μ ((volume : Measure (ι → ℝ)).map e.symm)   exact (c * ‖(e.symm : (ι → ℝ) →L[ℝ] E)‖₊ ^ p) * (c ^ p)⁻¹

MeasureTheory.lintegral_pow_le_pow_linte.comment:
The **Gagliardo-Nirenberg-Sobolev inequality**.  Let `u` be a continuously differentiable
compactly-supported function `u` on `ℝⁿ`, for `n ≥ 2`.  (More literally we encode `ℝⁿ` as

HasConstantSpeedOnWith.fullDefinition: def HasConstantSpeedOnWith :=   ∀ ⦃x⦄ (_ : x ∈ s) ⦃y⦄ (_ : y ∈ s), eVariationOn f (s ∩ Icc x y) = ENNReal.ofReal (l * (y - x))
HasConstantSpeedOnWith.description: The definition specifies that a function has constant speed on a set if the change in its values over any interval within that set is proportional to the length of the interval.
