mellin.code: mellin.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E] (f : ℝ → E) (s : ℂ) : E
mellin.comment:
The Mellin transform of a function `f` (for a complex exponent `s`), defined as the integral of
`t ^ (s - 1) • f` over `Ioi 0`.

explanatories.Set.Ioi: This definition denotes the set of elements that are strictly greater than a specified element in a preorder structure, resulting in a left-open and right-infinite interval.

mellin.fullDefinition: def mellin (f : ℝ → E) (s : ℂ) : E :=   ∫ t : ℝ in Ioi 0, (t : ℂ) ^ (s - 1) • f t
mellin.description: The Mellin transform of a function represents the integral of the product of that function and a power of its argument adjusted by a complex exponent.

mellin_cpow_smul.code:
mellin_cpow_smul.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E] (f : ℝ → E) (s a : ℂ) :
  mellin (fun t => ↑t ^ a • f t) s = mellin f (s + a)
mellin_cpow_smul.description: The Mellin transform of a function multiplied by a power of its argument results in the same transform as that function evaluated at an increased complex exponent.

mellin_const_smul.description: The Mellin transform of a scaled function is equivalent to the scale multiplied by the Mellin transform of the original function.

mellin_div_const.code: mellin_div_const (f : ℝ → ℂ) (s a : ℂ) : mellin (fun t => f t / a) s = mellin f s / a
mellin_div_const.description: The Mellin transform of a function divided by a constant is equal to the Mellin transform of the original function divided by that same constant.

mellin_comp_rpow.code:
mellin_comp_rpow.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E] (f : ℝ → E) (s : ℂ) (a : ℝ) :
  mellin (fun t => f (t ^ a)) s = |a|⁻¹ • mellin f (s / ↑a)
mellin_comp_rpow.description: The Mellin transform of a function composed with a power transformation is equal to the absolute reciprocal of the exponent multiplied by the Mellin transform of the original function evaluated at a scaled argument.

mellin_comp_mul_left.code:
mellin_comp_mul_left.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E] (f : ℝ → E) (s : ℂ) {a : ℝ}
  (ha : 0 < a) : mellin (fun t => f (a * t)) s = ↑a ^ (-s) • mellin f s
mellin_comp_mul_left.description: The Mellin transform of a function, when multiplied by a positive scalar in its argument, results in a scaled version of the original transform, where the scaling factor is determined by the scalar and the convergence parameter.

mellin_comp_mul_right.code:
mellin_comp_mul_right.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E] (f : ℝ → E) (s : ℂ) {a : ℝ}
  (ha : 0 < a) : mellin (fun t => f (t * a)) s = ↑a ^ (-s) • mellin f s
mellin_comp_mul_right.description: The Mellin transform of a function, when it is scaled by a positive real number, can be expressed as the product of the transformed function and the scaling factor raised to a specific power.

mellin_comp_inv.code:
mellin_comp_inv.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E] (f : ℝ → E) (s : ℂ) :
  mellin (fun t => f t⁻¹) s = mellin f (-s)
mellin_comp_inv.description: The Mellin transform of a function composed with an inverse transformation is equal to the Mellin transform of the original function evaluated at the negation of the original argument.

mellin_eq_fourierIntegral.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E] (f : ℝ → E) {s : ℂ} :
  mellin f s = 𝓕 (fun u => rexp (-s.re * u) • f (rexp (-u))) (s.im / (2 * π))

explanatories.Complex.re: This defines a function that extracts the real component from a complex number.
explanatories.Complex.im: This defines a function that extracts the imaginary component from a complex number.

mellin_eq_fourierIntegral.description: This theorem establishes that the Mellin transform of a function can be expressed as a Fourier integral involving an exponential decay factor and the original function evaluated at an exponential transformation of a variable.

mellinInv_eq_fourierIntegralInv.code:
mellinInv_eq_fourierIntegralInv.{u_1} {E : Type u_1} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E] (σ : ℝ) (f : ℂ → E)
  {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) : mellinInv σ f x = ↑x ^ (-↑σ) • 𝓕⁻ (fun y => f (↑σ + 2 * ↑π * ↑y * I)) (-Real.log x)

explanatories.Real.log: The real logarithm function is defined to extend the conventional logarithm to all real numbers, assigning specific values for positive, negative, and zero inputs while preserving key logarithmic properties.

mellinInv_eq_fourierIntegralInv.description: This theorem demonstrates that the inverse Mellin transform of a function can be represented as a product of a power of the variable with the inverse Fourier transform of the function evaluated at a logarithmic transformation of that variable.
